title: Layouts & workspaces
body:
## Context
E11 gives us one fast chart; E12/E13/E14 give it bars, indicators and drawings. None of that becomes a *terminal* until a trader can arrange several of those surfaces at once, link them, and have the arrangement survive a restart. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 scopes **E15 Layouts & workspaces** as: "Grid layouts (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 charts) with drag-to-resize; symbol/timeframe/crosshair sync groups by colour; named workspace save/load/duplicate/delete; per-workspace theme and density; last-session restore; workspace export/import JSON; server-persisted per user" (34 pts, S08–S09, module **M10**).

Two R1 exit criteria land squarely on this Epic. §5.3 criterion 5: "Chart state (symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout) survives reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss." §5.3 criterion 2: the 30 fps floor must hold "under the worst-case scenario (6-chart layout, all indicators, all drawings)" — which only exists because this Epic lets the trader build that layout in the first place. US-LAY-001's NFR is stricter still: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes on the reference machine.

The contracts are already written and normative. Persistence: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, migration `0011_workspace`). Transport: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`, `/chart-templates`, `/layout-presets`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` — all `x-rbac: {permissions: [workspaces:*], scope: self}`. Surface: **SCR-020** … **SCR-029** (the full workspace/dock band, 10 of 10 allocated), plus **SCR-049**, **SCR-011**, **SCR-150**, **SCR-153**. Engine hooks: `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2 pane synchronisation ("charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, propagated once per frame after input integration, never re-entrantly"), the `sync` event (§6, ≤1/frame), `syncGroup` on `ChartOptions`, requirement **R8** ("4 synchronised chart instances on one page within budget") and benchmark **B6**.

The invariant that governs every ticket here: **a layout mutation must never remount a WebGL context**. SCR-020's performance line states it ("layout changes never remount the WebGL context"), and it is the difference between a 300 ms preset switch and a two-second white flash with a cold data window.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories covering every Must/Should LAY story: **US-LAY-001** (grids), **US-LAY-002** (saved workspaces), **US-LAY-003** (cross-pane sync), **US-LAY-004** (scale linking), **US-LAY-005** (docking/visibility/float), **US-LAY-006** (hotkeys & pane focus), **US-LAY-007** (export/import), **US-LAY-008** (responsive & reduced-capability).
- Screens: **SCR-020** Workspace page, **SCR-021** Dock/panel system, **SCR-022** Layout preset gallery, **SCR-023** Multi-chart sync configuration, **SCR-024** Panel picker, **SCR-025** Workspace settings modal, **SCR-026** Workspace import, **SCR-027** Floating panel window (Electron), **SCR-028** Panel context menu, **SCR-029** Unsaved-changes / layout-conflict dialog, **SCR-049** Multi-chart grid panel, plus the workspace switcher in **SCR-011**, restore on **SCR-150** and the reduced-capability variant of **SCR-153**.
- Components: **CMP-080** DockPanel, **CMP-081** DockGrid/Layout Manager, **CMP-082** PanelHeader, **CMP-083** SplitPane, **CMP-196** MultiChartLinker, **CMP-214** DockDropZone, **CMP-215** FloatingWindowFrame, **CMP-216** PanelMenu, **CMP-217** LayoutPresetMenu, **CMP-218** SyncMenu, **CMP-073** WorkspaceSwitcher, **CMP-213** FuzzyList, **CMP-067** FileDrop, **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-227** EstimatedBadge.
- API: `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`, `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export`, `GET /api/v1/layout-presets`, `GET /api/v1/chart-templates`.
- Tables: `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes` (migration `0011_workspace`); `ix_lp_symbol` is the index E16's recorder queries to decide which symbols count as "chart open".
- Packages: `packages/dock` (framework-light layout tree + drop resolution) and the app-level `SyncBus`; both unit-testable without a DOM canvas.

## Out of scope
- The panels' own content — chart (E11/E12), indicators (E13), drawings (E14), DOM/footprint/tape (E18–E23), order ticket and positions grid (E30, E31). This Epic mounts them through a registry; it does not implement them. Panel kinds whose implementing Epic has not shipped appear in SCR-024 disabled with a reason.
- **Shared / multi-user workspaces and collaboration** — R5.
- Per-workspace *account* binding and the DEMO/LIVE chrome variants beyond rendering whatever badge E10's shell provides — **E27/E44**.
- Chart-template CRUD UI (`chart_templates`) beyond referencing an existing template id from a pane — **E13**.
- Server-pushed cross-device layout conflict events over WS — R1 detects conflicts via `If-Match`/412 only; live conflict push is a later refinement.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A four-pane workspace survives a full restart
  Given a trader has built a 2x2 workspace with distinct symbols, intervals, indicators and drawings and saved it as "EU session"
  When they quit the Electron app and relaunch it
  Then the workspace restores with the same panes, sizes, symbols, intervals, indicators, drawings, sync groups and scroll position
  And it reaches interactive within 3 s from warm cache

Scenario: Layout changes never churn the GL context
  Given a workspace with four chart panes is open
  When a preset is applied, a divider is dragged and a panel is moved by keyboard
  Then no WebGL context is created or lost, the rebuild completes in <= 300 ms, and no pane refetches history it already holds

Scenario: Sync applies only inside its group
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in sync group A and pane 3 is in group B
  When the crosshair moves in pane 1 and the symbol is changed in pane 1 with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  Then pane 2 follows both at the same timestamp within one frame, pane 3 is untouched, and pane 2 keeps its own interval

Scenario: A delisted symbol does not take the workspace down
  Given a saved workspace references a symbol that has since been delisted
  When the workspace is restored
  Then that pane shows an explicit error state naming the symbol, every other pane loads normally, and the workspace remains savable

Scenario: Export carries no secrets
  Given any workspace, including one whose panes were bound to accounts
  When it is exported and the JSON is inspected
  Then it contains no API keys, no tokens, no account ids and no user ids, and importing it as a different user drops account-scoped elements with a visible report

Scenario: Every layout operation is reachable without a pointer
  Given a keyboard-only trader with a screen reader
  When they add, move, split, float, resize, focus and close panels using only the keyboard
  Then each operation has an equivalent in the panel menu, focus is never lost, and each result is announced once in a live region
```

## Technical notes / design
The layout is a **tree**, not a grid of absolute rectangles: `row`/`column`/`tabset`/`leaf` nodes with fractional sizes, serialised into `layouts.grid_spec` when `grid_preset = 'custom'` and reduced to a named preset (`1x1`, `2x1`, `1x2`, `2x2`, `1+3`, `3x3`) when it matches one — the CHECK constraint in §3.8.1 enumerates exactly those. Panes are rows in `layout_panes` keyed by `slot_index` (0..15, matching SCR-020's ">16 panels" warning), each carrying `pane_kind`, `symbol`, `interval_code`, `chart_template_id`, `indicator_preset_ids` and a free-form `pane_config`.

Reconciliation is keyed by stable pane id so a move is a *reparent*, not an unmount — this is what protects the GL context. Writes are debounced 2 s and sent as a full `PUT` with `If-Match` (the OpenAPI description says exactly this); a 412 raises SCR-029's conflict variant rather than clobbering.

Sync is a client-side bus, deliberately not a server round-trip (SCR-023: "runtime over a local sync bus"). It dispatches straight into engine instances, never through React state, to hold the ≤4 ms-across-6-panes budget.

Capability degradation (US-LAY-008) is measured, never sniffed: the frame-time probe from E11's benchmark harness decides, and the user is told the measured cost.

## Test plan
Unit: layout-tree algebra (split/move/tabify/close/normalise), preset↔tree round-trip, sync-bus fan-out, export/import schema validation. Contract: schemathesis over every `/workspaces*` operation including 412 and 422 paths. Integration: Postgres round-trip of workspace→layouts→panes with cascade delete. E2E (Playwright web + Electron): build 2x2, save, reload, restore; drag-resize; keyboard move; preset hotkeys; float/redock (Electron); export→import across users; delisted-symbol restore. Perf: B6 (4 synchronised charts) and the 6-pane worst case from §5.3 criterion 2; restore-to-interactive ≤3 s; preset apply ≤300 ms. A11y: axe-core on SCR-020..029 plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass over the keyboard docking flow.

## Security notes
Everything here is `scope: self`: a user may only read and write their own workspaces, and cross-user access returns 404 rather than 403 so existence is not disclosed. The export file is the main new attack surface in both directions — outbound it must never embed keys, tokens, account ids or user ids (US-LAY-007 NFR); inbound it is untrusted JSON that must be schema-validated, size-capped and parsed in a worker before a single node is applied. Panel titles, workspace names and imported labels are user content: length-capped, control-characters stripped, never rendered as HTML. Viewer keeps `workspaces:write` (`21-database-schema.md` §RBAC note) precisely because arranging one's own panes cannot emit an order.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Each panel is a `role="region"` with an accessible name ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m"); `F6`/`Ctrl+Tab` cycles regions with a visible focus indicator; every drag-and-drop dock operation has a mandatory keyboard equivalent via CMP-216's "Move panel" directional chooser (CMP-214's catalogue entry makes this non-negotiable). Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow` and arrow-key resize. Sync group membership is conveyed by letter badge and name, never by colour alone. Layout changes announce once, politely.

## Performance notes
Budgets: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001 NFR); ≥30 fps floor in the 6-pane worst case (roadmap §5.3.2); restore to interactive ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR); sync propagation ≤1 frame and ≤4 ms across 6 panes (SCR-023); preset apply ≤300 ms and panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-022/SCR-024); 2 MB import validates in ≤500 ms off the main thread (SCR-026). Hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s; panels mount lazily on first visibility.

## Observability
Analytics events per the screen catalogue: `workspace.saved`, `workspace.updated`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.exported`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.panel_added|removed|moved|floated|maximised`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`, `layout.conflict_detected`, `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}`, `sync.group_changed`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`. Metrics: `workspace_restore_seconds` histogram, `layout_apply_duration_ms`, `layout_conflict_total`, `panes_per_layout` histogram, `http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/workspaces*"}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 5 demonstrated end-to-end (reload, app restart, Electron relaunch, zero loss) and recorded.
- [ ] Worst-case 6-pane layout measured against the 30 fps floor and the 4-pane order-flow layout against 55 fps; numbers attached.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on `packages/dock` and the workspace feature, ≥85% on the workspace API router.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-020..029 plus a signed-off manual screen-reader pass of the keyboard docking flow.
- [ ] Security sign-off on export/import (no secrets outbound, validated untrusted input inbound) and the IDOR matrix.
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `14-screens-catalogue.md` reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA epic-level regression pass recorded; zero open P0/P1; demoed to the Owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (chart engine instances, sync group plumbing, frame-time probe), **E13** (indicator presets referenced by `layout_panes.indicator_preset_ids`), **E10** (app shell, Electron window management, hotkey layer), **E09** (users, sessions, `workspaces:*` permissions). Blocks **E16** (auto-record via `ix_lp_symbol`), and every R2 panel that needs somewhere to be docked.

```mermaid
graph TD
  K01[E15-K01 Spike: pane budget & capability profile]
  T01[E15-T01 workspaces/layouts/panes API + migration]
  T02[E15-T02 packages/dock layout tree + DockGrid]
  T03[E15-T03 SyncBus + engine sync integration]
  S01[E15-S01 Grid presets, gallery & layout hotkeys]
  S02[E15-S02 Docking, float, panel picker & menus]
  S03[E15-S03 Saved workspaces: save/restore/conflict]
  S04[E15-S04 Cross-pane sync configuration]
  S05[E15-S05 Linked vs independent price scaling]
  S07[E15-S07 Workspace export & import]
  S08[E15-S08 Responsive & reduced-capability layout]
  K01 --> T02
  T02 --> S01
  T02 --> S02
  T01 --> S03
  T02 --> S03
  T02 --> T03
  T03 --> S04
  S04 --> S05
  S03 --> S07
  S02 --> S08
  K01 --> S08
```

## Branch
`feat/e15-layouts-workspaces`

## References
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 (E15 row), §5.3 criteria 2 and 5, §11 dependency graph; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §16 LAY (US-LAY-001..008); `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-011, SCR-150, SCR-153; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-073, CMP-080..083, CMP-196, CMP-213..220, CMP-227; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-LAY-001..008; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, migration `0011_workspace`, §RBAC; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`, `/layout-presets`, `/chart-templates`; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2, §6 `sync`, R8, B6; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: multi-pane workflows, sync groups and panel-docking mental models
body:
## Context
E15 delivers the surface the Owner and the account managers will spend their entire working day inside: SCR-020 is *the* application, and every other screen in the product is a panel hosted by it. Eight stories (US-LAY-001..008) introduce grid layouts, saved workspaces, cross-pane sync groups, scale linking, panel docking/floating, layout hotkeys, workspace export/import and a reduced-capability profile. Between them they touch twelve screens (SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-150, SCR-153) and roughly thirty components. That is far too much interaction surface to design on intuition.

Three questions are genuinely open and cannot be answered from `14-screens-catalogue.md`.

**(1) How many panes do people actually work with, and how do they arrange them?** US-LAY-001 offers 1/2/3/4/6-pane presets plus custom splits; SCR-022 lists ten named presets (Scalping, Order-flow, Swing 3TF, Analyst, Fan-out review, plus five geometric grids). We do not know whether users live in one preset all day, switch presets per market session, or build one bespoke layout and never touch the gallery. The answer decides whether the preset gallery is a prominent modal or a quiet menu, and whether `Ctrl+1..9` hotkeys are the primary path.

**(2) What does "synced" mean to a trader?** US-LAY-003 exposes six independent sync axes (symbol, interval, crosshair, time range, drawings, account/group scope) across lettered groups A/B/C. Six independent booleans times three groups is a configuration space users routinely get wrong in competitor products - the classic failure is "I changed the symbol in one chart and it wrecked my other five". We need to know the expected default (all-on within a group? symbol+crosshair only?) and whether the group badge alone is sufficient to predict propagation before acting.

**(3) Is docking worth its complexity?** US-LAY-005 specifies drag-to-dock with six drop targets, floating OS windows, hide/restore and per-workspace persistence. Docking is expensive to build, expensive to make keyboard-accessible (CMP-214 mandates a full keyboard equivalent) and historically under-used. We need evidence on whether users re-dock panels regularly or arrange once and freeze.

This research runs in Sprint 02, four sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story in Sprint 06, so the wireframes (E15-D02) and every hi-fi ticket downstream are grounded in evidence rather than in a designer's preference.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Participants**: the Owner plus 4-6 comparable multi-chart traders (a mix of scalper and swing profiles, at least one on a 1280x800 laptop and at least one keyboard-dominant user), recruited per the research protocol in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`.
- **Method**: (a) 45-minute contextual interview over the participant's current terminal, screen-recorded, counting panes, recording how often layout changes and what triggers it; (b) a card-sort of the ten SCR-022 presets to establish naming and grouping; (c) a paper/Figma-prototype comprehension test of the SCR-023 sync model - shown a lettered group configuration, the participant predicts what happens when the symbol changes in one pane; (d) a docking-need probe: how the participant currently rearranges, and whether they would use a keyboard move mode.
- **Instruments**: discussion guide, consent form, sync-comprehension stimulus set (6 configurations), preset card deck, note template - all committed under `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/`.
- **Outputs** written to `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/findings.md`:
  - Recommended **default pane count and default preset** for first run of SCR-020, with evidence.
  - Recommended **default sync-axis set** per new group, and whether groups default to on or off.
  - A ranked list of the SCR-022 presets by expressed value, so the gallery can order and, if needed, cut them.
  - A go/no-go/reduce recommendation on **free-form docking** vs a simpler fixed-slot model for v1, with the cost of the mandatory keyboard equivalent stated.
  - Findings on the **workspace-switching** mental model (tabs in SCR-020 vs the CMP-073 switcher in SCR-011) - are workspaces documents or modes?
  - The **unsaved-changes expectation** (SCR-029): do users expect layout autosave, or explicit `Ctrl+S`? This directly sets a default that, if wrong, loses work.
  - A first cut of analytics events worth instrumenting (`layout.preset_applied`, `sync.group_changed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `workspace.saved`) so post-release we can check the research conclusions.
- **Open-question register** listing anything that must be resolved by prototype testing instead (feeds E15-D02's validation round).

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, token, colour or type decision - this ticket produces evidence and recommendations only; hi-fi work lives in E15-D03..D12.
- The chart panel's own internals (E11/E12/E13/E14 own those); this study treats a chart as an opaque rectangle.
- Trading-panel research (order ticket, DOM) - those belong to E30/E21.
- Quantitative A/B testing; the population is too small for statistical claims and the findings must say so.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four research questions are answered with evidence
  Given the findings document is reviewed by the CDO and the E15 FE lead
  When each of the four questions (pane count, sync defaults, docking need, workspace model) is checked
  Then each has a stated recommendation, the evidence behind it, and a confidence level
  And any question the study could not settle is listed in the open-question register with how it will be settled

Scenario: The sync model is comprehensible before it is used
  Given six sync configurations are shown to participants as static stimuli
  When each participant predicts the effect of changing the symbol in one pane
  Then the prediction accuracy is recorded per configuration
  And any configuration predicted correctly by fewer than 4 of 6 participants is flagged as a redesign requirement for E15-D06

Scenario: A recommendation contradicts the catalogue
  Given research shows that free-form docking is not valued enough to justify its cost
  When the findings are presented
  Then a scope-change proposal is written naming the affected stories (US-LAY-005) and screens (SCR-021, SCR-027)
  And the Owner decides before E15-D02 wireframes begin, with the decision recorded in the ticket

Scenario: Keyboard-only and low-resolution users are represented
  Given the participant mix
  Then at least one participant works keyboard-dominantly and at least one on a 1280x800 display
  And their specific findings are called out separately rather than averaged away

Scenario: Recruitment falls short
  Given fewer than four external participants can be recruited within the sprint
  Then the study still runs with the Owner plus whoever is available
  And the findings document states the reduced sample prominently at the top, with the conclusions that are therefore low-confidence explicitly marked
```

## Technical notes / design
The sync-comprehension test is the highest-value instrument here, because sync errors are *silent and destructive*: a mis-predicted propagation changes what the trader is looking at without any error message, and in a trading context that is a correctness problem, not a usability nicety. Design the stimuli so that the lettered badge (per SCR-023, letter carries meaning, never colour alone) is the only cue available - if participants cannot predict from the badge, the badge needs more information, and that requirement lands in E15-D06.

For the docking probe, ask participants to *do*, not to *say* - observed rearrangement frequency over a session beats stated preference. If the observed answer is "arranges once per week", the recommendation should be to keep drag-docking but demote it below presets in the visual hierarchy, which is a cheap change now and an expensive one later.

Record pane counts against the performance budget from US-LAY-001 (>=55 fps with four active order-flow panes): if the observed working set is six-plus panes, that is a finding for E11/E15 engineering, not just for design, and it must be escalated in the sprint review.

## Test plan
(1) Pilot the discussion guide and stimulus set with one internal participant and revise before the real sessions. (2) Run sessions; two researchers present, one facilitating, one noting. (3) Two independent analysts code the transcripts and reconcile; disagreements above a stated threshold are re-examined rather than averaged. (4) Findings walkthrough with the CDO, Architect and E15 FE lead; every recommendation is challenged for feasibility before it is accepted. (5) Traceability check: every one of US-LAY-001..008 is named at least once in the findings, or explicitly recorded as not covered by this study.

## Security notes
Sessions are screen-recorded over participants' live trading terminals, which can expose account balances, positions, API-key management screens and, in the worst case, credentials typed on camera. The protocol therefore requires: explicit written consent naming what is recorded; a pre-session checklist asking the participant to close key-management and funding screens; a facilitator instruction to pause recording immediately if a secret becomes visible; storage of recordings in the private research drive with access limited to the research team; and deletion on the retention schedule in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. No recording, transcript or quote in `findings.md` may contain an account id, an API key fragment, a real position size or a participant's real name - participants are P1..P6 throughout.

## Accessibility notes
Accessibility is a research input here, not an afterthought. The keyboard-dominant participant's session specifically probes: how they would move a panel without a mouse, whether `F6`-style region cycling matches their expectation, and whether they can tell which pane is focused. The findings must state the keyboard model that E15-D04 and E15-D15 will specify, including what the mandatory keyboard equivalent for docking (CMP-214) should feel like. Sessions themselves are run accessibly - materials at >=16px, no colour-only stimuli in the sync test, and time limits relaxed on request.

## Performance notes
The study collects the empirical inputs to the E15 performance budgets: observed working pane count, observed number of simultaneously visible order-flow panels, and the display resolutions in use. These numbers are handed to E11/E15 engineering to validate the >=55 fps four-pane target from US-LAY-001 and the <=3 s four-pane restore target from US-LAY-002. If the observed working set exceeds what the budget assumes, the mismatch is raised as a risk (R2 Render performance) in the sprint review rather than absorbed silently.

## Observability
The findings propose the analytics event set for the layout domain (`layout.preset_applied`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.reset`, `sync.group_changed`, `workspace.saved`, `workspace.restored`) with the properties needed to verify each research conclusion post-release - for example, `layout.preset_applied{presetId}` tells us whether the preset ranking from the card sort matched reality. These are analytics-only events on user preference state, not audit events, per SCR-021's analytics note.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Discussion guide, consent form and stimulus set committed under `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/`.
- [ ] >=5 sessions run (Owner + >=4 others) or the shortfall documented at the top of the findings.
- [ ] `findings.md` merged with a recommendation and confidence level for each of the four research questions.
- [ ] Sync-comprehension results tabulated per configuration, with failures flagged as requirements for E15-D06.
- [ ] Docking go/no-go/reduce recommendation recorded, and an Owner decision captured if it proposes a scope change.
- [ ] Analytics event proposal listed and accepted by the FE lead.
- [ ] Open-question register created and linked from E15-D02.
- [ ] Recordings stored per policy; no secrets, account ids or real names in any artefact.
- [ ] Findings walkthrough held with CDO, Architect and E15 FE lead; attendance recorded.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket (Status = Done)** - this is the gate that unblocks E15-D02, at least four sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 consuming stories.

## Dependencies

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 16 (US-LAY-001..008) as the question source.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-153 for the surfaces under study.
- No ticket dependencies - this is the first E15 design activity.

title: Wireframes: workspace shell, dock model, presets and sync - greyscale end to end
body:
## Context
With E15-D01's evidence in hand, this ticket settles the *structure* of the workspace surface in greyscale, before any pixel is polished. Wireframing first is not ceremony here: SCR-020 hosts every other panel in the product, so a structural mistake - a panel header that steals 40 px of chart height, a workspace switcher that hides which environment you are trading in, a sync badge that is unreadable at a glance - propagates into every screen E18..E41 will later drop into this shell. Fixing it in greyscale costs a day; fixing it after ten hi-fi files exist costs a sprint.

The wireframes cover the complete E15 surface as one coherent model: the workspace page and its tab strip (SCR-020), the docking interaction with all six drop targets and the mandatory keyboard move mode (SCR-021, CMP-214), the preset gallery (SCR-022), the sync configuration (SCR-023), the panel picker (SCR-024), workspace settings (SCR-025), import (SCR-026), the floating window (SCR-027), the panel context menu (SCR-028), the unsaved/conflict dialog (SCR-029), the multi-chart grid panel (SCR-049), the workspace switcher in the nav rail (SCR-011), the boot/restore state (SCR-150) and the reduced-capability layout (SCR-153).

Sprint 03 places this three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story in Sprint 06, leaving Sprints 04-05 for hi-fi and Sprint 06 as slack.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Greyscale wireframes** for every screen listed above, at 1920x1080 and at the 1280x800 minimum from SCR-020's sign-off checklist, showing real content density (a chart with a footprint, a DOM ladder, a positions grid) rather than lorem rectangles.
- **The layout tree model** drawn explicitly: how a `LayoutTree` (CMP-081 prop) maps to what the user sees - rows, columns, tab groups, leaf panels - and what each split/tabify operation does to that tree. This diagram is the shared vocabulary for design, FE and the `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}` payload.
- **Docking storyboard** (SCR-021): drag start, hover over each of the six targets (N/S/E/W/centre-tabify/float), the translucent result preview, invalid-drop feedback, drop commit, and the undo path. Drawn as frames, not described in prose.
- **Keyboard move mode storyboard**: the CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel" path - directional chooser, live preview, commit, cancel - proving that no layout operation is pointer-only, per CMP-214's mandatory keyboard equivalent.
- **Sync model wireframes** (SCR-023): the six axes as independent switches, lettered group badges on panel headers, the "conflicting sync" warning, and the per-pane scale-link state from US-LAY-004 including the refusal case when two panes have incompatible price magnitudes.
- **State inventory per screen**: loading skeleton, empty workspace, populated, unsaved (`*` on tab), save conflict, restored-after-crash, too-many-panels warning, panel-too-small compact view, reduced-capability - each drawn, none described only in a note.
- **Flow diagrams** (mermaid, into `docs/design/specs/e15-layout-flows.md`): create workspace, switch workspace with unsaved changes, apply a preset over a dirty layout, add a panel, float and re-dock, export then import on another machine.
- **Hotkey map** for the layout layer: `Ctrl+1..9` presets, `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `Alt+drag` move, `F11` full-screen panel, `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycle panels, `F6` region cycle, `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` sync group, `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync, `Shift+F10` panel menu - cross-checked against the global hotkey table so that US-LAY-006's conflict scenario has a concrete list to detect conflicts against.
- **Validation round**: a clickable greyscale prototype tested with the Owner plus two participants from E15-D01, focused on the three interactions research flagged as risky (preset over dirty layout, sync prediction, keyboard move).

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, elevation, iconography and final spacing - all deferred to E15-D03..D12.
- Motion timing and easing (E15-D14).
- The internals of any hosted panel (chart, DOM, ticket) - represented as labelled rectangles.
- Design-system token or component authoring (E15-D13).
- The Electron window-management implementation detail; SCR-027 is wireframed as a window with chrome, not as an OS integration spec.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E15 screen exists in greyscale at both reference widths
  Given the wireframe file is reviewed
  When SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-023, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-026, SCR-027, SCR-028, SCR-029, SCR-049, SCR-150 and SCR-153 are walked
  Then each has frames at 1920x1080 and 1280x800
  And at 1280x800 no frame contains an overlap or a clipped control

Scenario: No layout operation is pointer-only
  Given the docking storyboard and the keyboard move storyboard
  When every operation in the pointer storyboard is enumerated (move, split, tabify, resize, float, close, maximise)
  Then each has a named keyboard equivalent drawn in the keyboard storyboard
  And the equivalents are reachable from CMP-216 PanelMenu and from a documented shortcut

Scenario: Applying a preset over unsaved work is never silently destructive
  Given a workspace with unsaved layout changes
  When a preset is applied from SCR-022
  Then the wireframe routes through SCR-029 with Save / Discard / Cancel as explicit verbs
  And no destructive option is the default focus

Scenario: Sync prediction improves over the research baseline
  Given the greyscale prototype is tested with three participants using the E15-D01 stimulus configurations
  When they predict the effect of changing the symbol in one pane
  Then prediction accuracy is at least 5 of 6 configurations per participant
  And any configuration still mispredicted is redesigned before sign-off

Scenario: A panel is dragged somewhere it cannot go
  Given a panel is dragged over a region that cannot accept it (for example a leaf below minimum size)
  Then the wireframe shows the invalid-drop treatment and a plain-language reason
  And the drag can be cancelled with Esc, returning the panel to its origin with no layout mutation

Scenario: The workspace fails to restore
  Given a saved workspace references a delisted symbol (US-LAY-002 edge case)
  Then the affected pane is drawn in an explicit error state naming the symbol
  And the remaining panes are drawn as loaded, proving partial restore is designed rather than an all-or-nothing failure
```

## Technical notes / design
The single most consequential structural decision is **chrome budget**. Every pixel spent on tab strip, panel header, sync badge and status bar is a pixel not showing market data, and SCR-020 stacks up to four levels of chrome above a chart. The wireframes must state a maximum total vertical chrome allowance at 1280x800 and demonstrate the layout inside it, with the compact density mode showing how it shrinks.

The layout tree diagram matters beyond design: CMP-081 takes `layout: LayoutTree` and the workspace document is persisted through `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, so design, FE and API must share one mental model of what a split is. Draw the tree next to the rendered result for at least three non-trivial layouts (2x2, 1+3, a tabified stack inside a column).

Crash restore (SCR-020's "Restored your layout from 14:02") is designed here rather than bolted on, because it changes the tab strip's information design - the user must be able to tell a restored layout from a saved one before they hit `Ctrl+S` and overwrite a good workspace with a recovered one.

The "too many panels" case (>16 per SCR-020, and US-LAY-001's confirmation-with-measured-frame-cost requirement) is drawn as a real frame showing where the measured cost appears and what the confirm step says. A warning that cannot be located is not a warning.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-by-screen walkthrough against the sign-off checklists already written in `14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-020..029, SCR-049 and SCR-153 - every checkbox in those lists is treated as an acceptance item here. (2) Flow walkthrough of the six mermaid flows with the FE lead, checking each is buildable against the `/workspaces` API surface. (3) Moderated greyscale prototype test (Owner + 2 participants) on the three risky interactions. (4) Keyboard-path audit: attempt every operation with a pointer disallowed. (5) 1280x800 overlap sweep. (6) Traceability check that every one of US-LAY-001..008 maps to at least one wireframe frame.

## Security notes
The workspace surface is where environment confusion becomes dangerous: a panel shows a DEMO position while the ticket next to it is bound to LIVE. The wireframes must establish, structurally, that the environment is visible from every panel that can place an order and from every floating window (SCR-027, CMP-215) - not merely once in the top bar. SCR-020's checklist already requires DEMO and LIVE chrome variants; this ticket draws them. Additionally, the import wireframe (SCR-026) must show, in copy, that an imported workspace carries no credentials and no account bindings (US-LAY-007), and the export preview must visibly enumerate what is included so that a user sharing a workspace with a manager can verify it before sending.

## Accessibility notes
The wireframes specify the structural a11y contract that hi-fi will style: each panel is a `role="region"` with an accessible name that includes panel type, symbol and interval ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m"); `F6` cycles regions and `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycles panels; the active panel has a focus affordance that is not colour-only; layout changes are announced through a polite live region ("Layout changed to 2 by 2", "Chart moved to bottom right") per CMP-081 and CMP-214; splitters are `role="separator"` with arrow-key resize and announced `aria-valuenow`; sync-group membership is conveyed by letter and name, never by colour alone. The keyboard move storyboard is a first-class deliverable, not an appendix.

## Performance notes
Structure drives cost. The wireframes must encode three performance-protecting decisions so hi-fi cannot undo them: (1) panels mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s, so the empty/loading frames show a skeleton rather than data; (2) a layout change must never remount the WebGL context, so the tab and preset flows are drawn as re-parenting, not as re-creation; (3) the drag preview is a single translucent rectangle drawn with transforms, never a live panel, so the storyboard shows a ghost. The budgets these protect are US-LAY-001's >=55 fps with four order-flow panes and US-LAY-002's <=3 s four-pane restore.

## Observability
The wireframes annotate where each analytics event fires, using the names already fixed in the screens catalogue: `layout.panel_added`, `layout.panel_removed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.saved`, `layout.reset`, `layout.preset_previewed`, `layout.preset_applied`, `sync.group_changed`, `layout.conflict_detected`, `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`. Annotating on the wireframe means FE inherits the instrumentation plan with the structure instead of retrofitting it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Wireframes complete for all 14 screens at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, with real-density content.
- [ ] Layout tree model diagram merged and agreed with the FE lead and the API owner.
- [ ] Docking and keyboard-move storyboards complete; pointer/keyboard parity audit passed.
- [ ] State inventory drawn for every screen (no state exists only as a note).
- [ ] Six flow diagrams merged into `docs/design/specs/e15-layout-flows.md`.
- [ ] Layout hotkey map cross-checked against the global hotkey table with conflicts listed.
- [ ] Greyscale prototype test run; sync prediction accuracy >=5/6 per participant or the failing configurations redesigned.
- [ ] Every sign-off checklist item from `14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-020..029, SCR-049 and SCR-153 is either satisfied or explicitly deferred to a named hi-fi ticket.
- [ ] Chrome budget at 1280x800 stated numerically and demonstrated.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 03, three sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D01** - research findings, especially the sync defaults, preset ranking and docking go/no-go.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` sign-off checklists for the E15 screens.
- E05 design system v0 for the greyscale primitives and density scale.
- E10 app shell structure (SCR-010) - the workspace mounts inside it; the chrome budget must be agreed with E10's shell design.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-150, SCR-153

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-020 workspace page, tab strip and panel chrome
body:
## Context
SCR-020 is the product. Route `/w/:workspaceId`, it is where the Owner spends the trading day, and it is the host for every panel E11..E41 will ever build. This ticket takes the greyscale structure from E15-D02 to a signed-off hi-fi specification of the workspace page itself and the panel chrome that frames every hosted panel: CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid, CMP-082 PanelHeader, plus the tab strip and the top-bar layout/sync/save controls.

The design tension is stated in one number: at 1280x800, every pixel of chrome is a pixel of missing market data, yet a panel with no visible identity is a panel whose symbol and environment the user can get wrong. The specification must resolve that tension explicitly with a measured chrome budget per density mode, rather than leaving it to be discovered during implementation.

Sprint 04 is two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 stories that consume it (US-LAY-001 grid layouts, US-LAY-002 saved workspaces, US-LAY-005 panel docking).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Hi-fi frames for SCR-020** in dark (default) and light themes, at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, in all three densities (compact / cosy / comfortable from `16-design-system-brief.md`), using real-density content: a footprint chart, a DOM ladder, a positions grid, a tape.
- **CMP-082 PanelHeader** specified completely: title, symbol/interval mini-controls, sync-group letter badge, environment indicator where applicable, action toolbar (`role="toolbar"` with arrow-key nav), overflow (CMP-216) and close. States: default, focused-panel, hovered, dragging, too-narrow (progressive disclosure order stated explicitly - what drops first), read-only (viewer role), error.
- **CMP-080 DockPanel** frame treatment: border, elevation, radius per tokens; the **active-panel affordance**, which must be perceivable without colour (SCR-020 checklist) and must not consume layout space when it changes state, so that focusing a panel never reflows the chart.
- **CMP-081 DockGrid** gutter, splitter hit areas (>=24 px per `05-accessibility-standard.md` while remaining visually thin), and the gutter's focus-visible treatment.
- **Tab strip**: workspace tabs with the unsaved `*` marker, active/inactive/hover/focus, the `+` new-workspace affordance, overflow when tabs exceed width, and a rename-in-place state.
- **CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher** as used in the tab strip context (its nav-rail placement is E15-D05): default, empty/first-run, many-workspaces.
- **Top-bar controls**: `[layout v] [sync v] [save] [reset]` with their disabled and dirty states, and the `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S` hints via CMP-022 Kbd.
- **Role variants**: the default owner layout, manager layout and viewer layout drawn as three distinct frames (SCR-020 checklist), with viewer's read-only degradation visible in the chrome.
- **DEMO and LIVE chrome variants** drawn (SCR-020 checklist), including how the environment reads from a panel that is not adjacent to the top bar.
- **States**: loading skeleton (panel frames, no data), empty workspace with the panel picker entry point, unsaved changes, save conflict entry to SCR-029, restored-after-crash banner ("Restored your layout from 14:02"), and >16 panels performance warning with the measured frame cost shown.
- **Chrome budget table**: measured vertical and horizontal chrome per density at both reference widths, with the remaining canvas area stated.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-page.md`; Storybook story list agreed with FE for CMP-073/080/081/082.

## Out of scope
- The docking interaction itself - drop zones, drag preview, keyboard move mode (E15-D04).
- Preset gallery (E15-D05), sync configuration UI (E15-D06), panel picker and context menu (E15-D07), settings/conflict dialogs (E15-D08), import (E15-D09), floating window (E15-D10), multi-chart grid (E15-D11), reduced-capability (E15-D12).
- Motion (E15-D14) beyond naming which transitions exist.
- Any new token or component - raised into E15-D13 instead of invented here.
- The internals of hosted panels.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The full state and density matrix is drawn
  Given the hi-fi file is reviewed
  When the matrix of (loading, empty, populated, unsaved, conflict, crash-restored, over-16-panels) x (compact, cosy, comfortable) x (dark, light) is walked
  Then every required cell exists as a frame
  And no cell is represented by a note reading "same as above"

Scenario: The focused panel is identifiable without colour
  Given the populated frame is rendered in greyscale and under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation
  Then the focused panel remains identifiable by a non-hue channel
  And the sync-group badge remains readable as a letter

Scenario: Chrome fits the minimum supported window
  Given the 1280x800 frame in compact density with four panels
  Then no control overlaps, no label is clipped, and the measured chrome total matches the budget table
  And every panel still shows its symbol, interval and environment

Scenario: Environment is unambiguous from any order-capable panel
  Given the LIVE variant frame
  When any panel capable of placing an order is examined in isolation, cropped away from the top bar
  Then the environment is still readable within that crop

Scenario: A panel is narrower than its header can show
  Given a panel resized below the width its header needs
  Then the progressive-disclosure frame shows which elements drop and in what order
  And the panel's accessible name is unchanged, so the screen-reader experience does not degrade with width

Scenario: Focus state causes no reflow
  Given the focused and unfocused frames of the same panel
  When their content rectangles are compared
  Then the content rectangle is identical, proving the focus affordance is drawn inside the existing frame
```

## Technical notes / design
The active-panel affordance is deliberately constrained to draw *inside* the existing panel frame. A focus ring that adds outward thickness changes the panel's content box, which forces a chart resize, which on a WebGL canvas means a re-allocation and a dropped frame - every time the user clicks between panels. Specify an inset treatment and say so in the spec, so the constraint survives implementation.

Panel header progressive disclosure needs an explicit order because it will be exercised constantly in 2x2 and 3x3 layouts: the recommended order is close > overflow > action toolbar > interval > symbol > title, with symbol and environment the last things standing, since those are the two facts a user must never lose.

Crash restore must be visually distinct from a normal load in the tab strip, not only in a transient banner: a user who misses the banner and presses `Ctrl+S` would overwrite a good saved workspace with a recovered one. Draw a persistent marker that clears on explicit save or discard.

The >16-panel warning carries the *measured* frame cost per US-LAY-001, not a generic caution. The spec must define where that number appears and what units it uses (ms/frame and the derived fps), because the story requires confirmation based on a measurement.

## Test plan
(1) Full matrix walk in dark, light, three densities, at 100/125/200% zoom. (2) Automated contrast measurement on every chrome element against the darkest and lightest hosted-panel backgrounds; values pasted into the spec. (3) Colour-vision simulation for focus affordance and sync badge. (4) Token audit - every value resolves to a token, no raw hex or px. (5) Crop test: each order-capable panel cropped alone must disclose symbol + environment. (6) Reflow test comparing focused/unfocused content rectangles. (7) Handoff dry run - an FE engineer rebuilds the panel header from the spec alone and the differences are recorded. (8) Checklist sweep against `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020's design sign-off list.

## Security notes
This surface is where environment confusion turns into real money lost. The specification must guarantee that DEMO/LIVE is disclosed on the workspace chrome *and* independently on every panel that can place an order, so that a maximised or cropped panel cannot hide it; it must also specify that the LIVE treatment is not a colour-only cue. Viewer-role chrome must show read-only affordances honestly - but the spec must state in writing that hiding a control is presentation, never authorisation: RBAC is enforced by the API (E09), and the design must not imply otherwise. Workspace names are user-supplied and rendered in tabs, so the spec states that names are truncated for display and treated as text, never as markup, and that the 1-40 character validation from SCR-020 is enforced at input.

## Accessibility notes
Each panel is a `role="region"` whose accessible name includes type, symbol and interval ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute"); `F6` cycles regions and `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycles panels, with the focus affordance visible in both themes and at 200% zoom. CMP-082's action area is a `role="toolbar"` with roving tabindex. Splitter hit areas are >=24 px. The tab strip is a proper tablist with arrow-key navigation, and the unsaved marker is conveyed in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"), not by the `*` glyph alone. Layout changes announce politely via CMP-081's live region. All text meets 4.5:1 and all UI/graphical elements 3:1, measured against both extremes of hosted-panel background.

## Performance notes
Three constraints are written into the spec as normative statements, not suggestions: the focus affordance must not change the content box (no chart resize on focus); chrome hover/active feedback is CSS-only and must never trigger a canvas repaint; and skeletons for the loading state must not fetch data, since panels mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s. Target budgets inherited: >=55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001), panel mount <=150 ms (CMP-080), layout transition <=200 ms (CMP-081), four-pane restore to interactive <=3 s (US-LAY-002).

## Observability
The spec annotates `workspace.saved`, `workspace.restored`, `panel.added`, `panel.removed`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset` and the crash-restore event with the properties needed to answer real questions later: how often crash restore fires, how many panels people actually run, and how often the >16-panel warning is overridden. It also names the one metric FE must emit for the warning itself - measured frame cost at the moment of the warning - since the story's confirmation text depends on it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full state x density x theme matrix drawn at both reference widths; no "same as above" cells.
- [ ] Owner, manager and viewer default layouts drawn; DEMO and LIVE variants drawn.
- [ ] Chrome budget table measured and recorded for all three densities at 1280x800 and 1920x1080.
- [ ] Contrast measurements recorded and passing WCAG 2.2 AA over both background extremes.
- [ ] Colour-blind simulation clean for focus affordance and sync badge.
- [ ] Focus-affordance reflow test passed (identical content rectangles).
- [ ] Crop test passed for every order-capable panel.
- [ ] Token audit clean; any needed new token raised into E15-D13.
- [ ] Storybook story lists agreed with FE for CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-page.md` merged; `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 and `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated where the design diverged.
- [ ] Every SCR-020 design sign-off checklist item satisfied.
- [ ] Handoff dry run completed with an FE engineer.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 04, two sprints before the Sprint 06 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D02** - structure, chrome budget and state inventory.
- E05 design system v0 (tokens, density scale, elevation, focus ring).
- E10 app shell (SCR-010) - the workspace mounts inside the shell; chrome totals must be agreed jointly.

## Branch
`design/e15-workspace-page-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 (incl. its design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-216, CMP-022
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-002, US-LAY-005

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-021 dock system - drop zones, drag preview, keyboard move mode
body:
## Context
Docking is the interaction that makes SCR-020 feel like a terminal rather than a web page, and it is also the single most accessibility-hostile pattern in the product: drag-and-drop with spatial drop targets is, by default, unusable without a pointer. `15-component-catalogue.md` therefore makes the keyboard equivalent **mandatory** for CMP-214 DockDropZone, and this ticket specifies both paths to the same fidelity - the pointer storyboard and the keyboard move mode are equal deliverables, not a primary and a fallback.

SCR-021 covers six drop targets (north, south, east, west, centre-tabify, float), splitter resizing by mouse or `Alt+Shift+arrows`, invalid-drop feedback, the floating/maximised/minimised-to-tab states, and the "panel too small - showing compact view" case. It consumes CMP-083 SplitPane, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-215 FloatingWindowFrame (frame reference only; full spec in E15-D10) and CMP-216 PanelMenu (menu spec in E15-D07).

Sprint 04, two sprints before the Sprint 06 US-LAY-005 story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pointer storyboard**, frame by frame: drag start (grab affordance, cursor, source panel treatment), hover over each of the six targets with its distinct zone highlight and a translucent preview of the *resulting rectangle* (not merely a highlighted edge), commit, and Esc-cancel returning to origin.
- **Zone geometry spec**: the pixel/percentage regions that map to each of the six targets within a panel, including how zones behave in a very small panel where naive edge bands would leave no centre region - the degenerate case must be drawn, not assumed away.
- **Invalid-drop treatment**: cursor, zone styling and the plain-language reason ("Can't dock here - the panel would be below its minimum size"), including where that text appears so it is visible while the pointer is held.
- **Keyboard move mode storyboard**, at equal fidelity: entered from CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel" or `Shift+F10`; a directional chooser showing the six destinations with their keys; live preview highlighting the resulting rectangle; Enter to commit, Esc to cancel; and the polite announcement text for each step ("Move mode. Choose a destination. Left, right, top, bottom, tab into, or float." / "Chart moved to bottom right.").
- **Keyboard resize**: splitter focus treatment, `Alt+Shift+arrow` and arrow-key behaviour on a focused `role="separator"`, the step size, the coarse/fine modifier, and the announced `aria-valuenow` text.
- **Splitter states**: rest, hover, active-drag, focused, at-minimum (cannot move further, with feedback), and the >=24 px hit area drawn over a visually thin divider.
- **Panel-too-small state**: the compact view threshold, what a panel shows below it, and how the user learns why.
- **Maximise / minimise-to-tab / float states** at the dock level: what the layout looks like while one panel is maximised (`F11`), how the rest is preserved, and how restore returns the exact previous tree.
- **Undo**: how a mis-drop is reverted, with the affordance drawn (toast with Undo, and/or `Ctrl+Z` scope stated explicitly - layout undo must not be confused with drawing undo from E14).
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-dock-system.md`; Storybook lists for CMP-083 and CMP-214.

## Out of scope
- The floating OS window's own chrome and multi-monitor behaviour (E15-D10).
- The panel context menu's full item set (E15-D07) - referenced here only as the entry point to move mode.
- Motion curves and durations (E15-D14); this ticket states which transitions exist and their perceptual requirement, not their easing.
- Workspace persistence of the resulting layout (E15-D08 settings, E15-D03 chrome).
- Multi-chart grid cell arrangement (E15-D11) - a different, panel-internal grid.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every pointer operation has an equal keyboard path
  Given the pointer storyboard enumerates move, split-left, split-right, split-top, split-bottom, tabify, float, resize, maximise and close
  When each is looked up in the keyboard storyboard
  Then each has a drawn keyboard path with a named key, a live preview and an announcement
  And no operation is documented as "pointer only"

Scenario: The drop preview shows the outcome, not the target
  Given a drag hovering the east zone of a panel
  Then the frame shows a translucent rectangle in the shape and position the panel will occupy after the drop
  And the existing panels are shown at the sizes they will have after the drop

Scenario: Drop zones remain usable in a small panel
  Given a panel at its minimum size where edge bands would consume the whole area
  Then the degenerate-case frame shows the reduced zone set that is offered and which targets are withdrawn
  And the withdrawn targets are still reachable through keyboard move mode

Scenario: A drop that would violate minimum size is refused
  Given a drag over a target that would make a neighbour smaller than its minimum
  Then the invalid-drop frame shows the refusal styling and a reason naming the constraint
  And releasing the pointer performs no layout mutation

Scenario: Esc during a drag restores the original layout exactly
  Given a drag in progress with a preview shown
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the frame shows the original layout unchanged and the preview removed
  And the same is specified for Esc during keyboard move mode

Scenario: A drag preview never obscures its own drop target
  Given the drag preview frames
  Then the ghost is specified to be offset or translucent such that the active zone highlight remains visible
  And this is demonstrated in the frame where the panel is larger than the target region
```

## Technical notes / design
Drop-zone geometry is specified in the design rather than left to FE because it is perceptual: bands that are too thin make docking feel like a dexterity test, bands that are too thick make tabify unreachable. Specify bands as a percentage of the panel's smaller dimension with an absolute minimum and maximum in px, and draw the result at three panel sizes.

Keyboard move mode is designed as a *mode with visible instructions*, not as a set of hidden shortcuts. A mode the user cannot see is a mode they cannot exit; the storyboard must show the persistent instruction affordance and the Esc route, matching SCR-021's checklist item "keyboard move mode drawn with its own visible instructions".

Layout undo scope must be stated explicitly. E14 gives `Ctrl+Z` to drawing operations on the chart canvas; if layout also claims `Ctrl+Z`, the binding is ambiguous depending on focus. The recommendation to specify and defend is: layout mutations are undone from a toast affordance and from the panel menu, and `Ctrl+Z` remains owned by the focused panel's own undo stack. Whatever is chosen must be recorded here and reflected in the E15-D02 hotkey map and in `US-SET-002`'s conflict detection.

The drop commits exactly one layout mutation (SCR-021 performance note) - the spec should make that visible by showing a single transition to the final state, never an intermediate reflow.

## Test plan
(1) Pointer/keyboard parity audit: enumerate operations, confirm each has both paths drawn. (2) Zone geometry validated at three panel sizes including minimum. (3) Contrast measurement of zone highlights and the focused-splitter treatment over the darkest and lightest panel content. (4) Colour-vision simulation - the active zone must be distinguishable without hue. (5) Moderated keyboard walkthrough with a keyboard-dominant participant using a clickable prototype of move mode; success criterion is completing a move to a named destination without instruction. (6) Announcement script review with the a11y specialist (feeds E15-D15). (7) Checklist sweep against SCR-021's sign-off list. (8) Handoff dry run rebuilding the splitter states from the spec alone.

## Security notes
No credentials, keys or account data appear on this surface, and layout operations are analytics-only, not audit events (per SCR-021). Two risks remain and are addressed in the spec. First, **destructive ambiguity**: a drag that lands wrongly can visually destroy a carefully built layout, and if the workspace autosaves, the damage is persisted; the spec therefore requires the undo affordance to remain available until the next explicit save, and requires that a drop never silently overwrites the saved workspace without either an explicit save or a clearly marked dirty state. Second, **maximise hiding environment**: `F11` full-screen on a trading panel must retain the DEMO/LIVE disclosure specified in E15-D03, so that a maximised panel cannot conceal which environment an order would reach.

## Accessibility notes
This is the ticket where WCAG 2.2's pointer-gesture and drag requirements are actually met. Every drag operation has a single-pointer alternative *and* a keyboard alternative (2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.1.1 Keyboard). Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-valuenow` announced as a percentage, arrow-key operable, with a >=24 px target (2.5.8). Move mode publishes its instructions visibly and announces each step through a polite live region; the commit announcement names the panel and its destination ("Chart moved to bottom right"). Focus never gets lost: after a move, focus stays on the moved panel's header. Zone highlights meet 3:1 against every possible underlying panel content, which is why the contrast measurement is taken against content extremes rather than against a neutral background.

## Performance notes
The spec states three normative constraints. The drag preview is CSS-transform-only - no live panel, no canvas in the ghost - so dragging cannot cost chart frames. The drop commits exactly one layout mutation, so the tree is rebuilt once. Splitter dragging must throttle layout writes to one per animation frame and must not remount the WebGL context, since a resize that recreates a GL context would stall visibly. The governing budgets are US-LAY-001's >=55 fps with four order-flow panes and CMP-081's <=200 ms layout transition.

## Observability
Annotated events: `layout.panel_moved{from,to,method:"pointer"|"keyboard"}`, `layout.split_created{orientation}`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.drop_rejected{reason}` and `layout.move_cancelled{method}`. The `method` property is deliberate - it is the only way to find out post-release whether the mandatory keyboard path is actually used, which is the question that decides whether to invest further in it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pointer storyboard complete for all six targets plus resize, maximise and float.
- [ ] Keyboard move-mode storyboard complete at equal fidelity, with visible instructions and announcements scripted.
- [ ] Pointer/keyboard parity audit passed; no operation is pointer-only.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-022 layout preset gallery & SCR-011 workspace switcher
body:
## Context
Most users will never build a layout by dragging panels; they will pick one from a gallery and live in it. That makes SCR-022 the real entry point to E15's value, and CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu the control that actually gets used, with `Ctrl+1..9` behind it for the power path (US-LAY-006). SCR-011, the expanded navigation rail with CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, is its sibling: the gallery picks an *arrangement*, the switcher picks a *saved workspace*, and users confuse the two unless the design distinguishes them clearly.

The gallery ships ten presets: five geometric (1x1, 2x1, 2x2, 1+3, 3+1) and five semantic (Scalping, Order-flow, Swing 3TF, Analyst, Fan-out review). E15-D01's card sort ranked them; this ticket applies that ranking to ordering and, if the research recommended cuts, records them. SCR-022's own checklist additionally names built-in presets (Scalper DOM, Footprint focus, Multi-chart 2x2, Analysis/journal, Replay) - reconciling that list with the catalogue's is part of this ticket's work, and the reconciled list must be written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md`.

Sprint 04, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 US-LAY-001/US-LAY-006 stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-022 hi-fi** in dark and light, both reference widths: the geometric preset row, the named-preset grid, the "Keep current symbols" option, and Apply/Cancel.
- **Preset thumbnails** as static SVG (performance note in SCR-022 mandates this), drawn so that the arrangement is readable at thumbnail size, plus the `alt`/accessible-name text for each one enumerating its panels ("Scalping: chart, DOM ladder, order ticket, tape").
- **Reconciled preset inventory**: one authoritative list merged from the catalogue's two lists, each with id, label, pane count, panel composition and a one-line description; delivered as a table in the spec and written back to SCR-022.
- **User presets**: saved-custom entries with rename and delete, the save-current affordance (`Ctrl+Shift+S` path), and the empty user-preset state with a clear first-run instruction.
- **Destructive confirmation**: the "Applying a preset replaces the current layout. Settings of surviving panels are kept." warning, drawn in place, plus the route into SCR-029 when the current layout is dirty.
- **CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu** as the compact top-bar menu variant: default, active preset indicated, with custom saved presets, overflow.
- **SCR-011 hi-fi**: the expanded navigation rail with CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher - workspace list with active indicator, create, rename-in-place, delete (confirm-gated per CMP-073), search/filter when the list is long, and the empty/first-run state.
- **Hotkey surfacing**: `Ctrl+1..9` shown against the first nine presets via CMP-022 Kbd, with the mapping rule stated (which nine, and what happens when the user has more than nine).
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-presets-and-switcher.md`; Storybook lists for CMP-217 and CMP-073.

## Out of scope
- The dock interaction that a preset ultimately produces (E15-D04).
- Workspace settings and the unsaved/conflict dialog internals (E15-D08).
- Panel picker (E15-D07).
- The layout-preset API shape - referenced (`GET /api/v1/layout-presets`, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`) but owned by the engineering chunk.
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every preset is identifiable without seeing the thumbnail
  Given the accessible-name text for each preset
  When a screen-reader script is read aloud with thumbnails hidden
  Then each preset's arrangement and panel composition are understandable from text alone
  And no name relies on the word "this" or on visual position

Scenario: Applying a preset over unsaved work is confirmed
  Given the current workspace has unsaved layout changes
  When Apply is chosen in the gallery
  Then the frame routes through SCR-029 with Save, Discard and Cancel as explicit verbs
  And no destructive action holds initial focus

Scenario: Thumbnails remain readable at their smallest rendered size
  Given the thumbnails rendered at the gallery's smallest breakpoint and at 200% browser zoom
  Then each arrangement is still distinguishable from every other in the set
  And any two thumbnails judged confusable are redrawn before sign-off

Scenario: The user has no custom presets yet
  Given a first-run user opens the gallery
  Then the empty user-preset region explains how a custom preset is created rather than showing a bare empty box

Scenario: More presets exist than there are number hotkeys
  Given a user has saved twelve custom presets
  Then the spec states which nine carry Ctrl+1..9, how that assignment is changed, and how the remaining presets are reached

Scenario: Workspace switching with unsaved changes
  Given the active workspace is dirty
  When another workspace is selected in SCR-011
  Then the switcher routes through the same SCR-029 dialog
  And the dirty marker is visible in the switcher list, not only on the tab strip
```

## Technical notes / design
The gallery must make the *difference between a preset and a workspace* obvious, because the failure mode is a user believing they have switched setups when they have only rearranged panes and lost their symbol bindings. The design lever is language plus placement: presets live behind the layout control in the top bar and speak in arrangements; workspaces live in the tab strip and the nav rail and speak in names. The spec states this rule so later screens do not blur it.

"Keep current symbols" is the option that decides whether applying a preset is cheap or catastrophic. Draw its default state explicitly (recommended: on) and show, in the confirmation copy, what happens to panels that have no counterpart in the new arrangement.

Thumbnails are static SVG by mandate. That means the visual language must carry panel *type* without live content - use labelled regions with the panel-type glyph, not miniature screenshots, and verify the labels remain legible at the smallest size.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-reader script read-through with thumbnails suppressed. (2) Thumbnail distinguishability check at the smallest size and at 200% zoom, pairwise. (3) Contrast measurement on cards, active indicators, hotkey chips. (4) Keyboard walkthrough: open gallery, traverse as a listbox, apply, and cancel - all without a pointer. (5) Dirty-state routing test through SCR-029 from both the gallery and the switcher. (6) Token audit. (7) Checklist sweep against SCR-022's and SCR-011's sign-off lists. (8) Handoff dry run rebuilding a preset card.

## Security notes
Presets and workspaces are user content with user-supplied names rendered in lists, tabs and menus; the spec requires display truncation and text-only rendering with the 1-40 character validation from SCR-020 enforced at input, so a crafted name cannot break layout or inject markup. Deletion of a workspace is confirm-gated per CMP-073 and, per SCR-025, requires typing the name - this ticket draws the entry point but must not offer a one-click delete anywhere in the switcher. Presets carry no account bindings or credentials; where a named preset implies a trading panel (Scalping, Fan-out review), the spec states that applying it never changes the selected account or environment - only the arrangement - and the confirmation copy says so.

## Accessibility notes
The gallery is a listbox of cards: each option has an accessible name describing the arrangement in words (per CMP-217), arrow keys move between options, Enter applies, Esc cancels, and applying announces the result ("Layout changed to 2 by 2, four panes"). Thumbnails carry `alt` text enumerating panels and are never the sole carrier of meaning. The active preset is indicated by more than colour. In SCR-011 the workspace list is a proper list with the active item programmatically marked, rename-in-place moves focus into an input with a label, and the dirty state is in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"). Hotkey hints use CMP-022 Kbd with text, not images.

## Performance notes
Thumbnails are static SVG; the gallery pre-warms nothing and makes no live panels. Applying a preset rebuilds the dock tree in <=300 ms (SCR-022) and reuses existing panel instances where the type matches, avoiding GL context churn - the spec states this as a design constraint so the visual transition does not imply a teardown. The switcher's list is virtualised above a stated threshold so a user with many workspaces does not pay a render cost on every open.

## Observability
Annotated events: `layout.preset_previewed{presetId}`, `layout.preset_applied{presetId, keepSymbols, entry:"gallery"|"hotkey"|"menu"}`, `layout.preset_saved_as`, `layout.preset_deleted`, `workspace.switched{from,to,dirty}`. The `entry` property validates E15-D01's finding on whether the gallery or the hotkeys are the real path, and `keepSymbols` tells us whether the default was right.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-022 and SCR-011 drawn in both themes at both reference widths, all states.
- [ ] Reconciled preset inventory table merged and written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-022.
- [ ] Thumbnails drawn as static SVG with accessible names; distinguishability check passed.
- [ ] Empty user-preset state, rename and delete paths drawn; delete is confirm-gated.
- [ ] Dirty-layout routing through SCR-029 drawn from both gallery and switcher.
- [ ] `Ctrl+1..9` mapping rule stated, including the >9 presets case.
- [ ] Contrast and keyboard walkthroughs passed; token audit clean.
- [ ] SCR-022 and SCR-011 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-presets-and-switcher.md` merged; CMP-217 and CMP-073 Storybook lists agreed with FE.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 04, two sprints before Sprint 06.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D01** - preset ranking from the card sort.
- **E15-D02** - structure and flows.
- **E15-D03** - tab strip and chrome language the switcher must match.

## Branch
`design/e15-presets-switcher-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-022, SCR-029
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-001, CMP-022, CMP-043, CMP-050, CMP-073, CMP-217
