title: Hi-fi design: SCR-023 cross-pane sync groups and price-scale linking
body:
## Context
Sync is the feature where a usability defect becomes a *correctness* defect. If a trader believes two panes are showing the same symbol and they are not, or believes the interval is independent when it is linked, they read the wrong chart and act on it. There is no error message for this - the UI looks perfectly healthy while being wrong. E15-D01 measured how well users predict propagation from a static configuration; this ticket turns those findings into the signed-off design for SCR-023 (sync configuration), the per-panel sync badges, and the price-scale linking behaviour of US-LAY-004 including its refusal case.

The model: lettered groups A/B/C (plus none), six independent axes (symbol, crosshair, interval, time range, drawings - same symbol only, y-scale, selected account/group), with membership shown on each panel header by a letter-plus-colour badge where **the letter carries the meaning** and colour is redundant. Sync runs on a local bus with no server round-trip and must propagate within one frame (<=4 ms across six panes), so the design must never require a React re-render to show a synced crosshair.

Sprint 05, one sprint after the other core hi-fi work and still two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07 consuming story for US-LAY-003/US-LAY-004.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-023 hi-fi** (popover and modal variants) in both themes: group selector (A/B/C/none), the six axis switches with their labels and helper text, the live membership list ("Panels in group A: Chart 1, Chart 2, DOM"), and the apply/close model.
- **Per-panel sync badge** (rendered in CMP-082 PanelHeader): letter + colour, sizes for all three densities, states for none/A/B/C, and the treatment when a panel is too narrow to show the badge alongside the symbol - the badge must survive, per the disclosure order in E15-D03.
- **Colour assignment** for groups drawn from `color.sync.*` tokens (CMP-218), verified for contrast against every panel background and under all three colour-vision simulations, with the letter proving redundancy.
- **Conflict and warning states**: SCR-023's required warning ("Chart 3 has a different interval - crosshair sync will align by timestamp"), and the general pattern for "this axis cannot fully apply here" including drawings sync across panels on different symbols.
- **Price-scale linking** (US-LAY-004): linked and unlinked per-pane states drawn on the axis itself ("its unlinked state is shown on the axis"), the linked-zoom behaviour illustrated across two panes, and the **refusal frame** for incompatible magnitudes with the percentage-scale suggestion offered as an action, not just as prose. The relevant context menu entry points in SCR-043 are drawn.
- **Joining and leaving a group**: the flow showing that leaving a group does not reset the panel's own settings (SCR-023 checklist), and what the panel retains.
- **Hotkeys**: `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` assign active panel to a group, `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync - surfaced in the popover via CMP-022 Kbd.
- **Crosshair sync visual**: the dashed synced crosshair in receiving panes, distinct from a locally driven crosshair, at the densities used in practice.
- **Comprehension re-test**: the E15-D01 stimulus set re-run against the hi-fi prototype, with the accuracy target from the acceptance criteria.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-sync-model.md`; Storybook list for CMP-218 (Unsynced, GroupA, AllAxesOn, PartialAxes, plus Conflict and ScaleLinkRefused).

## Out of scope
- The sync engine itself (CMP-196 MultiChartLinker is non-visual and belongs to engineering).
- Multi-chart grid cell-level sync UI (E15-D11 covers the grid's own header, referencing this spec).
- Replay-clock synchronisation (E26).
- Motion (E15-D14).
- Account/group scope semantics beyond showing the axis switch - the trading side is E28/E34.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Propagation is predictable before it is triggered
  Given the hi-fi prototype and the six stimulus configurations from E15-D01
  When three participants predict the effect of changing the symbol, then the interval, in one pane
  Then prediction accuracy is at least 5 of 6 configurations per participant
  And any configuration still mispredicted is redesigned and re-tested before sign-off

Scenario: Group membership is never colour-only
  Given the panel header frames for groups A, B and C
  When rendered in greyscale and under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation
  Then the group remains identifiable by its letter
  And the badge's accessible name states the group in words

Scenario: An axis cannot fully apply
  Given two panes in the same group on different intervals with crosshair sync on
  Then the warning frame states that alignment is by timestamp and which pane differs
  And the warning is attached to the configuration surface and to the affected panel, not only to a transient toast

Scenario: Linking incompatible price scales is refused
  Given two panes showing symbols with very different price magnitudes
  When scale linking is requested
  Then the refusal frame explains why in plain language
  And percentage scale is offered as an actionable alternative in the same frame

Scenario: Leaving a group preserves the panel's own settings
  Given a panel in group A with its own interval and indicator set
  When it is set to "none"
  Then the frame shows the panel retaining its current symbol, interval, scale and indicators
  And the spec states explicitly that unsync is not a reset

Scenario: Drawings sync is requested across different symbols
  Given two panes in a group showing different symbols with drawings sync enabled
  Then the frame shows that drawings propagate only between same-symbol panes
  And the panel where it does not apply discloses that, rather than silently ignoring the setting
```

## Technical notes / design
The design principle is **disclose the consequence at the point of configuration**. Six booleans across three groups is a combinatorial space; the mitigation is not fewer options but a live membership list and inline consequence statements, so the user reads what will happen in this specific configuration rather than deducing it. The membership list is therefore a required element, not decoration.

The synced crosshair must be visually distinguishable from the locally driven one (dashed vs solid per SCR-023), because the trader needs to know whether the price under the pointer is theirs or a mirrored timestamp. Verify the dash pattern remains perceptible over dense footprint cells, which is the hostile background.

Scale-link refusal is a design-led guardrail: rather than permitting a link that renders one pane as a flat line, the design refuses and offers percentage scale. The refusal copy must name both symbols and both magnitudes so the user learns the rule rather than just hitting a wall.

Crosshair sync is specified to dispatch straight into the engine with no React re-render (SCR-023 performance note, <=4 ms across six panes). The design must therefore avoid any synced element that lives in React chrome - for example a synced-price readout in the panel header would break that contract; if one is wanted, the spec must mark it as engine-rendered.

## Test plan
(1) Comprehension re-test with three participants against the target accuracy. (2) Colour-vision simulation across all group badges and the synced crosshair. (3) Contrast measurement of badges and dashed crosshair over the darkest and lightest chart content, including a dense footprint. (4) Keyboard walkthrough: assign a group, toggle each axis, unsync - pointer-free. (5) Screen-reader script review for group changes and conflict warnings. (6) Edge-case sweep: different intervals, different symbols with drawings sync, incompatible magnitudes, a panel alone in a group. (7) Token audit. (8) SCR-023 and SCR-043 checklist sweep. (9) Handoff dry run rebuilding the badge and one axis switch.

## Security notes
Sync carries a real cross-context hazard: the "selected account/group" axis propagates the *trading* context between panels. The spec must therefore require that account-scope propagation is visibly disclosed on every receiving panel that can place an order, and that syncing account scope can never change the environment (DEMO vs LIVE) implicitly - if a group spans panels bound to different environments, the design refuses the account axis and says why. This prevents the worst plausible outcome of E15's design: an order ticket silently re-pointed at a live account because a chart pane changed groups. Sync state is workspace data only, contains no credentials, and is exported without account bindings (US-LAY-007), which the spec restates so the export preview in E15-D09 stays consistent.

## Accessibility notes
Each sync axis is an independently labelled switch (CMP-218), not a compound control. Group membership is conveyed by name and letter badge as well as colour; the badge's accessible name is the words ("Sync group A"). Group changes announce politely ("Chart 1 joined sync group A. Symbol and crosshair are shared with 2 panels.") - the announcement includes the consequence, not only the fact. Conflict warnings are text, associated with the control via `aria-describedby`, and repeated in the affected panel's accessible name so a screen-reader user working inside that panel is not left uninformed. The scale-link refusal is announced as an assertive message with the alternative action reachable by keyboard. The dashed synced crosshair has no accessible equivalent by itself; the spec requires the receiving pane to expose the synced timestamp/price through the existing panel readout so the information is not vision-only.

## Performance notes
The governing budget is US-LAY-003's propagation within one frame and SCR-023's <=4 ms across six panes. The design constraint that protects it is written normatively: no synced state may live in React-rendered chrome; synced crosshair and synced scale are engine-drawn. Badges are static and change only on group membership changes, never per frame. The membership list in the popover is computed on open, not subscribed.

## Observability
Annotated events: `sync.group_created`, `sync.group_changed{panelId, from, to}`, `sync.axis_toggled{axis, value}`, `sync.panel_joined_group`, `sync.panel_left_group`, plus two added here: `sync.conflict_shown{axis, reason}` and `sync.scale_link_refused{symbolA, symbolB}`. The last two are the evidence that tells us post-release whether the guardrails fire often enough to deserve a better design.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-023 drawn in both variants and themes, with all six axes, group states and the membership list.
- [ ] Panel sync badge drawn for all densities and the narrow-panel case.
- [ ] Group colours assigned from tokens; contrast and colour-vision checks passed; letter redundancy proven.
- [ ] Conflict warning and drawings-sync-across-symbols disclosure drawn.
- [ ] Scale-link linked, unlinked and refused states drawn, with percentage scale offered as an action.
- [ ] Leaving-a-group frame proves settings are preserved; spec states unsync is not a reset.
- [ ] Account-axis environment guardrail specified and drawn.
- [ ] Comprehension re-test passed at >=5/6 per participant.
- [ ] SCR-023 and SCR-043 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-sync-model.md` merged; CMP-218 Storybook list agreed with FE.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D01** - sync comprehension baseline and recommended defaults.
- **E15-D02** - sync wireframes and the hotkey map.
- **E15-D03** - CMP-082 PanelHeader, which hosts the badge.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-024 panel picker and SCR-028 panel context menu
body:
## Context
These two surfaces are how the workspace grows and how every panel is managed. SCR-024 is the catalogue of everything that can be added - a list that will keep growing through E18..E41 until it holds several dozen panel types - and SCR-028 is the per-panel menu that, by design, is **identical for every panel type so muscle memory transfers**. Both are small screens with outsized leverage: the picker is where a user discovers that footprint, CVD, DOM heatmap and the journal exist at all, and the context menu is the guaranteed keyboard route to every layout operation specified in E15-D04.

Both must handle capability and role honestly. The picker lists entries that are unavailable - "Needs a recorded symbol", "Owner only", behind a feature flag - and must show them disabled **with a reason** rather than hiding them, so the product is discoverable without misleading anyone about what they can do.

Sprint 05, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07 US-LAY-005 work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-024 hi-fi** in both themes: grouped catalogue with category headings as real headings, each entry showing icon, name, one-line description, thumbnail, and chips for "requires recording", "(estimated)" (CMP-227), "owner only", "beta/flagged".
- Picker **states**: default, search active with CMP-213 FuzzyList results, category filter applied, no results, disabled entry with its reason surfaced inline, and the placement preview showing where the panel will be inserted (SCR-024 checklist).
- **Entry inventory**: the complete panel-type list as of R1 with its growth rule - how categories are ordered and where future panel types from E18..E41 will land, so later epics extend rather than redesign.
- **SCR-028 hi-fi**: the full item set - Settings..., Duplicate, Move to >, Float, Full screen, Sync group >, Reset settings, Copy panel link, Close - with submenu behaviour, overflow near viewport edges, keyboard shortcut hints via CMP-022 Kbd, and disabled items showing a reason.
- **Role and capability variants** of the menu: viewer-restricted, browser build (Float replaced with the maximised-overlay behaviour and its explanatory note), and a panel whose type has no settings.
- **Destructive grouping**: Close and Reset settings grouped last and separated, per CMP-216, with the confirm behaviour stated (which items confirm and which do not).
- **CMP-216 PanelMenu** spec: trigger button ("Panel options"), the `Shift+F10` and context-menu-key paths, roving focus, type-ahead.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-panel-picker-and-menu.md`; Storybook lists for CMP-213 and CMP-216.

## Out of scope
- The dock move mode the menu launches (E15-D04 owns the mode itself; this ticket owns the menu entry).
- The sync configuration the "Sync group" submenu leads to (E15-D06).
- Floating window chrome (E15-D10).
- Per-panel settings dialogs, which belong to each panel's own epic.
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An unavailable panel explains itself
  Given a panel type that requires a recorded symbol and the current symbol is not recorded
  Then the entry is shown disabled with the reason "Needs a recorded symbol" adjacent to it
  And the reason is part of the entry's accessible name, not a hover-only tooltip

Scenario: The menu is identical across panel types
  Given the context-menu frames for a chart, a DOM ladder and a positions grid
  When their item sets are compared
  Then the item order is identical
  And any item that does not apply is present-but-disabled with a reason rather than absent

Scenario: Search finds nothing
  Given a search term matching no panel type
  Then the no-results frame suggests clearing filters and names the categories that exist
  And the search input retains the term so it can be corrected rather than retyped

Scenario: The menu opens near the viewport edge
  Given a panel docked at the bottom-right corner
  When the context menu and then a submenu open
  Then the overflow frames show the menu and submenu flipping to remain fully visible
  And no item is clipped

Scenario: Float is unavailable in the browser build
  Given the browser (non-Electron) build
  Then the Float item is shown with the browser behaviour and an explanatory note
  And the note states what happens instead (maximised overlay), rather than only that the feature is missing

Scenario: The menu is fully operable from the keyboard
  Given focus inside a panel
  When Shift+F10 is pressed
  Then the menu opens with the first enabled item focused
  And arrow keys, type-ahead, Enter and Esc are all specified with their announcements
```

## Technical notes / design
The picker's growth rule is the most durable part of this ticket. R1 has a handful of panel types; by R4 there will be dozens. Fixing category taxonomy now - Charting, Order flow, Trading, Analysis, System - and stating where new types land means E18..E41 add an entry instead of renegotiating the screen. Write the taxonomy into the spec and into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-024.

Disabled-with-reason is chosen over hidden deliberately. Hiding produces a product that appears smaller than it is and generates support questions; disclosure with a reason teaches the capability model ("this needs recording", "this is owner-only"). The exception, stated in the spec, is anything whose *existence* is sensitive - admin-only objects follow the SCR-155 rule of not disclosing existence - which for panel types means owner-only *panels* are shown, but no owner-only *data* is previewed.

The context menu is built from a static descriptor rather than a per-open API call (SCR-028 performance note, <=80 ms open). That means role and capability gating must be expressible as static predicates over already-loaded state; the spec lists exactly which state each item depends on, so FE does not need a fetch to render the menu.

## Test plan
(1) Cross-type menu comparison for identical ordering. (2) Keyboard-only walkthrough of both surfaces including type-ahead and submenus. (3) Screen-reader pass verifying disabled reasons are announced. (4) Edge-position overflow check at all four corners. (5) Search behaviour check: fuzzy match, no results, filter combination. (6) Contrast and colour-vision checks on chips, disabled states and category headings - disabled must not rely on low contrast alone to signal state. (7) Token audit. (8) SCR-024 and SCR-028 checklist sweep. (9) Handoff dry run rebuilding one picker entry and the menu's disabled state.

## Security notes
The picker reads role and feature flags (`GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags` plus the caller's role) to decide what is offered. The spec must state that this is presentation only: RBAC is enforced server-side per E09, and a panel that is offered-but-unauthorised must fail safely at mount with the SCR-154 permission-denied treatment rather than rendering partial data. Reasons shown on disabled entries must not leak the existence of admin-only resources or account identifiers - "Owner only" is acceptable, naming a specific account is not. "Copy panel link" in SCR-028 produces a deep link; the spec requires that the link encodes workspace and panel identity only, never an account id, key or token, and that opening it on another session re-authorises rather than trusting the link.

## Accessibility notes
The picker is a searchable list with category headings as real headings, each entry's one-line description read together with its name, and the add action announcing the destination ("CVD added to the right column"). Disabled entries are `aria-disabled` and remain focusable so their reason can be read - a non-focusable disabled entry is an entry a screen-reader user cannot learn about. The context menu is a full keyboard menu (CMP-041 based): `Shift+F10` and the context-menu key both open it, roving focus, type-ahead, submenus on Right/Left arrow, Esc closes and restores focus to the panel header. Shortcut hints are text via CMP-022, never images. Disabled state is signalled by more than reduced contrast.

## Performance notes
The menu opens in <=80 ms from a static descriptor with no API call. The picker pre-warms nothing: thumbnails are static assets, and the newly added panel subscribes to its WS topics only after mount, with panel mount held to <=150 ms (CMP-080). The picker's list is virtualised above a stated entry count so that the R4-era catalogue with dozens of entries costs the same as today's.

## Observability
Annotated events: `panel.added{type, placement, entry:"picker"|"menu"|"preset"}`, `panel.picker_searched{hasResults}`, `panel.picker_disabled_entry_focused{type, reason}`, `panel.context_menu_opened{panelType, method}`, and the per-item events inherited from the actions the menu invokes. `panel.picker_disabled_entry_focused` is the signal that tells us which capabilities users want but cannot reach, which is a product input, not just telemetry.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-024 and SCR-028 drawn in both themes with every listed state.
- [ ] Category taxonomy and growth rule written into the spec and into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-024.
- [ ] Full context-menu item set drawn, identical across three panel types, destructive items grouped last.
- [ ] Disabled-with-reason pattern drawn for role, capability and feature-flag cases.
- [ ] Browser-build Float variant drawn with its explanatory note.
- [ ] Corner-overflow frames drawn for menu and submenu.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed; disabled reasons announced.
- [ ] Contrast, colour-vision and token audits clean.
- [ ] Deep-link content rule (no account ids, keys or tokens) stated in the spec.
- [ ] SCR-024 and SCR-028 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-panel-picker-and-menu.md` merged; CMP-213 and CMP-216 Storybook lists agreed with FE.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D02** - wireframes, flows and the hotkey map.
- **E15-D03** - panel chrome and the overflow trigger in CMP-082.
- **E15-D04** - the move mode this menu launches.
- E09 RBAC model for role gating semantics.

## Branch

- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-022, CMP-041, CMP-043, CMP-048, CMP-050, CMP-213, CMP-216, CMP-227
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-005

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-025 workspace settings & SCR-029 unsaved / conflict dialog
body:
## Context
These two dialogs govern the lifecycle of the user's most valuable configuration artefact. SCR-025 holds everything about a workspace that is not its layout - name, description, default symbol and interval, default account scope, density, theme override, open-on-startup, export-as-template and delete. SCR-029 is the guard that stands between the user and losing work: the unsaved-changes prompt and the cross-session conflict resolver.

SCR-029 deserves particular care. US-LAY-002 stores the entire trading setup in a workspace - panes, symbols, intervals, indicators, footprint settings, DOM config, panels and the hotkey profile. A careless Discard wipes hours of arrangement. The catalogue's checklist already fixes the rules: no default destructive button, and Esc maps to Cancel, never to Discard. This ticket draws them and proves them.

The conflict variant matters because workspaces are server-persisted per user and the same user can be open in two sessions (browser plus Electron shell, or two machines over Tailscale). SCR-020 specifies the outcome - "This workspace changed elsewhere. [Keep mine] [Load theirs]" - and SCR-029 adds a side-by-side summary of differences.

Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-025 hi-fi** in both themes: grouped fieldsets (identity, defaults, appearance, startup, danger zone) built from CMP-040 FormField and CMP-065 FormSection, with per-field validation, the error summary at the top with in-page links, and the saving/saved/failed states.
- **Field specification**: name (1-40 chars, unique per user), description, default symbol and interval, default account scope, density (compact/cosy/comfortable), theme override, open-on-startup, export-as-template entry point, delete.
- **Environment pinning**: the "this workspace is pinned to LIVE" warning required by SCR-025's checklist, drawn where it cannot be missed and phrased so the consequence is explicit.
- **Delete flow**: confirm requires typing the workspace name; the last workspace cannot be deleted ("You need at least one workspace.") - both drawn, including the disabled-delete state with its reason.
- **SCR-029 hi-fi, unsaved variant**: `role="alertdialog"`, three explicit verb buttons (Save layout / Discard changes / Cancel), a plain-language summary of what is unsaved (panel count delta, symbols changed, sync groups changed), no default destructive focus, Esc mapped to Cancel.
- **SCR-029 hi-fi, conflict variant**: side-by-side summary of differences (panel count, symbols, sync groups), [Keep mine] / [Load theirs] / Cancel, with a clear statement of what each choice discards and whether the discarded version is recoverable.
- **Entry-point matrix**: every route into SCR-029 - navigating away, switching workspace tab, switching from SCR-011, applying a preset, importing, closing the app - each drawn or explicitly mapped to an existing frame.
- **Autosave decision** from E15-D01 recorded and drawn: if autosave is adopted, the dirty state and manual-save affordance still exist and the spec says what autosave does *not* cover.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-settings-and-conflicts.md`.

## Out of scope
- Workspace import (E15-D09) and export file format.
- The layout surface itself (E15-D03) beyond the dirty marker it displays.
- Account and environment semantics (E27/E28) - this ticket draws the binding control and its warning, not the trading behaviour.
- Global settings (SCR-110+, E45).
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No destructive action is the default
  Given the unsaved-changes dialog and the conflict dialog
  When initial focus is examined
  Then focus rests on the safe action in both
  And neither Discard nor an overwriting choice carries the visual weight of a primary button

Scenario: Esc never destroys work
  Given the unsaved-changes dialog is open
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the specified behaviour is Cancel
  And the spec states that Esc must not map to Discard under any entry point

Scenario: The user can tell what will be lost
  Given a workspace with three added panels, two changed symbols and a new sync group
  Then the dialog summary enumerates those differences in plain sentences
  And the summary is text, not a canvas or an image

Scenario: Two sessions edited the same workspace
  Given the workspace revision changed in another session
  Then the conflict variant shows a side-by-side difference summary
  And each choice states explicitly what it discards and whether that version can be recovered

Scenario: Deleting the last workspace is prevented
  Given the user has exactly one workspace
  When the danger zone is examined
  Then delete is disabled with the reason "You need at least one workspace."
  And the reason is available to a screen reader, not conveyed by dimming alone

Scenario: Workspace name is invalid
  Given a name that is empty, over 40 characters, or duplicates an existing workspace
  Then the field shows an inline error naming the rule
  And the error summary at the top links to the offending field
```

## Technical notes / design
The conflict dialog's honesty requirement drives its design: a user choosing "Load theirs" must know whether their own version survives anywhere. If the implementation keeps the losing version (recommended - store it as an auto-named recovery entry), the copy says so and the dialog stops being frightening; if it does not, the copy must say that too. The spec states which behaviour it assumes and flags it as a requirement on the engineering chunk rather than leaving the copy to be written later.

The difference summary must be computed from the layout tree in terms users recognise - panels, symbols, sync groups - not in terms of the persisted JSON. Specify the exact sentence templates so FE does not improvise, and cap the list length with an "and N more differences" overflow.

Environment pinning is placed in settings but warned about everywhere: a workspace pinned to LIVE changes the meaning of every trading panel inside it, so the warning is specified both in this dialog and as a requirement on the workspace chrome from E15-D03.

Conflict detection compares layout revision ids received over WS and the dialog appears within 300 ms of detection (SCR-029 performance note). The design must therefore tolerate appearing *while the user is mid-action*; specify that it never steals focus from a trading control, and that it queues if an order ticket has focus.

## Test plan
(1) Focus-order and initial-focus verification on both variants. (2) Esc behaviour verification from all entry points in the matrix. (3) Copy review with the Owner for the conflict choices - the test is whether a reader can state what they will lose. (4) Validation-path check for each field rule. (5) Delete-flow test including the last-workspace and type-the-name cases. (6) Screen-reader pass on `alertdialog` semantics and the difference summary. (7) Contrast and colour-vision checks, especially the danger zone which must not rely on red alone. (8) Token audit. (9) SCR-025 and SCR-029 checklist sweep. (10) Handoff dry run rebuilding the danger zone.

## Security notes
The danger zone hosts an irreversible destructive action on server-persisted user data, so the design applies defence in depth: delete is visually separated, requires typing the workspace name, is confirm-gated, and is disabled with a reason when it would leave the user with no workspaces. The environment-pinning control changes which environment a workspace's trading panels address; its warning is mandatory and must not be dismissible-and-forgotten - the spec requires the pinned state to remain visible in the workspace chrome afterwards. Default account scope is selected here: the spec requires the control to show only accounts the caller is actually assigned (server-filtered), to display account labels rather than raw ids, and to state that selection is a preference, with authorisation enforced server-side per E09/E27. Export-as-template is an entry point only; the spec restates US-LAY-007's rule that exports contain no secrets and no account bindings, so a user cannot leak an account reference through a template.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-029 is `role="alertdialog"` with an accessible name, a described-by summary, focus trapped inside, initial focus on the safe action, and focus restored to the trigger on close. All three choices are named with verbs so a screen-reader user hears the consequence, never "OK/Cancel". SCR-025 is a standard modal form: labelled fields, grouped fieldsets, an error summary at the top with in-page links, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` on failing fields, and a save state announced politely. The disabled delete exposes its reason through `aria-describedby` rather than through dimming. The danger zone is identified by heading text as well as colour. Both dialogs are fully operable at 200% zoom with no clipping.

## Performance notes
Saving applies without a full workspace remount - only panels bound to a changed default re-resolve their data (SCR-025) - and the spec says so normatively, since a naive implementation would re-mount every panel and churn GL contexts when the user changes the density. Conflict detection is WS-driven with the dialog appearing within 300 ms of detection. The difference summary is computed once on open, not subscribed.

## Observability
Annotated events: `workspace.updated{fieldsChanged}`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.exported`, `workspace.default_account_changed`, `workspace.environment_pinned{env}`, `layout.conflict_detected{revisionLocal, revisionRemote}` and `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}`. `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}` is the number that tells us whether the conflict copy actually works: a strong skew towards one choice, or a high Cancel rate, means users cannot decide and the dialog needs work.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-025 drawn in both themes with all fieldsets, validation, saving states and the danger zone.
- [ ] LIVE-pinning warning drawn and its persistence into workspace chrome specified.
- [ ] Delete flow drawn including type-the-name confirm and the last-workspace prevention.
- [ ] SCR-029 unsaved and conflict variants drawn; no destructive default; Esc mapped to Cancel from every entry point.
- [ ] Difference-summary sentence templates specified with an overflow rule.
- [ ] Entry-point matrix complete, every route mapped to a frame.
- [ ] Autosave decision recorded and reflected in the dirty-state design.
- [ ] Screen-reader pass on alertdialog semantics and disabled-delete reason.
- [ ] Contrast, colour-vision and token audits clean.
- [ ] SCR-025 and SCR-029 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-settings-and-conflicts.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming story.

- **E15-D03** - the dirty marker and workspace chrome this dialog defends.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-026 workspace import/export, preview and rejection states
body:
## Context
US-LAY-007 lets the Owner export a workspace as a versioned JSON file and lets a manager import it - moving a setup between machines or sharing a working arrangement. It is the only place in E15 where a file crosses a trust boundary, which makes it the only E15 surface with a genuine security design problem: the file is user-supplied, arbitrary-sized, may come from a different app version, and may reference accounts the importer cannot see.

The story's rules are absolute: the export contains **no secrets and no account bindings**; any account-scoped element is dropped on import **with a clear report**; and a file from a newer app version is **refused with the versions stated**, never applied partially. SCR-026's own checklist adds that the import must never carry credentials or account bindings and that this is verified in copy - meaning the design must *tell the user* what travels, not merely arrange for it to be true.

Sprint 05, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07/08 consuming story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Export surface**: entry from SCR-025 and from the workspace menu; a pre-export preview enumerating exactly what is included (panels, symbols, intervals, indicator configs, sync groups, densities) and, as a first-class list, **what is excluded** (accounts, environment binding, credentials, alert bindings, anything account-scoped); the filename convention including the schema version; and the completion state.
- **SCR-026 import hi-fi** in both themes: a file drop zone (CMP-067) with a visible label and a keyboard-operable alternative, plus a file picker path.
- **Diff-style import preview** as a table (never a canvas, per SCR-026's a11y note): panels that will be added, symbols referenced, unknown panel types that will be dropped and why, account references that will be remapped to the importer's default, and a count summary.
- **Validation states**: schema-version mismatch ("This layout was exported by v2 and can't be imported into v1." with both versions named), malformed JSON, oversized file, wrong file type, and a file that validates but would exceed the panel performance budget.
- **Post-import report**: what was applied, what was dropped, what was remapped - persistent enough to be read and copied, not a transient toast.
- **Parse/validation progress** for large files, given parsing happens in a worker with a <=500 ms target for a 2 MB file.
- **Copy set**, reviewed word by word, for the trust claims: what leaves the machine on export and what is ignored on import.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-import-export.md`; Storybook list for CMP-067.

## Out of scope
- The export file schema itself (engineering chunk / `24-internal-schemas.md`); this ticket specifies what the user is told about it.
- Rule import/export (SCR-089, E35/E36) - a sibling surface that should reuse this pattern, noted as a reuse opportunity in the spec.
- Server-side validation logic.
- Sharing workflows beyond file transfer (no link sharing in v1).
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The user learns what travels before exporting
  Given the export preview
  Then the included list and the excluded list are both shown
  And the excluded list names accounts, environment binding and credentials explicitly

Scenario: A newer-version file is refused, not partially applied
  Given a workspace file whose schema version is newer than the app's
  Then the refusal frame names both versions
  And no import option is offered that would apply part of the file

Scenario: Unknown panel types are reported, not silently dropped
  Given a file containing two panel types this build does not know
  Then the preview lists both by their stored type name with the reason "not available in this version"
  And the post-import report repeats the list

Scenario: Account references are remapped and disclosed
  Given a file that references an account the importing user cannot access
  Then the preview shows the reference being dropped or remapped to the importer's default
  And the report states the remapping in plain language, naming no account the importer cannot see

Scenario: The file is malformed or oversized
  Given a file that is not valid JSON, or exceeds the size limit
  Then the rejection frame names the specific problem and the limit
  And the dialog remains open so another file can be chosen without restarting the flow

Scenario: Import is performed without a pointer
  Given keyboard-only operation
  When the import flow is walked from opening the dialog to confirming
  Then every step including file selection has a keyboard path
  And the preview table is navigable as a table with headers
```

## Technical notes / design
The preview is the whole design. An import that just says "Import?" is asking the user to trust an opaque file; a preview that enumerates additions, drops and remappings turns it into an informed decision. Specify the table columns (item, type, action: add/drop/remap, reason) and the ordering rule (drops and remaps first, additions after), so the surprising content is at the top.

The version rule is deliberately strict - refuse rather than degrade. Partial application of a layout produces a workspace the user believes is theirs but is not, which is exactly the class of silent wrongness E15 must avoid. The copy should offer the constructive route ("Export again from the older version", or "update this app") rather than ending at the refusal.

The oversize and budget checks belong to design because they are the user-visible guardrails around R2: a file that would create 30 panels must be caught in the preview with the same measured-frame-cost treatment as US-LAY-001's too-many-panels confirmation, reusing that component rather than inventing a second warning.

## Test plan
(1) Walk every validation state with a crafted fixture set (valid, newer version, older version, malformed, oversized, unknown panel types, unauthorised account reference, 30-panel file). (2) Keyboard-only walkthrough including file selection. (3) Screen-reader pass on the drop zone, the preview table and the report. (4) Copy review with the Security engineer specifically on the trust claims. (5) Contrast and colour-vision checks on the diff table's add/drop/remap indicators, which must not be colour-only. (6) Token audit. (7) SCR-026 checklist sweep. (8) Handoff dry run rebuilding the drop zone and one rejection state.

## Security notes
This is the E15 surface with a real trust boundary, so the design is explicit about all four hazards. **(1) Exfiltration**: the export must never contain API keys, tokens, account ids or environment bindings (US-LAY-007); the design makes this checkable by the user through the excluded-items list, so a mistake in implementation is visible rather than hidden. **(2) Injection through content**: every string from the file - workspace name, panel titles, symbol strings - is untrusted and is specified to be rendered as text with length-capped display in both the preview and the applied workspace; the preview must show the raw value truncated, never interpreted. **(3) Resource abuse**: size and panel-count limits are stated in the design with their user-facing messages, and parsing happens in a worker so a hostile file cannot freeze the UI thread. **(4) Privilege confusion**: an imported workspace must never grant or imply access - account references are dropped or remapped to the importer's own default, environment binding is never imported, and the resulting workspace starts unpinned. The post-import report is the audit trail the user sees; `layout.imported` and `layout.import_rejected{reason}` are recorded. The spec states that none of these client-side guards replace server-side validation of the workspace document on `PUT /workspaces/{workspaceId}`.

## Accessibility notes
The file input has a visible label and the drop zone has a keyboard alternative (a real button), per SCR-026. The diff preview is a semantic table with header cells and a caption stating the counts, so a screen-reader user gets the summary before the detail. Add/drop/remap is conveyed by text in its own column, never by row colour alone. Validation errors are listed as text naming the offending key, associated with the control, and announced. The post-import report is a focusable region that persists, with its content selectable and copyable. Progress during parsing is announced politely with a determinate value where available.

## Performance notes
Parsing and validation run in a worker; a 2 MB layout file validates in <=500 ms without blocking the UI thread (SCR-026). The design supports that with a progress state rather than a frozen dialog. Applying an import reuses the same dock-tree rebuild path as a preset (<=300 ms, reusing panel instances where types match) so importing does not churn GL contexts. Files that would exceed the panel budget are caught in preview with the measured frame cost shown, reusing the US-LAY-001 warning component.

## Observability
Annotated events: `workspace.exported{panelCount, schemaVersion}`, `layout.imported{panelCount, droppedCount, remappedCount, schemaVersion}`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}` where reason is one of `version-newer`, `version-older`, `malformed`, `oversized`, `wrong-type`, `budget-exceeded`. The rejection-reason distribution is the metric that shows whether the version rule is too strict in practice or whether users are mostly hitting malformed files.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Export preview drawn with both an included and an excluded list; excluded list names accounts, environment and credentials.
- [ ] SCR-026 import drawn in both themes: drop zone, picker, preview table, all six validation states, post-import report.
- [ ] Version-mismatch frame names both versions and offers a constructive next step; no partial-apply path exists.
- [ ] Diff indicators are text-plus-icon, not colour-only; contrast and colour-vision checks passed.
- [ ] Keyboard-only walkthrough passed including file selection; preview table navigable with headers.
- [ ] Copy reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer on the trust claims.
- [ ] Untrusted-string rendering rule and size/panel-count limits stated in the spec.
- [ ] SCR-026 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-import-export.md` merged; CMP-067 Storybook list agreed with FE.
- [ ] Reuse note filed for SCR-089 rule import/export.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D02** - the export/import flow diagram.
- **E15-D08** - the export entry point in workspace settings.
- Security engineer review slot for the copy and the trust claims.

## Branch

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-007

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-027 floating panel window (Electron) and its browser fallback
body:
## Context
Floating a panel into its own OS window is the feature that makes a multi-monitor desk work: the DOM ladder on the second screen, the chart on the first. US-LAY-005 specifies it as Electron-only, with the browser build hiding the control and explaining why; SCR-027 adds that a floating window participates in sync groups, carries a mandatory environment badge, remembers its position per workspace, and closes back into its origin dock slot.

The design risk is disclosure. A floating window is a separate document with its own chrome; if it does not repeat the environment, a user can have a LIVE ladder floating on a second monitor while the main window shows DEMO, and place a real order believing it is practice. CMP-215 already requires the environment word in the window *title* so the OS window list and the screen-reader window switcher both disclose it - this ticket designs the visual counterpart and the degraded paths.

Sprint 05, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07/08 consuming story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-027 hi-fi** in both themes: the slim title bar with panel name, symbol, environment badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal), sync-group letter badge, always-on-top control and "return to workspace" / re-dock control.
- **Window title string specification**: the exact composition ("Ladder - BTCUSDT - LIVE"), its truncation rule, and the guarantee that the environment word is never the part truncated away.
- **DEMO and LIVE variants**, with the LIVE treatment carried by more than colour, matching the chrome language established in E15-D03.
- **States**: normal, focused vs unfocused window, always-on-top active, display disconnected (recovered to the primary display next launch), parent-window-closed behaviour, and re-docking in progress.
- **Browser fallback**: the maximised-overlay behaviour that replaces float in the browser build, its explanatory note, and the SCR-028 menu item treatment (drawn in E15-D07, reconciled here) - the control is not silently missing.
- **Multi-monitor placement**: how position and size are remembered per workspace, and what happens on restore when the monitor layout changed.
- **Re-dock affordance**: returning to the origin slot, and the fallback when that slot no longer exists.
- **GPU budget disclosure**: the combined >=58 fps target across at most four GPU-heavy windows, and the shell warning shown beyond it (routing to SCR-046), drawn as a real frame.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-floating-window.md`; Storybook list for CMP-215 (Demo, Live, AlwaysOnTop, plus Unfocused and BrowserFallback).

## Out of scope
- Electron window-management implementation, IPC and process model (E10 / engineering chunk).
- The dock interaction that initiates the float (E15-D04).
- Panel-internal design for whatever is floated.
- Tauri behaviour (spike-gated, E06).
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Environment is disclosed in every floating window
  Given a floating window in LIVE
  When the window is examined with its content cropped away
  Then the environment is readable from the title bar chrome
  And the OS window title string contains the environment word

Scenario: Environment survives title truncation
  Given a long panel name and a narrow window
  When the title is truncated
  Then the environment word remains present
  And the truncation frame demonstrates it

Scenario: The browser build explains the missing capability
  Given the browser (non-Electron) build
  When float is invoked
  Then the maximised-overlay behaviour is shown with a note stating that separate windows require the desktop app
  And the note does not read as an error

Scenario: The monitor a window lived on is gone
  Given a floating window saved on a display that is no longer attached
  When the workspace is restored
  Then the window is placed on the primary display fully on-screen
  And the user is told where it went

Scenario: The parent window closes while panels are floating
  Given two floating windows and the main window being closed
  Then the specified behaviour is drawn (floating windows close with the workspace, after the same unsaved-changes guard)
  And no floating window is left orphaned without a route back

Scenario: Too many GPU-heavy windows are open
  Given five GPU-heavy windows on the reference machine
  Then the warning frame states the measured frame cost and what to close
  And the warning appears in the main window, not only in the window that triggered it
```

## Technical notes / design
The floating window is an independent document, which is easy to forget and expensive to get wrong. Its chrome must be minimal - it exists to give back screen area - yet it must carry four facts at all times: what panel, which symbol, which environment, which sync group. The spec resolves this by giving the title bar a fixed priority order and a truncation rule that sheds panel name before symbol and symbol before environment.

Multi-monitor restore needs a defensive rule, not a best-effort: always clamp the restored rectangle into an attached display's work area, and tell the user when the clamp happened. Silently restoring a window off-screen is indistinguishable from the feature being broken.

The browser fallback should be designed as a *different but complete* behaviour rather than a disabled control. A maximised overlay gives the same benefit on a single screen; the note explains the desktop-only part. That framing also matches US-LAY-005's requirement that the control is hidden in the browser build with an explanation.

Each floating window is a separate renderer with its own GL context, so the window count is a performance decision the user is making without knowing it. Drawing the budget warning makes the cost visible at the moment it is incurred.

## Test plan
(1) Crop test: each window variant cropped to its title bar must disclose panel, symbol and environment. (2) Truncation sweep at four window widths. (3) Multi-monitor scenario walkthrough: same layout, fewer displays, different scaling. (4) Parent-close scenario. (5) Keyboard walkthrough: float, move focus between windows, re-dock - all without a pointer. (6) Screen-reader pass on window titles and the per-window skip link. (7) Contrast and colour-vision checks on the environment badge over the title bar in both themes. (8) SCR-027 checklist sweep. (9) Handoff dry run rebuilding the title bar.

## Security notes
This surface exists to be looked at out of the corner of an eye on a second monitor, which is precisely when environment confusion causes a real loss. The design therefore treats the environment disclosure as a hard requirement with three independent carriers: the OS window title string (so it appears in the task switcher and to assistive technology), the visible badge in the window chrome, and the non-colour treatment of the LIVE variant. The spec forbids any state in which a floating window renders trading controls without a visible environment - including the unfocused window state, where chrome is often dimmed and must not be dimmed below the contrast floor. A floating window inherits the session and is subject to the same RBAC as the main window; the spec states that popping out never elevates capability and that a viewer's floating panel remains read-only in its own chrome. Deep links or window handles must not embed account ids or tokens, consistent with the E15-D07 rule for "Copy panel link".

## Accessibility notes
Each floating window is an independent document with its own title, skip link and focus scope (SCR-027). The window title names panel, symbol and environment. Moving focus between windows is OS-standard and is not intercepted. The re-dock and close controls are named buttons, not icon-only glyphs without labels. The always-on-top state is exposed as a pressed toggle, not as a visual-only cue. The unfocused-window treatment must keep text at >=4.5:1 and UI elements at >=3:1 - a common failure where inactive chrome is dimmed into non-compliance. The browser-fallback overlay traps focus correctly, announces itself, and is dismissible with Esc back to the docked state.

## Performance notes
Each floating window is a separate renderer process with its own GL context; the combined target is >=58 fps across at most four GPU-heavy windows on the reference machine, beyond which the shell warns (SCR-027, routing to SCR-046). The spec makes the window chrome static - no per-frame work, no animated badges - so a floating window costs its panel and nothing more. The re-dock path reuses the panel instance rather than remounting it, avoiding GL context churn.

## Observability
Annotated events: `panel.floated{panelType, display}`, `panel.redocked{originSlotExists}`, `window.opened`, `window.closed`, `window.restored_clamped{fromDisplay}` and `window.gpu_budget_warned{windowCount, measuredFrameMs}`. The clamped-restore and budget-warning events are the ones that reveal whether the multi-monitor and GPU assumptions hold on the Owner's actual hardware.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-027 drawn in both themes with all listed states, DEMO and LIVE variants.
- [ ] Window title composition and truncation rule specified; environment proven never to truncate away.
- [ ] Multi-monitor save/restore and the clamped-restore disclosure drawn.
- [ ] Parent-window-closed behaviour drawn with the unsaved-changes guard.
- [ ] Browser fallback drawn as a complete alternative behaviour with its note.
- [ ] GPU budget warning frame drawn with measured frame cost and remediation.
- [ ] Unfocused-window contrast verified to remain compliant.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed across windows.
- [ ] SCR-027 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-floating-window.md` merged; CMP-215 Storybook list agreed with FE.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the consuming story.

- **E15-D04** - the float operation and its dock-side behaviour.
- **E15-D03** - environment chrome language and panel header priority order.
- E10 Electron shell design for window chrome conventions and SCR-046's warning surface.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-049 multi-chart grid panel - cells, per-cell header, maximise
body:
## Context
SCR-049 is a second, panel-internal grid: two to nine chart instances inside one dock slot, sharing a header, used for multi-timeframe and multi-symbol context. It is easy to confuse with the workspace dock grid, and that confusion is the main design problem - a user must be able to tell at a glance whether they are looking at four docked chart panels or one multi-chart panel containing four cells, because the operations available differ (a dock panel can be floated; a cell cannot).

It is also the densest surface in E15 from a rendering perspective: one shared WebGL context with scissored viewports, a total budget of >=50 fps for four charts. The design must actively help that budget - per-cell chrome is repeated up to nine times, so every pixel and every DOM node in a cell header is multiplied.

Sprint 05, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07 consuming story (US-LAY-001 / US-LAY-003 / US-CHART-011).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-049 hi-fi** in both themes and all three densities: the shared panel header (grid selector, sync group, "propagate symbol" toggle) plus the cell matrix.
- **Grid arrangements** drawn: 1x2, 2x2, 3x3, 1+3 and a custom arrangement, per SCR-049's checklist, with the arrangement control and how a custom grid is expressed.
- **Per-cell header**: symbol, interval, sync-group letter tag, and a minimal action affordance - specified at minimum viable size, with an explicit progressive-disclosure order for narrow cells (the 3x3 case at 1280x800 is the hostile case and must be drawn).
- **Active-cell indication**: which cell has focus, using a non-colour channel, drawn so it is distinguishable from the *panel*-level focus affordance established in E15-D03.
- **Maximise-cell and restore**: the interaction, the chrome shown while maximised, and the exact restore to the prior arrangement.
- **Cell rebinding**: changing a cell's symbol or interval, the "propagate symbol" toggle's effect, and how that interacts with the workspace-level sync groups from E15-D06 - the precedence rule must be stated, not left ambiguous.
- **Degraded state**: the frame shown when the grid exceeds the GPU budget, with the explicit reduce-quality prompt required by SCR-049's checklist, stating the measured cost.
- **Empty and loading cells**: a cell with no symbol bound, a cell loading, and a cell whose symbol is unavailable (delisted) - the last mirroring US-LAY-002's partial-restore rule so one bad cell does not blank the grid.
- **Visual distinction** from the dock grid: the specific cue (gutter treatment, header weight, or frame style) that tells the user this is one panel, documented as a rule.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-multichart-grid.md`; Storybook additions for CMP-196-adjacent visuals and the grid header.

## Out of scope
- The chart rendering itself (E11/E12).
- The sync engine (CMP-196, non-visual) and the sync configuration UI (E15-D06) - referenced, not redefined.
- Workspace-level docking (E15-D04).
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A multi-chart panel is distinguishable from four docked panels
  Given a 2x2 multi-chart panel and a 2x2 dock layout side by side
  When a reviewer is shown both without labels
  Then the documented distinguishing cue makes the difference identifiable
  And the cue is present in all three densities

Scenario: The densest arrangement remains legible at the minimum width
  Given a 3x3 grid at 1280x800 in compact density
  Then every cell still shows its symbol and interval or the documented fallback
  And no cell header overlaps or clips

Scenario: Active cell is identifiable without colour
  Given the focused-cell frame in greyscale and under colour-vision simulation
  Then the focused cell is identifiable by a non-hue channel
  And it is not confusable with the panel-level focus affordance

Scenario: Sync precedence is unambiguous
  Given a multi-chart panel whose cells are in workspace sync group A and whose "propagate symbol" toggle is on
  Then the spec states which wins and the frame shows the resulting state
  And the header discloses the effective behaviour in words

Scenario: One cell's symbol is unavailable
  Given a saved grid where one cell references a delisted symbol
  Then that cell renders an explicit error state naming the symbol
  And the other cells render normally

Scenario: The grid exceeds the GPU budget
  Given a 3x3 grid of order-flow charts on the reference machine
  Then the degraded frame states the measured frame cost and offers a reduce-quality action
  And the action names what it will reduce
```

## Technical notes / design
Cell chrome is multiplied by up to nine, so the design budget is stated per cell in pixels and in DOM nodes, and the spec recommends rendering cell headers as a single chrome layer rather than nine independent React subtrees where possible. This is a design decision with an engineering consequence, so it is written as a recommendation with the rationale, and the FE lead signs it off during handoff.

The sync precedence rule is the sharpest correctness question here: a cell can be governed by the panel's propagate-symbol toggle *and* by a workspace sync group at once. The recommended and defensible rule is that the workspace group is authoritative and the propagate toggle applies only within the panel to cells not in a group, with the header disclosing the effective behaviour in a short sentence. Whatever is chosen, it must be a single sentence a user can remember.

Maximise-cell must restore exactly, including per-cell scroll position and scale, because it is used as a quick-look gesture dozens of times an hour; an imperfect restore turns a glance into a re-setup.

Degraded mode here should reuse the SCR-153 language and CMP-092/CMP-227 treatments rather than inventing a grid-specific dialect, so a user meets one vocabulary for reduced capability across the product.

## Test plan
(1) Blind distinguishability check between dock grid and multi-chart grid. (2) 3x3 at 1280x800 compact legibility sweep. (3) Colour-vision and greyscale checks on active-cell indication. (4) Sync precedence walkthrough with the E15-D06 author to confirm consistency. (5) Maximise/restore fidelity check including scroll and scale. (6) Error, empty and loading cell states walked. (7) Degraded-state copy consistency check against SCR-153. (8) Keyboard walkthrough: `Ctrl+Alt+1..9` cell focus, maximise, restore. (9) SCR-049 checklist sweep. (10) Handoff dry run rebuilding a cell header.

## Security notes
A multi-chart grid can show several symbols at once, and where chart trading is enabled (E31) a cell becomes order-capable. The spec therefore requires each order-capable cell to disclose the environment within the cell itself, not only in the panel header - the same rule E15-D03 applies to panels, applied one level down, because a maximised or glanced-at cell must not be ambiguous. Symbol strings rendered in cell headers come from user-saved workspace documents and imported files, so they are treated as untrusted text with capped display length, consistent with E15-D09. No account or credential data appears on this surface.

## Accessibility notes
Each sub-chart is a labelled region whose accessible name includes symbol and interval; `Ctrl+Alt+1..9` focuses a sub-chart (SCR-049) and the focus move is announced. The active cell's indication is non-colour and meets 3:1 against every chart background. Sync-group tags are letters with word-based accessible names, consistent with E15-D06. Maximise and restore are announced ("BTCUSDT 4 hour maximised", "Grid restored, four cells"). At the 3x3 minimum-width case, if a cell header must drop the interval visually, the accessible name retains it - the screen-reader experience must not degrade with pixel width. All cell headers remain operable at 200% zoom, with the documented fallback arrangement if they cannot.

## Performance notes
The governing budget is SCR-049's one shared WebGL context with scissored viewports and >=50 fps total for four charts, inside US-LAY-001's >=55 fps four-pane target. Design constraints written normatively: cell chrome is static and must not repaint on chart frames; the active-cell indicator draws inside the cell's existing box so focusing a cell never resizes a viewport; grid arrangement changes re-scissor rather than recreate contexts; and the degraded prompt names the specific reductions (fewer cells, lower cadence, reduced heatmap depth) rather than offering a vague "reduce quality".

## Observability
Annotated events: `multichart.grid_changed{arrangement}`, `multichart.cell_symbol_changed{cellIndex}`, `multichart.sync_group_changed`, `multichart.cell_maximised{cellIndex}`, plus `multichart.degraded_prompt_shown{cells, measuredFrameMs}` added here. The last one is the evidence for whether nine cells is a real capability or a theoretical one on the Owner's hardware.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five arrangements drawn in both themes and three densities, including 3x3 at 1280x800 compact.
- [ ] Per-cell header specified with progressive-disclosure order and a per-cell chrome budget.
- [ ] Active-cell indication drawn, non-colour, distinct from panel-level focus.
- [ ] Maximise/restore drawn with exact-restore requirement stated.
- [ ] Sync precedence rule written as a single sentence and disclosed in the header.
- [ ] Empty, loading and unavailable-symbol cell states drawn.
- [ ] Degraded frame drawn reusing SCR-153 vocabulary with measured cost and named reductions.
- [ ] Dock-grid vs multi-chart distinguishing cue documented and blind-checked.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed.
- [ ] SCR-049 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-multichart-grid.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D03** - panel chrome and focus language.
- **E15-D06** - sync groups and badge language, and the precedence rule's other half.
- E11/E12 engine capabilities for scissored viewports (consult, not blocking).

title: Hi-fi design: responsive & reduced-capability layout (SCR-153, SCR-150 restore)
body:
## Context
US-LAY-008 requires the layout to adapt to a small screen and a weak GPU: under 1280 px wide, panels collapse into a tabbed arrangement with **no loss of function**; when the measured frame time indicates a weak GPU, the app suggests a reduced profile (lower heatmap depth, 200 ms cadence, fewer panes) and applies it on acceptance; and the user can restore the full profile, with the choice remembered per device and the measured frame cost shown. Crucially, capability detection is based on measured frame time, never on user-agent strings - a design constraint as much as an engineering one, because it decides what the UI can honestly claim.

This ticket also covers SCR-150, the boot/restore experience, because it is where US-LAY-002's "<=3 s to interactive for a four-pane workspace" promise is either kept or visibly broken, and where progressive loading is either designed or improvised.

Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07/08 consuming story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Narrow-viewport layout** (<1280 px): the tabbed collapse rule - which panels group into which tabs, how the active tab is chosen, how a user reaches every panel, and proof that no function is lost (a function-parity table: every control available at full width, and where it lives when narrow).
- **Breakpoint set** for the workspace surface with the behaviour at each, plus the 1280x800 baseline already fixed in E15-D03.
- **SCR-153 degraded-mode hi-fi** for the E15-relevant causes: GPU budget exceeded and reduced-profile active, using CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner, CMP-028 Callout, CMP-069 InfoPanel and CMP-227 EstimatedBadge. Each variant states precisely what still works and what does not.
- **Reduced-profile proposal dialog**: what triggers it (measured frame time threshold, stated numerically), what it will change (heatmap depth, update cadence to 200 ms, pane count), the accept and decline paths, and the "don't ask again on this device" behaviour.
- **Manual controls**: reduce-quality and restore-full-profile affordances with the measured frame cost displayed, and per-device persistence disclosed to the user ("remembered for this device").
- **SCR-150 boot/restore**: the skeleton for a restoring workspace showing panel frames before data, the progressive-fill order (which panel becomes interactive first and why), a slow-restore state when the 3 s budget is missed, and the partial-failure state where one pane fails (delisted symbol per US-LAY-002) while the rest loads.
- **Copy set** for degradation that avoids both alarm and vagueness - naming the capability affected, not the subsystem.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-responsive-and-degraded.md`; Storybook list additions for CMP-092.

## Out of scope
- Non-E15 degradation causes (exchange WS down, recorder down, rule engine down) - owned by E08/E16/E35, though the visual language must be shared and is referenced here.
- The measurement implementation (engineering chunk) - this ticket specifies what is measured and how it is disclosed.
- Mobile/tablet layouts - out of scope for the product (web app on desktop; Android out of scope per the owner decision).
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No function is lost at narrow width
  Given the function-parity table
  When every control available at 1920 px is looked up in the narrow layout
  Then each has a stated location or a documented equivalent
  And any control that genuinely cannot be offered is listed explicitly with the reason

Scenario: The reduced profile is proposed, never imposed silently
  Given measured frame time crosses the stated threshold
  Then the proposal frame names the measured value, what will change, and offers accept and decline
  And if the user declines, the app continues at full profile with the cost still visible

Scenario: Degradation is disclosed, never silent
  Given the reduced profile is active
  Then the banner states which capabilities are reduced and which are unaffected
  And per-panel badges repeat the specific reduction in their accessible name

Scenario: The choice is remembered per device
  Given a user accepted the reduced profile on a laptop
  When the same user opens the workspace on the reference desktop
  Then the desktop is at full profile
  And the spec states that the preference is device-scoped, and where the user can see and change it

Scenario: Workspace restore exceeds its budget
  Given a four-pane workspace that has not become interactive within 3 seconds
  Then the slow-restore frame explains what is still loading and what is already usable
  And nothing implies the app has frozen

Scenario: One pane cannot restore
  Given a saved pane referencing a delisted symbol
  Then that pane shows an explicit error naming the symbol with a recovery action
  And the other panes are fully interactive
```

## Technical notes / design
"No loss of function" is a testable claim only if it is enumerated, which is why the function-parity table is a deliverable rather than a statement. Build it from the full-width control inventory in E15-D03 and E15-D07.

Capability detection based on measured frame time means the UI is making a claim about the user's machine; the copy must therefore show the measurement rather than assert a verdict. "Your last minute averaged 34 fps" is honest and actionable; "Your GPU is weak" is neither, and it is wrong the moment the user closes a video call.

The reduced profile must be reversible in one step and must never silently re-apply itself after being declined within the same session - a suggestion that keeps returning is a dialog the user learns to dismiss without reading, which defeats the disclosure requirement.

SCR-150's progressive-fill order is a product decision: the recommended order is shell, then the focused chart, then remaining charts, then order-flow panels, then auxiliary panels, so the first thing usable is the thing being looked at. State it, because otherwise load order will follow whatever the data layer resolves first.

## Test plan
(1) Function-parity audit against the full-width control inventory. (2) Breakpoint sweep at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1100 and 1024 px, checking overlap, clipping and reachability. (3) Copy review of every degraded variant for the "what still works" statement. (4) Screen-reader pass on the `role="status"` banner and per-panel badges. (5) Contrast checks at reduced-profile visual settings, since reduced heatmap depth changes the background against which chrome is read. (6) Restore-sequence walkthrough including slow and partial-failure states. (7) Keyboard reachability of every panel in the tabbed narrow layout. (8) SCR-153 and SCR-150 checklist sweep. (9) Handoff dry run rebuilding the banner and the proposal dialog.

## Security notes
Degradation must never quietly reduce a safety-relevant disclosure. The spec states explicitly that the reduced profile may shed heatmap depth, update cadence and pane count, but may never shed the environment badge, the armed/disarmed state of trading controls, the position and order display, or any error state - SCR-153's own rule is that trading remains possible or is explicitly blocked, never ambiguous. In the narrow tabbed layout, a panel that is in a background tab must not be treated as "handled": any alert, error or fill notification from a hidden panel must surface in the visible chrome, otherwise collapsing the layout creates a silent-failure channel. The per-device preference is stored locally and holds no credentials; the spec notes it is a preference, not a permission, and must not be usable to bypass any server-enforced limit.

## Accessibility notes
The degraded banner is `role="status"` naming exactly which capability is degraded and what still works, in plain sentences (SCR-153); per-panel badges repeat the specific degradation in their accessible name. The narrow tabbed layout is a proper tablist with arrow-key navigation, and each tab's accessible name states the panel and any pending condition ("Positions, 1 alert"). Reduced-profile settings must not reduce contrast below the standard - a lower-depth heatmap changes the backdrop, so contrast is re-measured under reduced settings rather than assumed. The restore sequence announces progress politely and announces when the workspace becomes interactive, so a screen-reader user is not left guessing during a 3 s load. All of this is checked again in E15-D15.

## Performance notes
This ticket is where E15's performance budgets become user-visible: US-LAY-001's >=55 fps with four order-flow panes, US-LAY-002's <=3 s four-pane restore, the 200 ms reduced cadence, and SCR-049's grid budget. The spec defines the measured-frame-time threshold that triggers the proposal, the averaging window (long enough not to fire on a single stall), and the hysteresis that prevents the app from oscillating between profiles. It also states that the reduced profile sheds optional work only - per SCR-153, order entry and position display keep their full budget.

## Observability
Annotated events: `degraded.entered{cause, sheddedFeatures}`, `degraded.exited{durationMs}`, `profile.reduced_proposed{measuredFrameMs}`, `profile.reduced_accepted`, `profile.reduced_declined`, `profile.restored_full`, `layout.narrow_collapsed{width}`, `workspace.restore_completed{ms, paneCount, failedPanes}`. `workspace.restore_completed` is the direct measurement of the US-LAY-002 promise and should be surfaced on the owner-facing observability dashboard (E04/OBS).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Narrow-viewport tabbed layout drawn with a completed function-parity table.
- [ ] Breakpoint set defined with behaviour at each; sweep passed with no overlap or clipping.
- [ ] SCR-153 variants for GPU-budget and reduced-profile drawn with what-still-works statements.
- [ ] Reduced-profile proposal drawn with measured value, named changes, accept/decline and no-nagging rule.
- [ ] Manual reduce/restore controls drawn with measured frame cost and per-device disclosure.
- [ ] SCR-150 restore skeleton, progressive-fill order, slow-restore and partial-failure states drawn.
- [ ] Safety-disclosure exclusion list (never shed) written into the spec.
- [ ] Hidden-tab notification surfacing rule specified.
- [ ] Contrast re-measured under reduced-profile visual settings.
- [ ] SCR-153 and SCR-150 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-responsive-and-degraded.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D03** - the full-width control inventory the parity table is built from.
- E08's connection/degradation visual language (shared SCR-152/SCR-153 vocabulary) for consistency.
- E11 engine measurement capability (consult on the frame-time metric available).

## Branch
`design/e15-responsive-degraded-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-150, SCR-153
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-028, CMP-069, CMP-083, CMP-092, CMP-214..216, CMP-227
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-002, US-LAY-008, US-DOM-005, US-SET-008
