title: Design-system contribution: layout tokens, dock primitives, catalogue entries
body:
## Context
E15 introduces the chrome that every future panel in the product will live inside, which means its tokens and components are not epic-local - they are the substrate for E18 footprint panels, E21 DOM panels, E30 order tickets, E39 journal panels and everything after. If those tokens are invented inside E15's hi-fi files and never promoted, each later epic will re-derive its own panel border, its own focus ring, its own gutter, and the terminal will drift into inconsistency by R3.

This ticket promotes E15's design decisions into the design system properly: named tokens with a rationale, updated component-catalogue entries, Storybook contracts, and documented usage rules. It is scheduled after the core hi-fi tickets (E15-D03, D04, D06) so it promotes decisions that have actually been tested, not proposals.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Token additions/confirmations** in `16-design-system-brief.md` and the token source, each with a stated purpose and usage rule:
  - `space.dockgrid.gutter` (referenced by CMP-081) per density.
  - `space.panelheader.*` (referenced by CMP-082) per density.
  - `color.border.panel`, `elevation.2`, `radius.md` usage in the dock context (confirmations, with the dock-specific rule).
  - `color.sync.*` - the full group palette from E15-D06 with its contrast evidence and the letter-redundancy rule attached to the token, so no consumer can use the colour alone.
  - `color.accent.subtle` usage for drop zones (CMP-214) with the contrast floor against arbitrary panel content.
  - `color.env.*` usage in floating-window chrome (CMP-215) including the unfocused-window contrast floor.
  - A **focus-affordance token set** for the inset panel focus treatment from E15-D03, with the normative rule that it must not change the content box.
- **Component-catalogue updates** in `15-component-catalogue.md` for CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-083, CMP-213, CMP-214, CMP-215, CMP-216, CMP-217, CMP-218 - props reconciled with the final designs, a11y contracts sharpened where the hi-fi work found gaps, Storybook story lists aligned with what was agreed per hi-fi ticket, and test expectations (unit/visual/axe/interaction/perf) stated.
- **New entries if required**: if E15's designs need a primitive that does not exist (for example a shared "panel-chrome badge" used by sync, environment and recording state), it is proposed here as a first-class catalogue entry with an ID allocated in the correct band, never as a one-off.
- **Usage rules document** in `docs/design/specs/e15-design-system-contributions.md`: how a future panel epic adopts panel chrome - what it must use, what it may override, and what it must never restyle (focus affordance, environment disclosure, sync badge).
- **Density specification** for the dock surface: the concrete values for compact/cosy/comfortable across gutter, header height, badge size and splitter thickness, with the 1280x800 compact case proven.
- **Deprecation/conflict pass**: any existing token or component E15 duplicates is identified and either reused or explicitly superseded with a migration note.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of the tokens in code (engineering chunk; this ticket delivers the specification and the catalogue edits).
- Motion tokens (E15-D14 defines them; this ticket only reserves their names).
- Tokens owned by other epics (chart palette E11/E12, order-flow colours E18..E25).
- Rebuilding E05's design system v0 foundations.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every value in E15's hi-fi files resolves to a token
  Given the E15 hi-fi files after this ticket
  When a token audit is run across SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-150 and SCR-153
  Then no raw hex, px or ms value remains outside the token layer
  And any exception is listed with a written justification

Scenario: Sync colours cannot be used without their letter
  Given the color.sync.* token documentation
  Then the usage rule states that group colour must always be paired with the group letter
  And the catalogue entry for CMP-218 and CMP-082 repeats the rule

Scenario: A future epic can adopt panel chrome without a designer
  Given the usage rules document
  When an engineer from a later epic follows it to add a new panel type
  Then the required chrome, the permitted overrides and the forbidden restyles are unambiguous
  And the dry run with an engineer from another epic confirms it

Scenario: A duplicated primitive is found
  Given an existing design-system component that overlaps something E15 designed
  Then the overlap is resolved by reuse or by an explicit supersession note with a migration path
  And no two components ship with the same responsibility

Scenario: Density values fail at the minimum width
  Given the compact density values applied at 1280x800 with four panels
  When the layout is measured
  Then the chrome budget from E15-D03 is met
  And if it is not, the density values are revised before sign-off rather than the budget
```

## Technical notes / design
The highest-leverage item is the **usage rules document**, because E15's chrome will be adopted by a dozen later epics with no E15 designer present. It should be written as rules with reasons, not as a style listing: "never restyle the panel focus affordance - it is inset specifically so that focusing a panel does not resize a WebGL canvas" travels much further than a colour swatch.

Token naming follows the existing brief's conventions; resist creating an `e15.*` namespace, since these tokens are product-wide chrome, not epic-local. Where a token is genuinely dock-specific (`space.dockgrid.gutter`), the name already says so.

The contrast floors for drop zones and sync badges are unusual in that the background is arbitrary - it is whatever panel content sits underneath. The token documentation must therefore record the measurement method (against the darkest and lightest hosted content in the product, including a dense footprint), not just a passing value, so a later epic introducing a new panel background knows what to re-check.

## Test plan
(1) Token audit across every E15 hi-fi file. (2) Contrast verification for each new token against the documented background extremes. (3) Colour-vision simulation across the sync palette. (4) Density value verification at 1280x800 compact against the E15-D03 chrome budget. (5) Catalogue diff review with the design-system team and the FE lead. (6) Adoption dry run: an engineer from another epic adds a hypothetical panel using only the usage rules. (7) Duplication sweep across the existing catalogue.

## Security notes
Two tokens carry safety meaning and are documented as such. `color.env.*` is the environment disclosure used across the workspace, floating windows and order-capable panels; its usage rule states that it must never be the sole carrier of environment meaning (text is mandatory), must meet contrast in both focused and unfocused chrome, and must not be redefined by any consuming epic. The sync palette's letter-redundancy rule exists for the same reason: a colour-only group indicator can mislead a user about which panes share a symbol. Recording these as token-level rules rather than as screen-level notes means a later epic cannot quietly drop them.

## Accessibility notes
Each catalogue entry updated here carries an explicit a11y contract - role, keyboard model, announcement text, focus behaviour - and each states its axe and interaction-test expectations. The mandatory keyboard equivalent for CMP-214 is written into the component contract, not left in a screen spec, so it cannot be lost when the component is reused. Focus-affordance tokens include the visible-focus requirement against both themes and the >=3:1 contrast floor. Target-size rules (>=24 px for splitters and panel controls) are recorded on CMP-083 and CMP-082 rather than only in SCR-021.

## Performance notes
The token set encodes performance-protecting decisions so they survive reuse: the inset focus affordance (no content-box change, therefore no canvas resize on focus), static chrome (no per-frame repaint), and drop-zone styling that is transform/opacity-only. Each is written as a usage rule with the budget it protects named (>=55 fps with four order-flow panes, <=200 ms layout transition, <=150 ms panel mount).

## Observability
Not an instrumented surface. The ticket does, however, consolidate the E15 analytics event names agreed across D03..D12 into one table in the contributions document, so that later epics adding panels emit `panel.added`, `panel.removed` and `panel.context_menu_opened` with consistent properties rather than inventing per-panel variants.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All listed tokens added or confirmed with purpose, usage rule and contrast evidence.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated for CMP-073, CMP-080..083, CMP-213..218 with reconciled props, a11y contracts, Storybook lists and test expectations.
- [ ] Any new primitive proposed with a correctly banded ID and a full entry.
- [ ] Density values specified for all three modes and verified at 1280x800 compact against the chrome budget.
- [ ] Usage rules document merged; adoption dry run with an engineer from another epic passed.
- [ ] Token audit across all E15 hi-fi files clean.
- [ ] Duplication sweep complete; overlaps reused or superseded with a migration note.
- [ ] Safety rules (env disclosure, sync letter redundancy) recorded at token and component level.
- [ ] Design-system team review recorded.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, ahead of the Sprint 07 consuming work.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D03**, **E15-D04**, **E15-D06** - the tested decisions being promoted.
- E05 design system v0 as the base.
- Design-system team review capacity in Sprint 05.

## Branch
`design/e15-design-system-contributions`

title: Motion spec: docking, layout transitions, workspace switching and reduced motion
body:
## Context
Motion in a trading terminal has one job: explain what just happened to the layout, without costing a frame of the chart. A panel that teleports across the screen leaves the user re-orienting; a panel that glides for 400 ms while a footprint chart stutters is worse. E15 has a lot of motion candidates - drag previews, drop commits, splitter resizes, preset application, tab switching, panel add/remove, float and re-dock, maximise and restore, dialog entry - and the specification's main value is deciding which of them move at all.

The constraint that governs everything: layout motion must never animate anything that forces a WebGL canvas resize per frame. Animating a panel's width means resizing its GL viewport sixty times a second, which is the single most reliable way to break US-LAY-001's >=55 fps four-pane target.

Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion inventory** for E15: every candidate transition listed with a verdict - animate, instant, or crossfade-only - and the reason.
- **Token-level specification** for those that animate: duration, easing, and the design-system motion token they use (`motion.fast` and siblings), with values consistent with `16-design-system-brief.md` rather than invented.
- **Drag and drop**: drag-preview follow behaviour (transform-only), drop-zone highlight fade-in/out, and the drop commit - specified as an **instant** layout mutation with, at most, a brief settle on the arriving panel's chrome, never an animated resize of the surrounding panels.
- **Splitter resize**: live, unanimated, throttled to one layout write per animation frame; the keyboard-resize step specified with its own feedback.
- **Preset application and layout change**: the transition between two dock trees, specified to reuse panel instances and to avoid any per-frame canvas resize; whether a crossfade is used and over what duration.
- **Workspace tab switching**: how the outgoing workspace leaves and the incoming one appears, with lazy-mount and the 30 s unsubscribe rule visible in the sequence.
- **Panel add/remove**, **maximise/restore**, **float/re-dock**: each with a verdict and, where animated, a specification.
- **Dialog and menu motion**: SCR-022, SCR-023, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-026, SCR-028, SCR-029 entry/exit consistent with the design system, with the alertdialog specified to appear without a delay that could be mistaken for lag.
- **Reduced-motion specification**: the complete `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for every item in the inventory - what becomes instant, what keeps a minimal opacity change, and the guarantee that no information is conveyed only by motion.
- **Prototype**: a short motion prototype for the three most consequential transitions (drop commit, preset application, workspace switch) reviewed against a live chart to confirm they do not read as stutter.
- Spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-motion.md`.

## Out of scope
- Chart-internal motion (E11/E12 - pan, zoom, transitions of data).
- Drawing tool motion (E14).
- Loading skeleton shimmer beyond stating whether it exists (E15-D12 owns the restore sequence's content).
- Implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No transition resizes a canvas per frame
  Given the motion inventory
  When each animated item is checked for whether it changes a panel's content box over time
  Then no animated item does so
  And any transition that would is specified as instant with its reason recorded

Scenario: Reduced motion loses no information
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled
  When every item in the inventory is walked
  Then each has a defined non-animated behaviour
  And every piece of information previously conveyed by movement is conveyed by text, position or an announcement instead

Scenario: Motion does not delay a trading action
  Given the dialog and menu specifications
  Then no transition on the path to an order-capable surface exceeds the design system's fast duration
  And the panel context menu opens within its 80 ms budget including any motion

Scenario: The drop commit reads as a single change
  Given the motion prototype for a drop commit
  When it is reviewed alongside a live four-pane chart workspace
  Then the layout changes once, with no intermediate reflow visible
  And no frame drop is observed on the reference machine during the transition

Scenario: A transition is proposed that cannot meet the budget
  Given a candidate transition that would require animating panel widths
  Then it is rejected in the inventory with the budget it would breach named
  And an alternative (instant change plus a settle on chrome only) is specified
```

## Technical notes / design
The inventory-with-verdicts format matters more than the easing curves. Most layout motion in trading terminals should not exist; writing down "instant, because animating this resizes a GL viewport" prevents a well-meaning implementation from adding it later.

Where motion survives, it should be on chrome, not on content: a drop zone can fade, a panel header can settle, a tab indicator can slide - none of those touch a canvas. This is the rule the spec states, and every animated item must satisfy it.

The workspace switch is the one place a crossfade genuinely helps, because the whole surface changes and an instant swap is disorienting. Even there, specify a short opacity transition on a static snapshot rather than on live panels, and state that panels mount lazily behind it.

Reduced motion is specified exhaustively rather than as "disable animations", because some of E15's motion carries meaning - the drop preview, for instance. Under reduced motion the preview must still appear, just without the transition, so the user does not lose the information.

## Test plan
(1) Inventory review with the FE lead, verdict by verdict. (2) Prototype review of the three key transitions against a live chart on the reference machine, watching the frame graph. (3) Reduced-motion walkthrough of every inventory item. (4) Vestibular-safety review: no large-area parallax, no rapid scaling, no flashing above the standard's threshold. (5) Timing check against the SCR-028 80 ms menu budget and the SCR-022 300 ms preset budget. (6) Token audit - durations and easings come from motion tokens. (7) Handoff review with FE confirming each verdict is implementable as specified.

## Security notes
Motion must never delay or obscure a safety-relevant disclosure. The spec states that environment badges, armed-state indicators, error states and the unsaved/conflict alertdialog appear without an entry animation that could hide them during the moment a user acts. It also forbids motion that could mask a change of state on an order-capable panel - for example animating a panel into a position while its environment badge fades in separately, which would create a window in which the panel renders trading controls with no visible environment.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured exhaustively, with a defined behaviour per item rather than a blanket disable, and with the guarantee that no information is motion-only. Nothing flashes more than three times per second. No transition moves a large area of the viewport in a way associated with vestibular discomfort. Focus is never animated away from where the user put it - after a drop or a preset application, focus lands deterministically and is announced ("Layout changed to 2 by 2"), with the announcement independent of whether the motion ran. Menu and dialog motion never delays focus entry.

## Performance notes
Every animated property is restricted to `transform` and `opacity`. No animated item changes a panel's content box. Splitter dragging throttles to one layout write per animation frame. The preset transition stays inside SCR-022's <=300 ms rebuild and reuses panel instances. The context menu stays inside SCR-028's <=80 ms open. The governing budgets - >=55 fps with four order-flow panes, <=200 ms layout transition, <=150 ms panel mount - are named in the spec against each relevant item, and the prototype review measures against them rather than assuming.

## Observability
Not instrumented directly. The spec does recommend one measurement for the engineering chunk: record the actual duration of layout transitions (`layout.transition_ms`) in development builds so that a regression in transition cost is visible in the performance test suite rather than discovered by feel.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion inventory complete with a verdict and reason for every E15 transition candidate.
- [ ] Animated items specified with duration, easing and motion token; all restricted to transform/opacity.
- [ ] No animated item changes a panel content box; exceptions none, or justified and approved.
- [ ] Reduced-motion behaviour defined for every inventory item with no motion-only information.
- [ ] Prototype for drop commit, preset application and workspace switch reviewed against a live chart with no observed frame drops.
- [ ] Timing verified against the 80 ms menu and 300 ms preset budgets.
- [ ] Safety rule (no motion delaying environment/armed/error disclosure) written into the spec.
- [ ] Vestibular-safety and flash-threshold review passed.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-motion.md` merged; motion token usage agreed with the design-system team.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D04** - the dock interaction whose transitions this specifies.
- **E15-D03**, **E15-D05** - chrome and preset application.
- E05 motion tokens.

## Branch
`design/e15-motion-spec`

## References
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (motion tokens, durations, easing)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-028
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (reduced motion, flashing, focus)
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`

title: Accessibility design review: keyboard model and screen-reader script (E15)
body:
## Context
E15 is the epic where accessibility is either won or lost for the whole product. Every panel in CandleViewer lives inside this shell, so the region model, the focus model and the announcement vocabulary defined here become the experience of every screen built afterwards. It is also the epic with the most inherently inaccessible interaction in the product - drag-and-drop docking - which `15-component-catalogue.md` makes non-negotiable: CMP-214 requires a mandatory keyboard equivalent.

This ticket is a single consolidated review across all twelve E15 surfaces rather than a per-screen check, because the failures that matter are cross-surface: focus that vanishes after a layout change, two different region-cycling keys, a sync badge announced three different ways, an announcement queue that talks over an order confirmation. Those are invisible when reviewing one screen at a time.

Sprint 05, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 07 stories that consume the reviewed designs.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Consolidated keyboard model** for the workspace, published as one table: `F6` region cycling, `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` panel cycling, `Ctrl+Tab` pane focus (US-LAY-001), `Ctrl+1..9` presets, `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` / `Ctrl+Shift+0` sync groups, `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `F11` full-screen panel, `Shift+F10` panel menu, `Alt+Shift+arrows` splitter resize, and the move-mode keys - each with its scope (global, panel-scoped, mode-scoped) and its conflict status against the global hotkey layer required by US-LAY-006 and US-SET-002.
- **Focus model specification**: where focus goes after every layout mutation (move, split, tabify, float, re-dock, maximise, restore, preset apply, workspace switch, panel add, panel close), written as a rule per operation and verified to never leave focus on a removed element.
- **Region and landmark map** for SCR-020: what is a landmark, what is a `region`, how panel accessible names are composed ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, sync group A"), and the naming rule later epics must follow.
- **Screen-reader announcement script** covering every E15 state change: layout changed, panel moved, panel added/removed, move mode entered/exited, sync group joined/left with consequence, scale link refused, conflict detected, workspace restored, degraded mode entered/exited, import applied with drops. Written as exact strings, with a politeness level and a queueing rule for each.
- **Announcement budget**: a rule preventing announcement storms - which events coalesce, which are suppressed during a drag, and the ordering guarantee relative to trading announcements from later epics.
- **Drag-and-drop compliance audit** against WCAG 2.2: 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size - each with the E15 evidence.
- **Contrast and non-colour audit** consolidated across E15 surfaces: focus affordances, sync badges, drop zones, environment badges, degraded indicators, diff indicators - measured against the darkest and lightest panel content.
- **Screen-reader walkthrough** of the clickable prototypes with NVDA and VoiceOver, plus a keyboard-only walkthrough by a user who does not use a pointer, covering: build a 2x2 layout, bind symbols, join a sync group, save the workspace, reopen it.
- **Findings register** with severity, the owning hi-fi ticket and the resolution, all resolved or accepted before sign-off.
- Review report `docs/design/specs/e15-a11y-review.md`.

## Out of scope
- Code-level a11y testing (axe-core CI, E15 QA chunk) - this is a design-stage review of specifications and prototypes.
- Other epics' surfaces, except where E15's model constrains them (the naming rule is published for their benefit).
- Remediation work itself - findings are fixed in the owning hi-fi tickets, tracked here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every layout operation is achievable without a pointer
  Given the consolidated keyboard model and the E15 prototypes
  When a keyboard-only reviewer performs move, split, tabify, resize, float, re-dock, maximise, close, preset apply and workspace switch
  Then each is completed without a pointer
  And each is confirmed by an announcement naming the result

Scenario: Focus is never lost or orphaned
  Given the focus model table
  When each layout mutation is performed in the prototype
  Then focus lands on the specified element
  And no operation leaves focus on the document body or on a removed element

Scenario: No hotkey conflicts remain unresolved
  Given the E15 hotkey table and the global hotkey layer
  When they are diffed
  Then every collision is listed with a resolution
  And US-LAY-006's requirement that conflicts must be resolved before saving is satisfied by a documented mechanism

Scenario: Announcements do not storm
  Given a preset application that adds four panels and changes two sync groups
  Then the announcement rule coalesces the change into a summary
  And the prototype walkthrough confirms no more than the specified number of utterances

Scenario: A finding cannot be fixed before sign-off
  Given a finding that requires an engineering capability not yet available
  Then it is recorded with a severity, an owner and a target ticket
  And sign-off states explicitly which findings are accepted and why, rather than omitting them

Scenario: A screen-reader user can restore their workspace
  Given NVDA and a saved four-pane workspace
  When the workspace is opened
  Then progress is announced and interactivity is announced when reached
  And any pane that failed to restore is announced with its symbol named
```

## Technical notes / design
The announcement script is the most reusable artefact here. Trading terminals fail screen-reader users not because controls lack labels but because state changes are silent or overwhelming. Writing the exact strings, politeness levels and coalescing rules turns an abstract requirement into something FE can implement and QA can assert against, and it establishes the vocabulary that later epics extend rather than reinvent.

The announcement budget deserves emphasis: E15's layout events will eventually compete with order fills, alerts and connection changes. Set the precedence now - safety-critical trading announcements are assertive and pre-empt; layout announcements are polite and coalesce; and layout announcements are suppressed entirely during an active drag, with one summary on commit.

The focus model must be a table, not a principle. "Focus goes somewhere sensible" produces ten different implementations across ten operations. Naming the destination per operation makes it testable.

WCAG 2.2's newer criteria are exactly the ones this epic risks: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured is easy to fail when a floating window or a dialog overlaps a focused panel control, and 2.5.7 Dragging Movements is the reason the keyboard move mode exists. Audit them explicitly rather than assuming AA by inheritance.

## Test plan
(1) Keyboard-only walkthrough of the five-task scenario by a reviewer who does not use a pointer. (2) NVDA and VoiceOver walkthroughs of the same scenario, transcribing what is actually announced and diffing against the script. (3) Focus-model verification per operation. (4) Hotkey diff against the global layer. (5) Announcement-storm test on preset application and workspace restore. (6) Consolidated contrast measurement and colour-vision simulation across all E15 surfaces. (7) WCAG 2.2 criterion-by-criterion audit for the six named criteria plus the standard AA set. (8) Findings triage with the CDO and the FE lead.

## Security notes
Accessibility and safety intersect on disclosure. The review verifies that every safety-relevant fact is available non-visually: the environment (DEMO/LIVE) must be in the accessible name of every order-capable panel and in every floating window's title; the armed/disarmed state of trading controls must be exposed as a pressed state, not a colour; degraded mode must be announced with what still works; and the unsaved/conflict alertdialog must be announced assertively with its consequences in the text. The review also checks that announcements never leak data a user should not have - a sync or layout announcement must not name an account the user cannot access, consistent with the E15-D09 remapping rule.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable, but two standing rules are recorded for later epics. First, **panel naming**: every panel's accessible name is composed as type, symbol, interval, then state qualifiers, so a screen-reader user hears the same shape everywhere. Second, **no information by position alone**: a user who cannot see the grid cannot know that "the chart on the right" means anything, so every announcement references panels by name rather than by location, with location added as a secondary clause ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, moved to bottom right").

## Performance notes
The review checks that accessibility requirements are specified in a way that does not breach E15's budgets: live regions update on state change only, never per frame; accessible names are computed on change rather than on every render; and the announcement coalescing rule exists partly to prevent the DOM churn that a naive per-event live region would cause on a busy layout. Where a requirement and a budget appear to conflict, the finding is escalated rather than silently resolved in favour of performance.

## Observability
The review recommends two instrumented signals for post-release verification: `a11y.keyboard_layout_operation{operation}` (already partly covered by `layout.panel_moved{method}` from E15-D04), and a count of announcements per minute in development builds, so an announcement storm is caught by the performance suite rather than by a user.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Consolidated keyboard model published with scope and conflict status per binding; all conflicts resolved or with a documented resolution mechanism.
- [ ] Focus model table complete for all listed operations; verified in prototype with no orphaned focus.
- [ ] Region/landmark map and panel-naming rule published for later epics.
- [ ] Full announcement script with exact strings, politeness levels, coalescing and precedence rules.
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 audit complete for 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8 plus the AA set, with evidence.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and NVDA/VoiceOver walkthroughs completed on the five-task scenario; transcripts attached.
- [ ] Consolidated contrast and non-colour audit passed across all E15 surfaces.
- [ ] Findings register complete; every finding fixed in its owning hi-fi ticket or explicitly accepted with a reason.
- [ ] Safety-disclosure checks (environment, armed state, degraded mode) passed non-visually.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-a11y-review.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)**, with the accessibility specialist's concurrence, in Sprint 05 - two sprints before the Sprint 07 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D03**, **E15-D04**, **E15-D05**, **E15-D06**, **E15-D07**, **E15-D08** - the specifications and prototypes under review (D04, D06, D07 and D08 are the blocking ones; later hi-fi tickets feed findings back).

title: Engineering handoff pack for the layouts & workspaces band
body:
## Context
Twelve hi-fi and specification tickets produce a lot of material spread across Figma files and spec pages. Without consolidation, the Sprint 06-09 engineers building US-LAY-001..008 will each assemble their own partial picture, and the inconsistencies will surface as design-QA defects in E15-D17 rather than as questions during development.

This pack is the single entry point: one document that says, for each story in the epic, which spec pages apply, which components are involved, what the states are, what the test ids are, and what is deliberately unresolved. It is produced in Sprint 05, one sprint before the first FE story starts in Sprint 06, so it is ready before anyone opens a branch.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Handoff index** at `docs/design/specs/e15-handoff.md` mapping each of US-LAY-001..008 to: its screens, its components, the spec pages from E15-D03..D14, the Figma frames, and its acceptance-relevant states.
- **Component build order** recommended to FE, respecting dependencies: CMP-080/CMP-082 panel chrome, then CMP-081 dock grid, then CMP-083/CMP-214 interaction, then CMP-216/CMP-217/CMP-218 chrome menus, then CMP-215 floating window, then CMP-073 switcher, then CMP-213 in the picker.
- **Test-id convention** for the E15 surfaces, agreed with QA so that the E2E suite (Playwright, web and Electron) has stable selectors: naming scheme, where ids are required (every panel, every drop zone, every dialog action, every sync axis switch), and where they are forbidden (inside the WebGL canvas).
- **State/prop reconciliation table**: each component's catalogue props against what the designs actually require, with any mismatch resolved before handoff (feeding corrections back into E15-D13 if needed).
- **Storybook story list** consolidated for all E15 components, matching the per-ticket agreements, so the visual-regression baseline is complete on day one.
- **Copy deck**: every user-facing string across E15 in one table - warnings, confirmations, empty states, error states, announcements - so that wording is reviewed once and implemented consistently, and so translation, if ever needed, has a single source.
- **Known gaps and deferrals**: what is deliberately unresolved, who decides, and by when - so engineers do not discover an open question mid-sprint.
- **Handoff session**: a walkthrough with the E15 FE engineers, QA and the Architect, with questions captured and answered in the pack rather than in chat.
- **Design-QA criteria preview**: the checklist E15-D17 will use, published up front so engineers build against the same list they will be reviewed against.

## Out of scope
- New design work - anything discovered here that needs design goes back to the owning hi-fi ticket.
- Engineering estimates or sprint assignment (the eng chunk owns those).
- Test implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every story has a complete handoff entry
  Given the handoff index
  When US-LAY-001 through US-LAY-008 are each looked up
  Then each names its screens, components, spec pages, Figma frames and states
  And no entry is missing a spec page reference

Scenario: An engineer can build without asking a designer
  Given an FE engineer who has not attended any E15 design review
  When they build CMP-082 PanelHeader from the pack alone
  Then the result matches the spec within the design-QA tolerance
  And any question they had to ask is added to the pack as a gap

Scenario: A prop mismatch is found
  Given the state/prop reconciliation table
  When a component's catalogue props cannot express a designed state
  Then the mismatch is resolved before handoff completes
  And the catalogue is corrected rather than the design being silently reduced

Scenario: Copy is consistent across surfaces
  Given the copy deck
  When the same concept appears on more than one surface (for example unsaved changes)
  Then the wording is identical or the difference is deliberate and noted
  And no two surfaces describe the same state differently

Scenario: An open question remains at handoff
  Given a decision that could not be made in Sprint 05
  Then it is listed in known gaps with an owner and a decision date before the consuming sprint
  And the affected story is flagged so it is not started blind
```

## Technical notes / design
The copy deck is the least glamorous and most valuable item. E15 has an unusual density of consequential strings - what is discarded, what is dropped on import, what a preset replaces, what degraded mode still supports - and each one appears on more than one surface. Reviewing them together catches contradictions ("panels are kept" on one screen, "settings are reset" on another) that no single-screen review can.

The test-id convention needs QA in the room because E15's E2E surface is unusually structural: tests will assert on layout trees, focus order and announcement text rather than on content. Agreeing where ids live - and that they do not live inside the canvas - saves the QA chunk from selector archaeology.

Publishing the design-QA checklist up front is deliberate. A review checklist that engineers have not seen until review time produces defensive rework; the same checklist given at handoff produces compliance.

## Test plan
(1) Completeness audit: every story, screen and component in E15's traceability row has an entry. (2) Cold-build test with an engineer who has not attended the reviews. (3) Prop reconciliation walkthrough with the FE lead. (4) Copy consistency diff across surfaces. (5) Test-id review with QA against the planned E2E scenarios. (6) Handoff session with questions captured and resolved into the pack. (7) Link check - every reference resolves.

## Security notes
The pack carries forward the security-relevant design rules so they cannot be lost in implementation, each stated as a build requirement with its source: environment disclosure on every order-capable panel and floating window (E15-D03, D10); RBAC gating is presentation only, enforcement is server-side (E15-D07); imported and saved workspace strings are untrusted and rendered as capped text (E15-D09); exports contain no credentials, account bindings or environment pinning (E15-D09); deep links carry no account ids or tokens (E15-D07); degraded mode may never shed a safety disclosure (E15-D12). The pack contains no credentials, no real account data and no production identifiers in any example or screenshot - sample workspaces use placeholder names.

## Accessibility notes
The pack includes the full E15-D15 output as a build requirement, not as an appendix: the keyboard model table, the focus-destination table, the panel-naming rule and the exact announcement strings. Each component entry states its role, keyboard model and axe expectations. The pack explicitly lists the accessibility items that are acceptance-blocking for the consuming stories, so an engineer knows which ones cannot be deferred to a follow-up.

## Performance notes
The pack restates E15's budgets against the stories that must meet them: >=55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001), <=3 s four-pane restore to interactive (US-LAY-002), sync propagation within one frame and <=4 ms across six panes (US-LAY-003), panel mount <=150 ms, layout transition <=200 ms, preset rebuild <=300 ms, context menu open <=80 ms, 2 MB import validated in <=500 ms off the main thread. It also carries the normative design constraints that protect them - inset focus affordance, static chrome, transform-only drag preview, single layout mutation per drop, no canvas resize in any animation - so they are implemented rather than rediscovered.

## Observability
The pack consolidates the E15 analytics event table from D03..D12 into one list with properties and firing points, so instrumentation is implemented alongside the feature rather than retrofitted. It flags the three events that answer design questions post-release - `layout.panel_moved{method}`, `layout.preset_applied{entry}` and `workspace.restore_completed{ms,paneCount}` - as required rather than optional.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-handoff.md` merged with an entry for every US-LAY-001..008.
- [ ] Component build order recommended and agreed with the FE lead.
- [ ] Test-id convention agreed with QA and documented.
- [ ] State/prop reconciliation table complete; all mismatches resolved and the catalogue corrected.
- [ ] Consolidated Storybook story list published.
- [ ] Copy deck complete and consistency-diffed across surfaces.
- [ ] Security, accessibility and performance requirement lists carried forward as build requirements.
- [ ] Analytics event table consolidated with required events flagged.
- [ ] Known gaps listed with owners and decision dates.
- [ ] Cold-build test passed; questions folded back into the pack.
- [ ] Handoff session held with FE, QA and the Architect; attendance and questions recorded.
- [ ] Design-QA checklist published in advance.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 05, before the Sprint 06 FE start.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D03..E15-D14** - all specification and hi-fi work being consolidated.
- FE lead, QA and Architect availability for the handoff session in Sprint 05.

title: Spike: pane-count budget curve and measured capability profile
body:
## Context
Three separate requirements in this Epic are written as numbers we do not yet have. US-LAY-001 scenario 3 says adding a pane beyond "the performance budget" must warn "with the measured frame cost". US-LAY-008 says capability detection must be "based on measured frame time, not on user-agent strings", and that restoring the full profile shows "the measured frame cost". SCR-020 says >16 panels triggers a degradation warning. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 2 fixes a 30 fps floor for a 6-chart layout with all indicators and all drawings, while US-LAY-001's NFR fixes ≥55 fps for four order-flow panes.

None of those can be implemented as a guess. This Spike produces the actual curve — frame time as a function of pane count and pane kind — on the reference machine and on at least one deliberately weak device, using E11's existing benchmark harness and seeded synthetic dataset. Its output is a small committed table plus a probe API that S01, S02 and S08 consume as fact rather than inventing thresholds each.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark scenario in E11's harness (`benchmarks/layout-scaling`) that instantiates N chart panes (N = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16) at three densities (bare candles / candles + R1 indicator stack / candles + indicators + 200 drawings) against the seeded 100k-bar dataset.
- Runs on: the reference machine in Electron, the reference machine in Chromium, and one low-power profile (integrated GPU, CPU throttled 4x) — the latter being the stand-in for US-LAY-008's "weak GPU".
- A written finding in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR or a benchmark note, Architect's call) recording: the p95 frame time per (N, density, device), the pane count at which p95 crosses 16.6 ms, the count at which it crosses 33.3 ms (the 30 fps floor), and the marginal cost of one additional pane of each kind.
- A **capability probe** API shipped in the app shell: samples frame time over a warm-up window and returns `{ p95FrameMs, recommendedMaxPanes, recommendedProfile: 'full' | 'reduced' }` — no user-agent inspection anywhere in the implementation.
- The reduced profile's concrete content, agreed with the Architect: which knobs it turns (heatmap depth, 200 ms cadence, max panes, detector evaluation) per SCR-153, expressed as a config object, not prose.
- A recommendation on whether sync propagation is cheap enough at 6 and at 16 panes to stay on the main thread or must be moved, feeding **E15-T03**.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the warning UI, the reduced-profile toggle, or the degraded banner (**E15-S01**, **E15-S08**).
- Changing the engine to make any number better — this Spike measures, it does not optimise; optimisation findings are raised as E11/E46 tickets.
- Non-chart pane kinds whose implementing Epic has not shipped (DOM, footprint): estimated by proxy and flagged as estimated, to be re-measured in R2.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The curve exists and is reproducible
  Given the layout-scaling benchmark is run twice on the reference machine
  When the two result sets are compared
  Then p95 frame time per configuration agrees within 10%, and the results are committed as a table with the hardware and build identified

Scenario: The probe classifies a weak device without sniffing
  Given the app runs under a 4x CPU throttle with an integrated GPU
  When the capability probe completes its warm-up
  Then it returns recommendedProfile = 'reduced' with a recommendedMaxPanes below the reference machine's value
  And a grep of the implementation finds no reference to navigator.userAgent or any GPU renderer string used for branching

Scenario: The pane-limit threshold is derived, not invented
  When E15-S01 needs the number at which to warn on adding a pane
  Then it reads recommendedMaxPanes from the probe, and the committed table shows the measurement that produced it

Scenario: A configuration that cannot hold 30 fps is identified explicitly
  Given the 6-pane all-indicators all-drawings configuration is measured
  When p95 exceeds 33.3 ms on any target device
  Then the finding names it as a roadmap exit-criterion risk and a follow-up ticket is raised against E11 or E46 before this Spike closes
```

## Technical notes / design
Reuse E11's harness rather than building a second one — `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 already defines B1..B8 and the seeded dataset, and B6 ("4 synchronised charts, half density") is the nearest existing point; this Spike extends that axis rather than forking it. Measure with the harness's existing p95 methodology so numbers are comparable to the ones CI already gates on.

The probe must warm up: a cold first-frame measurement will misclassify every device. Sample after the first N frames have settled, over a fixed window, and cache the classification per device (US-LAY-008: "the choice is remembered per device").

Timebox: 2 points. If the low-power profile cannot be produced reliably in CI, run it manually once and record the hardware — a manual number beats no number.

## Test plan
The deliverable is measurement, so the "tests" are reproducibility and the probe's own unit tests: probe classification against synthetic frame-time series (fast, borderline, slow, noisy with one 200 ms GC spike that must not flip the classification). The benchmark scenario itself is added to the harness but is **not** made a blocking CI check by this Spike — gating comes later with E46.

## Security notes
None — no user data, no network, no new surface. The probe reports only aggregate timing and stores its result in local device-scoped storage, not on the server; it must not be used as a device fingerprint or transmitted with user identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI. The probe's output must be expressible as plain text ("measured 24 ms per frame with 6 panes") because SCR-153 and US-LAY-008 require the measured cost to be *shown* to the user, not just acted on.

## Performance notes
This ticket is entirely about performance numbers. Reference budgets it must report against: 16.6 ms p95 (budget #1), 33.3 ms floor (roadmap §5.3.2), ≥55 fps / 18.2 ms for four order-flow panes (US-LAY-001 NFR).

## Observability
The probe emits `capability.profile_measured {p95FrameMs, recommendedProfile, paneCount}` once per device session (analytics only). Benchmark runs publish to the same artifact store as E11's harness results so the trend is visible across builds.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings written up and merged under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` or the benchmark notes, with hardware, build sha and methodology stated.
- [ ] Committed results table covering every (N, density, device) cell, with estimated cells marked estimated.
- [ ] Capability probe merged with unit tests, no user-agent branching (verified by a lint rule or a grep assertion in CI).
- [ ] Reduced-profile config object agreed with the Architect and referenced by E15-S08.
- [ ] Recommendation on sync-propagation threading recorded and linked from E15-T03.
- [ ] Any configuration failing the 30 fps floor has a follow-up ticket filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (engine instances and benchmark harness must exist to measure). Blocks **E15-T02**, **E15-S01**, **E15-S08**; informs **E15-T03**.

## Branch
`spike/e15-pane-budget-curve`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001 (scenario 3, NFR), US-LAY-008; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 benchmarks B1..B8, R8; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 1 and 2; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 (>16 panels state), SCR-153; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1 and #14.

title: workspaces/layouts/layout_panes migration and /workspaces REST API
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 5 requires chart state to survive "reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss". That guarantee is only as good as the server-side store behind it, because local storage does not survive a machine change and the roadmap explicitly specifies workspaces as "server-persisted per user". This Task implements that store and its contract, interface-first, so the client work (E15-T02, E15-S03) codes against a merged API rather than a promise.

Both halves are already specified. The schema is `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 — `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, shipped in migration `0011_workspace`. The contract is drafted in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` under the `workspaces` tag, every operation carrying `x-rbac: { permissions: [workspaces:read|write], scope: self }`.

One detail carries weight far outside this Epic: `ix_lp_symbol ON layout_panes (symbol) WHERE symbol IS NOT NULL` is, per §3.8.1, "what the recorder queries to decide which symbols are 'chart open' for auto-recording". E16 depends on this index existing and being accurate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration `0011_workspace` (the workspaces portion) creating exactly per §3.8.1:
  - `workspaces` — `id`, `user_id` FK→`users` ON DELETE CASCADE, `name`, `is_default`, `icon_token`, `sort_order`, timestamps, `deleted_at`; unique indexes `ux_ws_name` (per user, lower(name), alive rows) and `ux_ws_default` (one default per user, alive rows).
  - `layouts` — `id`, `workspace_id` FK ON DELETE CASCADE, `name`, `grid_preset`, `grid_spec` jsonb, `crosshair_sync`, `level_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `hotkey_slot`, `is_default`, timestamps, `deleted_at`; constraints `lay_preset` and `lay_slot`; unique indexes `ux_lay_name`, `ux_lay_slot`.
  - `layout_panes` — `id`, `layout_id` FK ON DELETE CASCADE, `slot_index`, `pane_kind`, `symbol`, `interval_code`, `chart_template_id` FK→`chart_templates` ON DELETE SET NULL, `indicator_preset_ids` uuid[], `pane_config` jsonb, `scale_mode`, timestamps; constraints `lp_kind`, `lp_slot`, `lp_scale`; `UNIQUE (layout_id, slot_index)`; indexes `ix_lp_layout`, `ix_lp_symbol`.
- Endpoints per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces`; `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`; `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`; `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`; `GET /api/v1/layout-presets` (static built-in catalogue, no auth-scoped rows).
- `PUT` on workspace and layout honours `If-Match` and returns **412** on a stale token — the OpenAPI description states the reason: "prevents a stale tab from clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window".
- `POST/PUT /layouts` replaces the pane set transactionally: panes are validated as a whole (slot uniqueness, `pane_kind` enum, `slot_index` 0..15, `scale_mode` enum, `grid_spec` shape when `grid_preset='custom'`) and written in one transaction; partial application is impossible.
- `GET /workspaces/{id}` returns `WorkspaceDetail` — workspace metadata plus its layouts in one round-trip, so restore is a single request per workspace.
- `is_default` is enforced by the partial unique index, and setting a new default clears the old one inside the same transaction.
- Soft delete via `deleted_at` on `workspaces`/`layouts`; deleting the **last** alive workspace of a user is refused with 409 (SCR-025: "You need at least one workspace.").
- Owner scoping on every read and write; cross-user ids return **404**.
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI document; drift fails CI.

## Out of scope
- `chart_templates`, `drawings`, `indicator_presets`, `hotkey_profiles` tables — same migration file, different Epics (E13/E14/E10); this Task only takes the FK reference to `chart_templates`.
- `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` and import — **E15-S07** (it needs the redaction rules, not just the rows).
- Any client code or debounce logic — **E15-T02**, **E15-S03**.
- WS push of layout changes to other sessions — out of R1 scope; conflicts are detected by `If-Match` only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A workspace with layouts and panes round-trips exactly
  Given user A creates a workspace and a 2x2 layout with four panes of differing kinds, symbols and intervals
  When GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id} is called as user A
  Then the response contains the workspace and the layout with all four panes, each with identical slot_index, pane_kind, symbol, interval_code, indicator_preset_ids and pane_config

Scenario: A stale client cannot clobber a newer arrangement
  Given two sessions loaded the same layout and session B saved a change
  When session A sends PUT with its original If-Match token
  Then the API responds 412, the stored layout is unchanged, and session A can re-read the current version

Scenario: Cross-user access is denied without disclosing existence
  Given user B knows user A's workspaceId
  When user B calls GET, PUT or DELETE on it
  Then the API responds 404 and nothing is mutated

Scenario: An invalid pane set is rejected whole
  When a layout is PUT with two panes claiming slot_index 3, or a pane_kind outside the lp_kind enum, or slot_index 16
  Then the API responds 422 naming the offending pane, and the previously stored pane set is intact

Scenario: The last workspace cannot be deleted
  Given a user has exactly one alive workspace
  When they DELETE it
  Then the API responds 409 with an explanatory code and the workspace remains

Scenario: Deleting a workspace cascades to layouts and panes
  Given a workspace with two layouts of four panes each
  When it is deleted and the user has another workspace
  Then the workspace is soft-deleted, its layouts are no longer returned, and a subsequent hard purge removes the layout_panes rows

Scenario: The recorder can find chart-open symbols
  Given three layouts across two users contain panes bound to BTCUSDT
  When the recorder queries layout_panes by symbol
  Then the query uses ix_lp_symbol and returns those panes without a sequential scan
```

## Technical notes / design
The layout tree lives in `grid_spec` as jsonb only when `grid_preset = 'custom'`; named presets store their name and an empty spec, keeping the common case small and queryable. Validation of `grid_spec` is a JSON Schema check at the API boundary, not a database constraint — the CHECK constraints in §3.8.1 cover only the enums.

`If-Match` tokens are derived from `updated_at` (weak ETag over the layout aggregate including its panes, so a pane-only change bumps the token). A `PUT` that changes nothing still returns 200 with an unchanged token rather than a spurious write, so the client's 2 s debounce can be naive.

Pane writes are full replacement, not diff: the client always knows the whole tree, and replacement makes slot uniqueness trivially enforceable inside one transaction. Row churn is irrelevant here — §sizing caps all config tables at <100 MB, "bounded by human editing rate".

## Test plan
Unit: pane-set validators, ETag derivation, default-workspace transition, last-workspace guard. Contract: schemathesis across every operation including 412, 409, 422 and 404 paths. Integration: Postgres-backed round-trip; cascade delete; concurrent `PUT` race resolving to exactly one winner and one 412; `EXPLAIN` assertion that the recorder's symbol query uses `ix_lp_symbol`. Security: IDOR matrix (owner/other/viewer × read/write/delete over workspace, layout and nested pane ids). Migration: apply and roll back on a seeded database.

## Security notes
STRIDE: the dominant threats are Tampering and Information disclosure via IDOR on `workspaceId`/`layoutId`, both covered by the explicit test matrix and the 404-not-403 rule. Stored user content — `name`, `icon_token`, `pane_config` — is length-capped (name 1..40 per SCR-020's validation rule), control characters stripped, and `pane_config` size-capped and schema-validated so a pane cannot become an arbitrary blob store. `icon_token` is validated against the design-system token list, never a URL. No secrets, no PII, no financial data: classification is user preference data. RBAC per E09 — Viewer holds `workspaces:write` deliberately (`21-database-schema.md` §RBAC), scoped to self only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The API returns `name`, `pane_kind` and `symbol` so the client can compose accessible region names ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m") without extra round-trips.

## Performance notes
`GET /workspaces/{id}` with 4 layouts × 8 panes < 10 ms p99. `PUT` of a 16-pane layout < 25 ms p99. The recorder's symbol query < 5 ms p99 via `ix_lp_symbol`. Restore is one request per workspace by design — the 3 s restore-to-interactive NFR cannot afford an N+1 per pane.

## Observability
`http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/workspaces*"}`, `layout_conflict_total` (412 count), `panes_per_layout` histogram on write, `workspaces_total` gauge per user bucket. Structured logs carry `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `layout_id`, `pane_count` — never `pane_config` contents.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the workspace router and repository.
- [ ] Migration applies and rolls back cleanly on a seeded database; `0011_workspace` documented in §migrations.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` merged and contract tests green; deliberate drift fails CI.
- [ ] IDOR matrix executed; Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] `EXPLAIN` evidence attached for the recorder's `ix_lp_symbol` query, linked from E16.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E09** (users, sessions, `workspaces:read`/`workspaces:write` permissions). Blocks **E15-S03**, **E15-S07**; unblocks **E16**'s auto-record trigger.

## Branch
`feat/e15-workspaces-api`

## References
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, migration `0011_workspace`, §RBAC permission catalogue, §sizing; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`, `/layout-presets`, schemas `Workspace`, `WorkspaceInput`, `WorkspaceDetail`, `Layout`, `LayoutInput`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-002; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-025; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 5.

title: packages/dock: layout tree, reconciler and DockGrid without GL churn
body:
## Context
Every user-facing ticket in this Epic — presets, docking, save/restore, sync, responsive collapse — is a different way of mutating the same data structure. Writing that structure once, in a package with no React and no chart knowledge, is what keeps those five Stories from each inventing their own tree algebra. It also makes the hardest requirement testable in a unit test instead of an E2E: SCR-020's "layout changes never remount the WebGL context".

That requirement is a reconciliation property, not a rendering trick. If a move is expressed as "remove leaf, insert leaf", React unmounts the canvas and E11 loses its context, its buffers and its data window — a visible flash plus a refetch, and R1 exit criterion 5 ("zero loss") starts leaking. If a move is expressed as "reparent the node with this stable id", nothing unmounts. This Task builds the structure that makes the second one the only option available.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/dock` — framework-free, no React, no `fetch`, no chart-engine import (enforced by an import-linter contract in the same style as `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 for the engine):
  - Node model: `row | column | tabset | leaf`, each with a stable `id`, `leaf` carrying `{ paneId, kind, minWidth, minHeight }`, containers carrying fractional `sizes[]`.
  - Operations: `split(targetId, direction, newLeaf)`, `move(paneId, targetId, zone)`, `tabify`, `close(paneId)`, `resize(separatorId, delta)`, `maximise/restore(paneId)`, `float/redock(paneId)`, `applyPreset(preset, existingPanes)`.
  - `normalise(tree)` — collapses single-child containers, removes empty tabsets, clamps fractions to sum 1, enforces minimum sizes; every operation returns a normalised tree.
  - `matchPreset(tree)` → `'1x1' | '2x1' | '1x2' | '2x2' | '1+3' | '3x3' | 'custom'`, and `presetToTree(preset, panes)` — the mapping onto the `lay_preset` CHECK constraint in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1.
  - Serialisation: `toLayoutInput(tree, panes)` / `fromLayout(layout)` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`'s `LayoutInput`/`Layout`, including the `slot_index` assignment that `layout_panes` requires.
  - `resolveDrop(tree, pointerRect, panes)` → the candidate zone set used by CMP-214, and its keyboard twin `resolveDirectionalMove(tree, paneId, direction)` used by CMP-216's "Move panel" chooser — one code path, two entry points, so the keyboard equivalent cannot drift from the pointer one.
- **CMP-081 DockGrid / Layout Manager**, **CMP-080 DockPanel**, **CMP-082 PanelHeader**, **CMP-083 SplitPane** in the app, rendering a tree from the package:
  - Reconciliation keyed by stable `paneId` so any operation is a reparent; panel content is mounted through a **pane registry** (`kind` → component) so E11/E13/E18+ panels plug in without DockGrid knowing them.
  - Lazy mount on first visibility; hidden-tab panels unsubscribe after 30 s (SCR-020 performance line).
  - Resize via CSS/flex fractions only — no per-frame React state, no layout thrash; the engine is told its new size once per commit.
- A **GL-churn guard**: a test utility that counts `webglcontextlost`/context creations and canvas unmounts across an operation sequence, wired into the package's own test suite so the invariant regresses loudly.

## Out of scope
- The drop-zone visuals, panel menu, preset gallery, floating windows — **E15-S01**, **E15-S02** consume this package.
- Persistence, debounce, conflict handling — **E15-S03**.
- Sync between panes — **E15-T03**.
- Any actual panel implementation; the registry ships with a placeholder panel plus whatever kinds E11–E14 already expose.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Moving a pane never remounts its canvas
  Given a 2x2 tree with four chart leaves each holding a live GL context
  When a pane is moved to the opposite corner, then tabified, then split out again
  Then the GL-churn guard reports zero context losses and zero canvas unmounts, and each pane keeps its data window

Scenario: Every operation returns a normalised tree
  Given a randomised sequence of 1000 split/move/close/resize operations from a property-based generator
  When each result is checked
  Then no container has a single child, no tabset is empty, every sizes[] sums to 1 within floating-point tolerance, and no leaf is smaller than its minimum

Scenario: Preset detection and reconstruction round-trip
  Given a tree built by applyPreset('2x2', panes)
  When matchPreset is called on it
  Then it returns '2x2', and presetToTree('2x2', panes) reproduces an equivalent tree with the same pane ids

Scenario: Keyboard move and pointer drop agree
  Given a pane and a target with any zone
  When the same relocation is expressed as resolveDrop and as resolveDirectionalMove
  Then both produce the identical resulting tree

Scenario: Applying a preset preserves matching panes
  Given a 2x2 layout of four chart panes
  When the 1+3 preset is applied
  Then the four existing pane instances are reused in the new slots rather than recreated, and SCR-022's <= 300 ms budget is met

Scenario: Serialisation matches the stored schema
  When toLayoutInput is called on a custom tree of 16 panes
  Then slot_index values are unique and within 0..15, grid_preset is 'custom', grid_spec validates against the layout JSON Schema, and fromLayout of the result is structurally identical
```

## Technical notes / design
The tree is immutable — every operation returns a new tree — which makes undo, conflict diffing (SCR-029's "side-by-side summary of differences") and property testing straightforward, and makes accidental in-place mutation from a React render impossible.

The package is deliberately ignorant: it knows `kind` is a string and `minWidth` is a number, nothing more. That is what lets it be unit-tested with no DOM, no canvas and no network, which in turn is what makes the 1000-operation property test cheap enough to run on every PR.

The pane registry inverts the dependency: DockGrid imports no panel, panels register themselves. Panel kinds whose Epic has not landed register a disabled stub carrying the reason string SCR-024 shows ("Needs a recorded symbol", "Owner only").

`resolveDrop`/`resolveDirectionalMove` sharing one implementation is not a tidiness preference — CMP-214's catalogue entry makes the keyboard equivalent **mandatory**, and two implementations would diverge by the second bug fix.

Minimum sizes feed SCR-021's "panel too small — showing compact view" state; the package reports the condition, the app renders it.

## Test plan
Unit (the bulk, headless): tree algebra, normalisation invariants, preset match/build, serialisation round-trip, drop resolution, directional move equivalence. Property-based: the 1000-operation sequence above, plus a shrinking check that any violating sequence is reported minimally. Component: DockGrid with fake panels — reparent without unmount (React profiler / instance identity assertions), lazy mount, 30 s unsubscribe, keyboard resize on CMP-083's `role="separator"`. Perf: preset apply ≤300 ms and panel mount ≤150 ms measured in a component benchmark with the pane counts from E15-K01. A11y: axe on DockGrid/DockPanel/PanelHeader/SplitPane; focus-order assertion that visual order and focus order agree (or that `aria-owns` corrects it, per CMP-081).

## Security notes
No network, no credentials, no user-supplied HTML: the package handles ids, numbers and enum strings. Two guards matter anyway — pane `kind` is validated against the registry before mount so a tampered or imported layout cannot name an arbitrary component, and tree depth and node count are capped (16 panes per `lp_slot`, depth cap on nesting) so a hostile imported layout cannot cause unbounded recursion in normalise. Both caps are enforced here, which is what lets E15-S07 trust the tree it imports.

## Accessibility notes
Each DockPanel is `role="region"` with an accessible name composed from kind + symbol + interval (CMP-080). SplitPane dividers are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-valuenow`, arrow-key resizable (CMP-083). Panel focus order follows visual reading order, corrected via `aria-owns` when DOM order cannot match (CMP-081). Every operation exposed by the package has a keyboard entry point by construction — `resolveDirectionalMove` exists precisely so no layout operation is pointer-only (CMP-214). Layout changes are announced politely once per commit, not per intermediate frame.

## Performance notes
Tree operations are O(nodes) with n ≤ 31 for 16 panes — negligible; the budget risk is entirely in the React commit. Targets: preset apply ≤300 ms (SCR-022), panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-024, CMP-080), layout transition ≤200 ms (CMP-081), drag preview on CSS transforms only with exactly one layout mutation on drop (SCR-021). Resize must not re-render panel content — the engine receives one resize call per commit, not per pointer move.

## Observability
The package is instrumented but does not log: it emits a `layoutChanged { op, paneCount, preset, durationMs }` callback the app forwards to analytics as `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.preset_applied` etc. The GL-churn guard's counters are exported in dev builds so a regression is visible in Storybook, not only in CI.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test, including the property-based sequence.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on `packages/dock` (engine-package floor, since it is framework-free logic), ≥80% on the app-side DockGrid components.
- [ ] Import-linter contract merged: `packages/dock` may not import React, the chart engine, or anything doing I/O.
- [ ] GL-churn guard wired into CI; a deliberate remount-causing change fails the build.
- [ ] Storybook entries per CMP-080/081/082/083 catalogue lists, including the keyboard resize and keyboard reposition demos.
- [ ] axe-core green; focus-order assertion passing.
- [ ] Perf numbers recorded against E15-K01's curve.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC per unit of work (package and app wiring split across PRs), 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-K01** (pane budget informs minimum sizes and the compact-view threshold), **E11** (engine instances to prove no GL churn), **E10** (app shell, hotkey layer, Electron window plumbing for the float hook). Blocks **E15-S01**, **E15-S02**, **E15-S03**, **E15-T03**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-dock-package`

## References
`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-083, CMP-214, CMP-216; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 (performance line, >16 panels), SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-024; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`lay_preset`, `lp_slot`, `layout_panes`); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `LayoutInput`, `Layout`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-005; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2, §5 context-loss handling; `/CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16.


## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

title: Black-box test plan for the E15 layout, workspace and sync story groups
body:
## Context
E15 turns a single chart into the daily working surface: preset and custom grids, dockable panels, cross-pane sync groups, named workspaces persisted server-side, layout hotkeys, export/import and a reduced-capability profile. Every later epic (E18 footprint, E21 DOM+heatmap, E30 order ticket) mounts *inside* this dock tree, so a defect here is felt by every subsequent surface and is expensive to find late.

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded black-box QA pass non-skippable for each Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written per-feature test plan plus a white-box review checklist. Today the E15 story tickets describe *what to build*; there is no single artefact a QA engineer can execute against a staging build to assert "layouts and workspaces behave as specified".

This ticket produces that artefact. It is deliberately black-box — written against the screens `SCR-020..029`, `SCR-011`, `SCR-022`, `SCR-043`, `SCR-049`, `SCR-150`, `SCR-153` and the public REST contract `/workspaces*` — so it survives refactors of the internal dock-tree representation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md`, organised as five executable groups:
  1. **Grid layouts & dock system** (US-LAY-001, US-LAY-005) — `SCR-020`, `SCR-021`, `SCR-024`, `SCR-028`; CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid / Layout Manager, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-083 SplitPane, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-216 PanelMenu.
  2. **Workspaces persistence & restore** (US-LAY-002) — `SCR-020`, `SCR-025`, `SCR-150`; `GET /api/v1/workspaces`, `POST /api/v1/workspaces`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `GET|POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`; tables `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, `chart_templates`.
  3. **Cross-pane sync & scale linking** (US-LAY-003, US-LAY-004) — `SCR-023`, `SCR-043`, `SCR-049`; CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-218 SyncMenu, CMP-188/CMP-189 scale menus.
  4. **Hotkeys & quick switching** (US-LAY-006) — `SCR-011`, `SCR-022`; `Ctrl+1..9`, `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `Ctrl+Tab`, `F6`, `F11`, `Ctrl+Shift+1..3`, `Ctrl+Shift+0`.
  5. **Export/import & reduced capability** (US-LAY-007, US-LAY-008) — `SCR-026`, `SCR-153`; `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export`, import validation, degraded-profile prompt.
- Per case: id `E15-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (seeded user + seeded workspace fixture), steps, expected result, the `US-LAY-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E15-Q02`/`E15-Q03`, or manual-only).
- **Fixture appendix**: seeded owner / manager / viewer; three seeded workspaces (empty, 4-pane `2x2` matching the `fourPane` example in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, 16-pane stress); a workspace referencing a delisted symbol; a workspace export file at the current schema version and one at version+1.
- **Traceability table** US-LAY-001..008 × test cases × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.16, proving no story is untested.
- **White-box review checklist** for reviewers: dock-tree mutations are single-commit, layout changes never remount the WebGL context, hidden panels unsubscribe after 30 s.
- Defect-reporting conventions: severity mapping per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3; "workspace save silently loses panes" is always `priority/p0`.

## Out of scope
- Panel *content* correctness (bars, footprint, DOM) — owned by E12/E18/E21 test plans; E15 asserts only mount, bind, resize, unmount and lifecycle.
- Electron packaging/update behaviour (E10); this plan covers floating windows only as a workspace-state concern.
- Load and chaos execution (`E15-Q04`, `E15-Q05`) and adversarial import cases (`E15-X02`) — this plan references them and does not duplicate them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Plan covers every LAY story
  Given the published qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 16
  Then each of US-LAY-001..008 maps to at least one case per Gherkin scenario in its story, including the stated edge case
  And every case names the screen or endpoint it exercises

Scenario: A case is executable by someone new to the epic
  Given a QA engineer who has not worked on E15
  When they run group 2 against a staging build using only the fixture appendix
  Then they can reach a pass/fail verdict on every case without asking the authors a question

Scenario: Failure case - stale-write conflict is specified
  Given a workspace opened in two tabs and modified in both
  When the second tab saves with a stale If-Match
  Then the plan requires a 412 PreconditionFailed and the SCR-020 "This workspace changed elsewhere. [Keep mine] [Load theirs]" dialog, and forbids silent overwrite

Scenario: Edge case - missing symbol does not fail the workspace
  Given a saved workspace whose pane references a delisted symbol
  When it is restored
  Then the plan requires that pane to show a named error state and all other panes to load normally

Scenario: Plan is reviewed and merged
  When the plan PR is opened
  Then it carries approvals from the E15 frontend lead and the SDET, and is linked from the E15 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure the plan by *observable surface*, not by component: reviewers must be able to re-run it after the dock tree is refactored.
- The 16-pane stress fixture exists to exercise the SCR-020 ">16 panels" warning and the US-LAY-001 pane-limit confirmation, which must state the *measured* frame cost, not a static string.
- Sync cases must assert group scoping (group A changes never touch group B) and the letter-plus-colour badge rule from `SCR-023` — colour alone is a defect (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- Persisted shape follows `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1: `workspaces` (unique name per user, single default), `layouts` (unique name and unique `hotkey_slot` per workspace), `layout_panes` (unique `slot_index` per layout). Cases must cover each uniqueness violation returning 422, not a 500.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own verification is a dry run: execute one group end-to-end against the current staging build, record timings and any ambiguity found, and fix the plan before merge. Record the dry-run log as an attachment so the plan's executability claim is evidenced rather than asserted.

## Security notes
- The plan must include the negative assertion that an exported workspace contains no secrets, tokens or account ids (US-LAY-007); the deep adversarial version lives in `E15-X02`.
- Cross-user access cases (user B requesting user A's `workspaceId`) are listed here as smoke-level and owned in depth by `E15-X02`; expected result is 404, never 403-with-existence-disclosure.
- Fixtures must never contain real Bybit API keys or live account identifiers; seeded users use deterministic throwaway credentials.

## Accessibility notes
- Every pointer-driven case has a paired keyboard case: docking via CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel", splitter resize via `Alt+Shift+arrows`, region cycling via `F6`, pane focus via `Ctrl+Tab`.
- Cases assert each panel is a `region` with an accessible name of the form "Chart, BTCUSDT 1m" and that dock operations announce their result in a live region ("Chart moved to bottom-right").
- Depth a11y auditing is `E15-Q06`; this plan carries the smoke-level assertions so a regression is caught in the functional pass too.

## Performance notes
- Plan records, per case where relevant, the budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001 NFR), workspace restore to interactive ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR), sync propagation ≤1 frame (US-LAY-003 NFR), preset apply ≤300 ms (`SCR-022`), panel mount ≤150 ms (`SCR-024`), context menu ≤80 ms (`SCR-028`).
- Measurement is by the instrumented build; the rigorous benchmark run is `E15-Q04`.

## Observability
- Cases assert the analytics/audit events named in the screens catalogue actually fire with the documented payloads: `workspace.saved`, `workspace.updated`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.exported`, `panel.added`, `panel.removed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`, `sync.group_changed`.
- The plan states where to read them during a manual run (the dev analytics sink), so "event missing" is a reportable defect rather than an invisible one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan merged at `qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md` with all five groups, fixtures, traceability table and white-box checklist.
- [ ] Dry-run log of at least one full group attached to the ticket.

- [ ] Automation split agreed and recorded with `E15-Q02` and `E15-Q03`.
- [ ] Reviewed by the E15 frontend lead and an SDET; linked from the E15 epic.

## Dependencies
- `E15-S01` (grid layouts), `E15-S02` (saved workspaces), `E15-S03` (cross-pane sync), `E15-S05` (docking) must be far enough along that the surfaces are testable.
- Consumes `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, `11-user-stories.md` §16, `14-screens-catalogue.md` §2, `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.16, `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`.
