title: Grid presets, preset gallery and layout hotkeys (SCR-022)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-001** ("Preset grid: when I choose 2×2, four panes are created, each independently bindable to a symbol and interval"; "Custom split: dragging a divider resizes with live preview and sizes persist"; "Pane limit: adding another pane beyond the performance budget warns with the measured frame cost and requires confirmation") and **US-LAY-006** ("Preset hotkey: Ctrl+1 loads layout preset 1 with its saved bindings"; "Pane focus: Ctrl+Tab advances focus with a visible indicator and screen-reader announcement"; "Conflict: a preset hotkey colliding with a trading hotkey is flagged in settings and must be resolved before saving").

The surfaces are **SCR-022** Layout preset gallery and the preset/focus behaviour on **SCR-020**. The hotkey slots are already modelled: `layouts.hotkey_slot` (1..9, unique per workspace) in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, and `layout.preset_1..9` → `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` in the default hotkey table.

This is the first Story to consume `packages/dock`, so it is also the first place the "reuse existing panel instances where the type matches, avoiding GL context churn" rule (SCR-022) is visible to a user.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built-in grid presets wired to `presetToTree`: 1×1, 2×1, 1×2, 2×2, 1+3, 3×1, 3×3 — exactly the `lay_preset` CHECK enum plus the named compositions SCR-022 lists (Scalping = chart+DOM+ticket+tape, Order-flow = chart+footprint+CVD+profile, Swing = 3 timeframes, Analyst = read-only chart+journal+replay, Fan-out review). Compositions whose panel kinds are not yet implemented render their available subset and mark the rest disabled with a reason, per SCR-024's convention.
- **SCR-022** gallery modal (**CMP-217** LayoutPresetMenu, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-050 Card, CMP-001 Button): static SVG thumbnails (no live panels), a "Keep current symbols" checkbox, an Apply action, and the warning "Applying a preset replaces the current layout. Settings of surviving panels are kept."
- Preset application reuses matching pane instances by kind so no GL context is recreated; surviving panes keep symbol, interval, indicators and drawings when "Keep current symbols" is on.
- Saved custom presets: "Save current as preset" writes a layout with a `hotkey_slot`; rename and delete; the empty user-preset state.
- Hotkeys `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` bound through E10's global hotkey layer to `layouts.hotkey_slot`, remappable per US-LAY-006's NFR, with the collision check against trading hotkeys surfaced in settings and blocking save.
- Pane focus cycling: `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` and `F6` region cycling, with a visible focus ring and one polite announcement naming the pane ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, pane 2 of 4").
- Drag-to-resize dividers with live preview, committing exactly one layout mutation on release (SCR-021 performance line).
- Pane-limit guard: adding a pane beyond E15-K01's `recommendedMaxPanes` shows the measured frame cost and requires explicit confirmation; >16 panes is refused outright by `lp_slot`.

## Out of scope
- Persisting the applied layout to the server — **E15-S03** (this Story mutates client state and emits the change).
- Docking by drag, floating windows, the panel picker — **E15-S02**.
- Sync configuration — **E15-S04**.
- Chart-template selection inside a preset — **E13**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Applying 2x2 creates four independently bindable panes
  Given a 1x1 workspace showing BTCUSDT 1m
  When the trader applies the 2x2 preset
  Then four panes exist, each with its own symbol and interval control, and changing pane 3's interval leaves panes 1, 2 and 4 unchanged

Scenario: Surviving panes keep their state and their GL context
  Given a 2x2 layout of four chart panes with indicators and drawings
  When the 1+3 preset is applied with "Keep current symbols" checked
  Then all four panes keep their symbol, interval, indicators and drawings
  And zero WebGL contexts are created or lost, and the rebuild completes within 300 ms

Scenario: A preset hotkey loads its layout
  Given a custom preset is saved to slot 1
  When the trader presses Ctrl+1 from anywhere in the workspace
  Then that layout loads with its saved pane bindings and the change is announced once

Scenario: Hotkey collision blocks saving
  Given Ctrl+2 is already bound to a trading action
  When the trader assigns Ctrl+2 to a layout preset
  Then the conflict is shown in settings naming both actions, and the assignment cannot be saved until it is resolved

Scenario: Exceeding the measured pane budget requires confirmation
  Given the capability probe reported recommendedMaxPanes = 6 at 24 ms per frame
  When the trader adds a seventh pane
  Then a confirmation states the measured frame cost and what it means, and the pane is added only on explicit confirmation

Scenario: Keyboard-only pane focus
  Given a 2x2 layout and a keyboard-only trader
  When they press Ctrl+Tab three times
  Then focus visits each pane in visual reading order with a visible focus indicator, and each pane is announced by name and position

Scenario: Divider drag previews then commits once
  When a divider is dragged and released
  Then a live preview follows the pointer, exactly one layout mutation is committed on release, and the new sizes are reflected in the layout tree
```

## Technical notes / design
Presets are data, not code: a preset is `{ id, label, tree, paneKinds[], thumbnail }`, so adding one in R2 (an order-flow composition) is a data change. `matchPreset` from `packages/dock` keeps the gallery's active-preset highlight honest after manual resizing — a dragged divider silently turns `2x2` into `custom`, and the gallery must show that rather than lie.

Instance reuse is a matching problem: pair old leaves to new slots by `kind` first, then by original position, so a 2×2→1+3 transition keeps the visually corresponding panes. Unmatched old panes are closed; unmatched new slots mount fresh.

The pane-limit warning must quote a **measured** number (E15-K01), never a constant — US-LAY-001 says "states the measured frame cost", and a hard-coded 6 would be wrong on both the reference machine and a laptop.

Hotkeys route through E10's layer so remapping and conflict detection are one implementation across the app, not a layout-local special case.

## Test plan
Unit: preset data→tree mapping, instance-matching algorithm, `matchPreset` after manual resize, hotkey slot uniqueness. Component: gallery rendering, "keep symbols" behaviour, disabled panel kinds with reasons, empty custom-preset state. Integration: preset apply with live engines asserting zero GL churn and ≤300 ms. E2E (Playwright + Electron): Ctrl+1..9 preset switching, Ctrl+Tab focus cycle, divider drag, pane-limit confirmation. A11y: axe on SCR-022; screen-reader script verifying preset names describe the arrangement in words ("Two by two, four panes", CMP-217) and that thumbnails carry enumerating alt text; focus-ring visibility at AA contrast. Perf: preset apply ≤300 ms at 4 and 6 panes.

## Security notes
Low surface. Custom preset names are user content: 1..40 chars, control characters stripped, rendered as text. Hotkey bindings are per-user preference and cannot invoke a trading action indirectly — the collision check exists so a layout binding never shadows an order-entry binding, which is a safety property as much as a usability one. No new endpoints beyond `GET /api/v1/layout-presets` (read-only, built-in catalogue).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The gallery is a listbox of cards; each preset's accessible name describes the arrangement in words, not by thumbnail alone, and thumbnails carry alt text enumerating their panels (CMP-217, SCR-022). Applying a preset announces the result once. `Ctrl+Tab`/`F6` pane cycling has a visible focus indicator and a name+position announcement (US-LAY-006). Dividers are keyboard-resizable via CMP-083's `role="separator"`. Applying a preset that would discard unsaved panes routes through SCR-029 rather than silently destroying work. Hotkey hints use CMP-022 Kbd so they are readable, not icon-only.

## Performance notes
Preset apply ≤300 ms rebuilding the dock tree and reusing panel instances (SCR-022); thumbnails are static SVG so the gallery costs nothing to open; layout transition ≤200 ms (CMP-081); divider drag uses CSS transforms with one mutation on release (SCR-021). Pane-limit thresholds come from E15-K01's measured curve.

## Observability
`layout.preset_previewed`, `layout.preset_applied {presetId, paneCount, reusedPanes}`, `layout.preset_saved_as`, `layout.preset_deleted`, `layout.panel_added {type, placement}`, `layout.pane_limit_warning_shown {measuredFrameMs, paneCount}`, `layout.pane_limit_confirmed`. Client metric `layout_apply_duration_ms` reported with pane count.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the preset and hotkey modules.
- [ ] SCR-022 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior (design-ahead rule) or a recorded waiver; its sign-off checklist items verified in the built UI.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-022; manual screen-reader pass of preset apply and pane focus cycling.
- [ ] Zero-GL-churn assertion passing for preset application; ≤300 ms recorded.
- [ ] Hotkey collision path demonstrated in settings.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (tree, presets, instance reuse), **E15-K01** (measured pane budget), **E05** (design system: Dialog, Card, Button, Kbd tokens). Relies on **E10**'s hotkey layer.

## Branch
`feat/e15-preset-gallery`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-006; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-217, CMP-081, CMP-083, CMP-022, CMP-043, CMP-050; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-006 rows; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`lay_preset`, `hotkey_slot`, `ux_lay_slot`), §hotkey defaults `layout.preset_1..9`; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/layout-presets`.

title: Panel docking, floating windows, panel picker and panel menu
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-005** — "dock, float, resize and hide panels (DOM, tape, positions, stats, alerts), so that my screen fits my workflow" — whose three scenarios are: dragging the DOM panel to the right edge docks it with a preview and persists its width; hiding the tape leaves it restorable from the view menu and by hotkey; floating a panel in the Electron shell opens a separate always-on-top window whose position persists per workspace. Its NFR is unambiguous: "docking has keyboard-accessible equivalents; floating windows are Electron-only and the control is hidden in the browser build with an explanation."

Surfaces: **SCR-021** Dock/panel system (drop zones, splitters, float), **SCR-024** Panel picker, **SCR-027** Floating panel window (Electron), **SCR-028** Panel context menu. Components: **CMP-214** DockDropZone, **CMP-215** FloatingWindowFrame, **CMP-216** PanelMenu, **CMP-213** FuzzyList, plus CMP-080/082 from E15-T02.

CMP-214's catalogue entry states the a11y rule as a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have: "drag-and-drop has a **mandatory** keyboard equivalent — 'Move panel' from CMP-216 PanelMenu opens a directional chooser (left/right/top/bottom/tab-into) so no layout operation is pointer-only." E15-T02 already made both paths share one resolver; this Story surfaces them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Drag docking (SCR-021)**: six drop targets (N/S/E/W/centre-tabify/float) highlighted with a 4 px accent and a translucent preview of the resulting rectangle; invalid-drop feedback ("Can't dock here"); drag preview on CSS transforms only; exactly one layout mutation on drop.
- **Keyboard docking**: "Move panel" in CMP-216 opens a directional chooser (left/right/top/bottom/tab-into) driving `resolveDirectionalMove`; splitters resize by `Alt+Shift+arrows`; a live region announces "Chart moved to bottom-right".
- **Panel picker (SCR-024)**: grouped catalogue from the pane registry with one-line descriptions, thumbnails and chips ("requires recording", "(estimated)" via CMP-227, "owner only"); fuzzy search (CMP-213); category headings as real headings; disabled entries state their reason; placement is previewed before insert; adding announces where the panel landed.
- **Panel menu (SCR-028)**: Settings…, Duplicate, Move to ▸, Float, Full screen, Sync group ▸, Reset settings, Copy panel link, Close — identical for every panel kind so muscle memory transfers; built from a static descriptor (no per-open API call); opens from the ⋮ button, `Shift+F10` and the context-menu key; disabled items show a reason; destructive items grouped last.
- **Hide/restore**: hiding a panel removes it from the grid but keeps it in the view menu and on its hotkey; minimised-to-tab state.
- **Full screen / maximise**: `F11` maximises the active panel; restoring returns it to its exact prior slot.
- **Floating windows (SCR-027, Electron only)**: pop a panel into an OS window with a slim title bar carrying panel name, symbol and environment badge (**CMP-215**, **CMP-075**), always-on-top option, "return to workspace" re-dock into the origin slot, per-workspace position persistence, and recovery to the primary display when a monitor disappears. The floating window participates in sync groups through the same in-process bus.
- **Browser fallback**: in the non-Electron build the float control degrades to a maximised overlay panel with an explanatory note — hidden-with-explanation, never a dead control.
- Panel-too-small state: below a pane's minimum size, the compact view is shown with its explanatory label (SCR-021).

## Out of scope
- The content of any panel; this Story mounts registry entries.
- Persisting the resulting layout — **E15-S03**.
- Sync group assignment UI beyond the menu entry that opens it — **E15-S04**.
- Multi-window *data* architecture (each floating window is its own renderer with its own GL context per SCR-027; the shared-worker WS client that makes that affordable is **E17**/**E11**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dragging a panel to an edge docks it with a preview
  Given a workspace with a chart and a DOM panel
  When the DOM panel is dragged toward the right edge
  Then the east drop zone highlights with a preview of the resulting rectangle
  And on release the panel docks there with exactly one layout mutation, and its width is part of the layout tree

Scenario: Every dock operation is reachable by keyboard
  Given a keyboard-only trader focused on a panel header
  When they open the panel menu with Shift+F10 and choose Move panel, then a direction
  Then the panel moves to the same position a pointer drop to that zone would have produced
  And a live region announces the new position once

Scenario: Invalid drops are refused visibly
  When a panel is dragged over a target that cannot accept it
  Then the cursor and an inline label state "Can't dock here" and releasing makes no change to the layout

Scenario: Hiding a panel keeps it recoverable
  When the tape panel is hidden
  Then it disappears from the grid and remains restorable from the view menu and by its hotkey, with its settings intact on restore

Scenario: Floating in Electron and re-docking
  Given the Electron shell and a chart panel
  When the panel is floated
  Then a separate window opens with the panel name, symbol and environment badge in its title, it can be set always-on-top, it still follows its sync group
  And re-docking returns it to its origin slot; its position is restored on the next launch of that workspace

Scenario: The browser build explains rather than pretends
  Given the app is running in a browser, not Electron
  When the trader opens the panel menu
  Then the float control is not offered as a working action, and an explanation states that floating windows require the desktop app

Scenario: A missing monitor does not lose the panel
  Given a floating panel was positioned on a second display that is no longer connected
  When the workspace is next opened
  Then the panel is restored onto the primary display rather than off-screen

Scenario: Unavailable panel kinds are disabled with a reason
  Given a panel kind whose feature is not enabled for this role or requires a recorded symbol
  When the panel picker is opened
  Then that entry is shown disabled with its reason stated, and it cannot be added
```

## Technical notes / design
Drag is pointer-events based with the preview drawn purely by CSS transform — the tree is not touched until drop, which is what keeps a drag from costing a layout pass per pointer move (SCR-021 performance line).

The float boundary is the interesting one. In Electron a floated panel is a separate renderer process with its own GL context (SCR-027), so the sync bus must reach across windows: R1 does this by keeping the workspace's sync state in the main process and mirroring it, rather than by attempting shared memory. SCR-027's budget — ≥58 fps across at most 4 GPU-heavy windows — is checked against E15-K01's numbers, and beyond that the shell warns.

Re-dock needs the origin slot to still be meaningful after the layout has changed underneath: store the origin as a pane id plus a fallback zone, and if the origin is gone, dock into the largest compatible container rather than failing.

The panel menu being a static descriptor (SCR-028: "not a per-open API call") is what holds the ≤80 ms open budget and makes the menu identical across panel kinds.

## Test plan
Unit: drop-zone geometry resolution, origin-slot fallback, hidden-panel registry, menu descriptor per kind. Component: drop-zone highlighting states, invalid drop, compact view at minimum size, picker search/filter/disabled reasons, menu keyboard open and roving focus. E2E Playwright (web): drag docking, hide/restore, maximise/restore, keyboard move path, browser float fallback notice. E2E Electron: float, always-on-top, badge presence in every window, re-dock, position persistence across relaunch, disconnected-display recovery (simulated). A11y: axe on SCR-021/024/027/028; manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass of the keyboard move flow and the floating window's independent focus scope; assertion that the floating window title includes the environment word (CMP-215). Perf: panel mount ≤150 ms, menu open ≤80 ms, drag at 60 fps, 4-window Electron FPS against SCR-027's ≥58 fps.

## Security notes
Floating windows are the notable surface: every window must repeat the DEMO/LIVE environment badge in its chrome and in its OS title (CMP-215, SCR-027) so a trader can never act in a detached window without knowing its environment — this is a safety control, and its absence is a release blocker, not a cosmetic bug. Windows are created with `nodeIntegration` off and `contextIsolation` on, inheriting E10's shell hardening; no window may be opened from untrusted input (an imported layout naming a panel kind is validated against the registry by E15-T02 before any window is created). "Copy panel link" produces an in-app route reference containing no tokens, no account ids and no user ids. Panel titles are user-influenced content rendered as text.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this Story carries the Epic's heaviest a11y load. No layout operation may be pointer-only (CMP-214, mandatory): the directional chooser is the keyboard twin of every drop zone. The panel menu is a full keyboard menu with type-ahead and shortcut hints, reachable via `Shift+F10` and the context-menu key (SCR-028). The picker's categories are real headings, each entry's one-line description is read with its name, and insertion announces placement ("CVD added to the right column", SCR-024). Each floating window is an independent document with its own title, skip link and focus scope, its title naming panel, symbol and environment (SCR-027). Splitters resize with `Alt+Shift+arrows`. All announcements are polite and fire once per committed operation.

## Performance notes
Panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-024, CMP-080); menu open ≤80 ms (SCR-028); drag preview CSS-transform only with one mutation on drop (SCR-021); newly added panels subscribe WS topics only after mount, and the picker pre-warms nothing (SCR-024); Electron multi-window target ≥58 fps across ≤4 GPU-heavy windows (SCR-027), validated against E15-K01.

## Observability
`layout.panel_added {type, placement}`, `layout.panel_removed`, `layout.panel_moved {method: 'pointer'|'keyboard'}`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `panel.redocked`, `window.opened`, `window.closed`, `panel.context_menu_opened`. Tracking `method` on moves is deliberate: it tells us whether the keyboard path is actually usable or merely present.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test, including the Electron-only ones.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on docking, picker, menu and float modules.
- [ ] SCR-021, SCR-024, SCR-027, SCR-028 design tickets Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waivers recorded; their sign-off checklists verified in the built UI.
- [ ] axe-core green on all four screens; manual screen-reader pass of the keyboard move flow signed off by the a11y specialist.
- [ ] Environment badge present in every floating window, verified by an Electron E2E assertion.
- [ ] Perf budgets recorded (mount, menu, drag, 4-window FPS).
- [ ] PRs ≤400 LOC each, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (tree, drop resolution, registry), **E10** (Electron shell, window management, environment badge, view menu), **E05** (Menu, Dialog, Combobox, Card, Drawer tokens). Blocks **E15-S08**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-docking-and-float`

## References

title: SyncBus: cross-pane crosshair, symbol, interval and time-range propagation
body:
## Context
US-LAY-003's NFR is "sync propagation ≤1 frame", and SCR-023 is more specific about how: "crosshair sync must not trigger a React re-render — it dispatches straight into the engine (≤4 ms across 6 panels)". A crosshair moves on every pointer event; routing that through application state would put a React commit on the pointer path and blow the frame budget the moment a fourth pane joined.

The engine side already anticipates this. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2: "charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, propagated once per frame after input integration (never re-entrantly)". `ChartOptions` carries `syncGroup?: string` and the engine emits a `sync` event carrying `{ groupId, timeRange, crosshair }` at ≤1/frame (§6). This Task builds the bus that connects those emitters to those consumers, and **CMP-196 MultiChartLinker** is its non-visual React binding.

The hard part is not fan-out; it is not looping. A propagates to B, B emits, B propagates back to A. The engine's "never re-entrantly" wording is the contract this Task must actually implement.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `SyncBus` in the app layer (not in `packages/dock`, not in the engine): group registry, per-axis membership, and a publish path that runs **once per animation frame**, after input integration, never during a pointer handler.
- Axes, independently toggleable per group, matching SCR-023's control set: `symbol`, `interval`, `crosshair`, `timeRange`, `drawings` (same-symbol only), `scale` (the last delegated to **E15-S05**), plus `account/group` selection reserved for R3.
- Loop suppression: an origin token on every propagation so a pane never re-emits a value it was just given; a per-frame coalescing buffer so N updates in one frame become one dispatch per subscriber; an assertion (dev builds) that fires if re-entrancy is ever observed.
- Timestamp-based crosshair alignment, not index-based: panes on different intervals align by time, and a pane whose interval has no bar at that timestamp shows the crosshair at the containing bar — SCR-023's "Chart 3 has a different interval — crosshair sync will align by timestamp" warning is driven from this.
- **CMP-196 MultiChartLinker**: the non-visual hook binding a DockGrid pane to its group, subscribing/unsubscribing on mount/unmount and on group change, with zero renders of its own.
- Persistence hooks: group membership and axis flags are read from and written to the layout (`layouts.crosshair_sync`, `layouts.symbol_sync`, `layouts.level_sync` plus per-pane group id in `pane_config`), so E15-S03 saves them without special-casing.
- A headless test harness with fake engine instances so fan-out, coalescing and loop suppression are unit-testable without a GPU.

## Out of scope
- The sync configuration UI (SCR-023, CMP-218) — **E15-S04**.
- Price-scale linking semantics and the incompatible-link refusal — **E15-S05**.
- Drawing synchronisation *content* (which drawings, how they merge) — **E14** owns drawings; this bus only carries the event on the same symbol.
- Cross-device or cross-window sync (a floated Electron window participates through the same in-process bus; two browser tabs do not sync in R1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crosshair propagates within one frame without a React render
  Given panes 1, 2 and 3 are in group A with crosshair sync enabled
  When the pointer moves across pane 1
  Then panes 2 and 3 show the crosshair at the same timestamp on the next frame
  And a React profiler recording of the interaction shows zero component renders attributable to crosshair movement

Scenario: Propagation does not loop
  Given two panes in the same group with every axis enabled
  When a symbol change originates in pane 1
  Then pane 2 applies it exactly once, pane 1 receives no echo, and the dev-build re-entrancy assertion does not fire

Scenario: Groups are isolated
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A and pane 3 is in group B
  When any synced value changes in pane 1
  Then pane 2 updates and pane 3 is completely untouched, including its crosshair, symbol, interval and time range

Scenario: Axes are independent
  Given a group with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When the symbol changes in one pane
  Then every member changes symbol and each member keeps its own interval

Scenario: Mismatched intervals align by timestamp
  Given a 1m pane and a 1h pane in one crosshair-synced group
  When the crosshair sits on the 14:37 bar in the 1m pane
  Then the 1h pane highlights the 14:00 bar that contains that timestamp, not the 37th bar from its right edge

Scenario: Budget holds at six panes
  Given six chart panes in one group with all axes enabled
  When the crosshair is swept for 5 seconds
  Then total sync work stays under 4 ms per frame and no frame exceeds 16.6 ms attributable to sync

Scenario: Leaving a group is clean
  Given a pane is removed from its group or unmounted mid-sweep
  Then it stops receiving updates immediately, no listener leaks, and the remaining members continue unaffected
```

## Technical notes / design
One bus per workspace, keyed by group id, holding weak references to engine handles rather than React components — the bus must outlive no component and hold up no unmount.

Publishing is scheduled, not immediate: a pointer handler writes into a per-frame slot and requests a frame; the flush runs after input integration, exactly as §4.2 specifies. That single choice gives coalescing, ordering and loop-freedom together, and it is why the bus lives in the app rather than inside the engine, which has no view of sibling instances.

The origin token is the pane id, not a boolean flag: with three-plus members, a boolean "applying" flag suppresses legitimate concurrent updates, while an origin token suppresses only the echo.

E15-K01's finding on propagation cost at 6 and 16 panes decides whether the flush stays on the main thread; if it recommends otherwise, the bus's scheduled-flush shape makes moving it a contained change.

## Test plan
Unit (headless, fake engines): fan-out per axis, group isolation, loop suppression with 2/3/6 members, coalescing (10 updates in one frame → 1 dispatch), timestamp alignment across intervals, unsubscribe on unmount and on group change, no listener leaks over 1000 mount/unmount cycles. Integration: real engine instances in a 4-pane DockGrid — crosshair sweep with a React profiler assertion of zero renders. Perf: the 6-pane sweep against the 4 ms budget, recorded. E2E: Playwright — assign panes to groups A and B, verify isolation and timestamp alignment visually via engine state, not pixels.

## Security notes
Purely in-process client state: no network, no persistence of anything beyond the flags already covered by E15-T01's validation. The only consideration worth stating is isolation — sync must never be a channel by which one pane reads another's account or environment binding, so the bus carries an explicit allow-list of axis payload shapes (`symbol`, `interval`, `timeRange`, `crosshair`, `priceLevel`) and rejects anything else, keeping R3's account-scoped sync a deliberate future addition rather than an accident.

## Accessibility notes
Sync changes are not announced per movement — a crosshair sweep announcing in every pane would be unusable. Announcements are limited to membership and axis changes ("Chart 2 joined sync group A"), emitted by **E15-S04**'s UI, not by the bus. The bus exposes the current group and axes so each panel's accessible name can include them (CMP-218 requires membership be conveyed by name and letter, never colour alone).

## Performance notes
≤1 frame propagation (US-LAY-003 NFR); ≤4 ms total across 6 panes (SCR-023); zero React renders on the crosshair path; ≤1 `sync` emission per frame per group (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §6). Measured against E15-K01's pane-count curve and benchmark B6.

## Observability
`sync.group_joined`, `sync.group_left`, `sync.axis_toggled` (emitted by the UI, defined here). Dev-build counters: dispatches per frame, suppressed echoes, re-entrancy assertion hits — surfaced in the engine debug overlay so a regression is visible while developing, not only in CI.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the SyncBus module.
- [ ] Zero-React-render assertion for the crosshair path present in CI, not just measured once.
- [ ] 6-pane perf number recorded against the 4 ms budget.
- [ ] CMP-196 Storybook/test entries per the catalogue.
- [ ] Re-entrancy assertion present in dev builds and documented.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (panes must exist in a tree with stable ids), **E11** (`syncGroup`, the `sync` event and crosshair dispatch). Blocks **E15-S04**, **E15-S05**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-sync-bus`

## References
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2 pane synchronisation, §6 `sync` event, `ChartOptions.syncGroup`, R8, B6; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-003, US-LAY-004; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-049; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-196, CMP-218; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`).


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-196, CMP-218, SCR-023, SCR-049
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e15-sync-bus`
- PR title: `E15-T03: SyncBus: cross-pane crosshair, symbol, interval and time-range propagation`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-T03)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/tech, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, perf, qa

**Done means**
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the SyncBus module.
- [ ] Zero-React-render assertion for the crosshair path present in CI, not just measured once.
- [ ] 6-pane perf number recorded against the 4 ms budget.
- [ ] CMP-196 Storybook/test entries per the catalogue.
- [ ] Re-entrancy assertion present in dev builds and documented.

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not widen a performance budget or edit a benchmark baseline to make a regression pass (AGENTS.md §8).

title: STRIDE threat model for workspaces, layout persistence and export/import
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and the planning brief require a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes a threat-model kickoff a DoR item for any epic touching persisted user data. E15 looks cosmetic and is not: it introduces a **user-authored document that is persisted server-side and exchanged between users as a file**. That is a classic injection and deserialization surface, an authorization surface (`workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, scope `self`), and a stored-XSS surface (workspace and layout names rendered in tabs, menus and window titles).

US-LAY-007 makes it sharper: workspaces are exported as JSON and imported by *another user*, with the explicit requirement that the file contains no secrets and no account bindings, and that account-scoped elements are dropped with a report on import. An import path that trusts its input is how a "layout file" becomes a foothold.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/security/threat-models/e15-layouts-workspaces.md`, built from a data-flow diagram covering: browser dock state → debounced `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{id}` → API → Postgres (`workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, `chart_templates`); export `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` → file → another user's import → validation → dock state; and the local autosave used for crash-restore.
- **STRIDE enumeration** per element and per flow, with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — importing a file that claims another user's workspace id or ownership; a floating window (`SCR-027`) misrepresenting DEMO/LIVE.
  - **Tampering** — a crafted layout document injecting unexpected pane kinds, oversized grids, cyclic/deeply nested trees, or a `chart_template_id` pointing at another user's template; tampering with the local autosave.
  - **Repudiation** — layout events are analytics-only by design (`SCR-021`); confirm nothing security-relevant hides in them and that `workspace.deleted`/`workspace.exported` are audited per `21-database-schema.md`.
  - **Information disclosure** — secrets, tokens, account ids, balances or symbol watchlists leaking through export files, window titles, panel names, error messages, or a cross-user `workspaceId` probe distinguishing 403 from 404.
  - **Denial of service** — unbounded pane counts, huge layout documents, import zip-bomb-equivalents (deeply nested JSON), write-storms against the 2-second debounce, and per-user workspace/layout count growth.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — an imported workspace causing a viewer to mount an owner-only panel, or a pane binding to an account the user cannot read; `workspaces:*` scope `self` being bypassed by a nested id.
- **Risk rating** (likelihood × impact) with the mitigation owner and the ticket that implements each mitigation; anything unmitigated is an explicit accepted risk with Owner sign-off.
- **Security requirements list** `SR-E15-nn` that `E15-X02` (abuse cases), `E15-X03` (SAST/DAST) and `E15-X04` (review) test against.

## Out of scope
- Auth and session design itself (E09) — consumed as an assumption, with the assumption stated.
- WS transport security (E17).
- Threats of the panels' own content (footprint, DOM, order ticket) — their epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model covers every flow
  Given the data-flow diagram
  Then every trust boundary crossing has at least one STRIDE entry, and every entry has a rating and a named mitigation owner

Scenario: Export contents are constrained by requirement, not by hope
  When the model analyses the export flow
  Then it produces an explicit allow-list of exportable fields and a denial rule for secrets, tokens, account ids and user ids
  And that allow-list is referenced by the export implementation ticket

Scenario: Failure case - an unmitigated high risk blocks the epic
  Given a High-rated threat with no mitigation
  Then the epic cannot reach Done until the mitigation ships or the Owner records an accepted risk with a review date

Scenario: Edge case - import from a newer schema version
  Given a workspace file exported by a newer app version
  Then the model requires refusal with both versions stated, not partial application, and treats partial application as a tampering risk

Scenario: Model is reviewed
  When the model is published
  Then it carries review from the Security engineer and the Architect, and is linked from the E15 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Treat the imported workspace document as **fully untrusted input** even though it came from a colleague: validate against a strict JSON Schema (additionalProperties false), bound depth, node count, string lengths and numeric ranges before any of it reaches application state.
- Ids in an imported file must be *regenerated*, never honoured: importing must not let a caller assert `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `chart_template_id` or account references. This single rule kills most of the spoofing and EoP branches.
- Names are rendered in tabs, menus, live-region announcements and OS window titles — the model must require output encoding at every one of those sinks, not only the React ones (an Electron window title is not React).
- Bound the document: max panes per layout, max layouts per workspace, max workspaces per user, max serialized size; `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 already gives uniqueness constraints, and the model should demand 422 rather than 500 on violation.
- Note the RBAC shape from `24-internal-schemas.md` §3063: `workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, granted to owner/manager/viewer for *their own* resources — the model must verify "own" is enforced in the query, not in the handler's afterthought.

## Test plan
- The model is validated by review plus a tabletop: walk three attack narratives end-to-end (malicious import, cross-user probe, layout write-storm) and confirm the model predicted each.
- Every `SR-E15-nn` requirement must be testable; any requirement no one can write a test for is rewritten.
- Hand the requirement list to `E15-X02` and confirm each maps to at least one abuse case.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security artefact; its own hygiene matters: the document names concrete endpoints and tables and avoids hand-waving categories.
- Explicitly record the assumption set inherited from E09 (authenticated session, deny-by-default RBAC, audit log) so a later change to those assumptions triggers a re-review.
- Classify a workspace export as *user-confidential*: it reveals which symbols a trader watches and how they trade, which is sensitive even without credentials.

## Accessibility notes
- Security controls must not be pointer-only or vision-only: the import rejection report, the dropped-elements report and the version-mismatch refusal must be text, keyboard-reachable and announced — a security message no one can perceive is not a control.
- The DEMO/LIVE environment indicator is a safety control; the model treats degrading it (including in floating windows and for screen-reader users) as a spoofing risk.

## Performance notes
- Validation must be bounded and cheap: schema validation of a 2 MB layout file completes in ≤500 ms in a worker (`SCR-026`) and must not be a DoS amplifier itself; the model records this as a requirement.
- Rate limits on workspace writes must protect the API without breaking the legitimate 2-second debounce; the model states the intended limit so `E15-X02` can test both sides.

## Observability
- Requires that import rejections emit `layout.import_rejected{reason}` with a bounded reason enum, and that repeated rejections from one user are visible in the ops dashboard as a possible probing signal.
- Requires that `workspace.deleted` and `workspace.exported` reach the append-only audit log, not merely analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Threat model published with DFD, full STRIDE enumeration, ratings, owners and `SR-E15-nn` requirements.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] Every High/Critical threat has a mitigation ticket or a written accepted risk with a review date.
- [ ] Requirement list handed to `E15-X02` and `E15-X03` and referenced by the export/import story.
- [ ] Linked from the E15 epic and from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`'s per-epic index.

## Dependencies
- `E15-S02` (persistence shape must exist to model it); E09 auth/RBAC assumptions; `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1; `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`.

`chore/e15-threat-model`

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`

title: Functional pack for cross-pane sync groups and price-scale linking
body:
## Context
Cross-pane sync (US-LAY-003) and scale linking (US-LAY-004) are the features most likely to produce subtle, hard-to-reproduce wrongness: a crosshair that aligns by index instead of timestamp, a group that leaks into another group, a drawing that syncs onto a pane showing a different symbol, or a linked price scale that silently rescales a pane the trader is reading. Those are analysis-integrity bugs (risk R7 in spirit, R2 in cost) and they are invisible in a screenshot.

`SCR-023` specifies the contract: independent toggles for symbol / interval / crosshair / time range / drawings / y-scale / account-group; membership of groups A/B/C with letter-plus-colour badges; runtime over a local sync bus with no server round-trip; propagation that must not trigger a React re-render (≤4 ms across 6 panes). This ticket builds the pack that proves it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/specs/layouts/sync-groups.spec.ts` plus a component-level harness suite under `web/src/features/layout/__tests__/syncBus.spec.ts`:
  - **Axis independence**: for each of the seven toggles, enabling it propagates exactly that axis and nothing else (a 7 × 7 matrix asserting the off-diagonal is inert).
  - **Group scoping**: panes in group A and group B; changes in A never reach B or ungrouped panes; `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` assignment and `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync.
  - **Crosshair alignment by timestamp**: a 1 m pane and a 5 m pane on the same symbol; moving the crosshair at t aligns the 5 m pane to the bar *containing* t, and the `SCR-023` conflicting-interval notice is shown.
  - **Drawing sync same-symbol rule**: a drawing created in a BTCUSDT pane appears in the other BTCUSDT pane in the group and does **not** appear in the ETHUSDT pane.
  - **Scale linking** (`SCR-043`, CMP-188/CMP-189): linked panes on the same symbol share price-axis zoom; unlinking restores independence and the axis shows the unlinked state; linking panes with very different price magnitudes is refused with an explanation and percentage-scale is suggested.
  - **Persistence**: group membership, per-axis toggles and per-pane link state round-trip through `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}` and survive a reload.
- A **render-purity assertion**: instrumentation counting React commits during a crosshair sweep across 6 panes; the spec fails if commits exceed the documented zero-React-render expectation.
- A regression fixture `six-pane-sync` (3 symbols × 2 intervals) reused by `E15-Q04` and `E15-Q08`.

## Out of scope
- Drawing tool correctness itself (E14) — this pack asserts propagation, not geometry.
- Indicator set sync beyond what E13 already exposes.
- Sub-frame timing measurement under load — `E15-Q04`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Selective sync propagates exactly one axis
  Given panes P1 and P2 are in sync group A with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When P1 is switched from BTCUSDT 1m to ETHUSDT
  Then P2 shows ETHUSDT and keeps its own interval
  And no other pane property on P2 changes

Scenario: Groups do not leak
  Given P1,P2 are in group A and P3,P4 are in group B
  When the crosshair moves in P1
  Then P2 shows a crosshair at the same timestamp and P3,P4 show none

Scenario: Failure case - incompatible scale link is refused
  Given a BTCUSDT pane near 60000 and a pane on a symbol near 0.5
  When the trader links their price scales
  Then linking is refused with an explanation naming the magnitude difference and offering percentage scale
  And neither pane's existing scale is mutated

Scenario: Edge case - crosshair across mismatched intervals
  Given a 1m pane and a 5m pane are crosshair-synced
  When the crosshair sits on the 1m bar at 10:03
  Then the 5m pane highlights the 10:00-10:05 bar and shows the interval-mismatch notice

Scenario: Group identity is not colour-only
  When a pane joins group B
  Then its badge renders the letter "B" as text alongside the colour
  And a screen reader announces the group change
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drive the sync bus directly in the component-level suite (fast, deterministic, covers the 7×7 matrix) and keep the E2E spec to a representative subset — a full matrix in Playwright would be slow and flaky for no extra signal.
- Assert timestamps, never pixel positions, for crosshair alignment; pixel assertions break on any axis-margin change.
- Persisted sync state lives in the layout document (`layouts` / `layout_panes` per `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1), not in a separate table — the round-trip assertion must read it back through the API to catch serializer drift.

## Test plan
- Component suite runs on every PR (sub-second); E2E subset joins the `E15-Q02` suite.
- Manual exploratory addendum: one 30-minute charter driving six panes with mixed symbols/intervals looking for propagation ordering artefacts (e.g. the last pane in a group lagging a frame).
- Negative verification: temporarily broaden a group filter locally and confirm the group-scoping specs fail.

## Security notes
- Sync is client-local (no server round-trip per `SCR-023`); a spec asserts that no network request is issued during a crosshair sweep, which also prevents a future regression from leaking per-move telemetry about what a trader is inspecting.
- Account/group sync (the "Selected account/group" toggle) must never cause a pane to display data for an account the user cannot read; a case asserts the pane refuses and shows a permission notice rather than rendering.

## Accessibility notes
- Badge text assertion (letter present, not colour alone) per `05-accessibility-standard.md` and the `SCR-023` sign-off checklist.
- Group change announcements are asserted via the live region text.
- Sync toggles are reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus; the popover traps and restores focus correctly.

## Performance notes
- Propagation budget ≤1 frame (US-LAY-003 NFR) and ≤4 ms across 6 panes (`SCR-023`); the pack asserts these with the app's performance marks as a guard rail, with the authoritative measurement in `E15-Q04`.
- React commit count during a sweep is asserted to stay at the documented floor — this is the cheapest early warning that someone routed sync through component state.

## Observability
- Assert `sync.group_created`, `sync.group_changed`, `sync.axis_toggled`, `sync.panel_joined_group`, `sync.panel_left_group` fire with the documented payloads.
- The harness dumps the sync-bus event log on failure so an ordering bug is diagnosable from CI output alone.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Component suite covering the full 7×7 axis matrix merged and green.
- [ ] E2E subset merged into the layouts suite and green on web and Electron.
- [ ] `six-pane-sync` fixture published and referenced by `E15-Q04` and `E15-Q08`.
- [ ] Render-purity assertion in place and passing.
- [ ] Exploratory charter executed once and findings filed.

## Dependencies
- `E15-Q01` (case ids), `E15-S03` (sync), `E15-S04` (scale linking); E14 for a drawing to propagate.

## Branch
`chore/e15-qa-sync-pack`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-003, US-LAY-004
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-043, SCR-049
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-196, CMP-218, CMP-188, CMP-189

title: Saved workspaces: switcher, settings, restore and conflict handling
body:
## Context
This Story is where R1 exit criterion 5 is actually earned: "Chart state (symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout) survives reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss." It implements **US-LAY-002** — save a workspace as "EU session" storing "panes, symbols, intervals, indicators, footprint settings, DOM config, panels and hotkey profile"; restore "including scroll position and pane sizes, with data loading progressively"; and the failure case that matters most, a delisted symbol: "the pane opens in an explicit error state naming the symbol, and the rest of the workspace still loads". Its NFR is a hard number: restore to interactive in ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache.

Surfaces: **SCR-020** workspace tabs and save/reset chrome, **SCR-011** workspace switcher (CMP-073), **SCR-025** Workspace settings modal, **SCR-029** Unsaved-changes / layout-conflict dialog, **SCR-150** global boot/restore state. Storage and transport are already built by **E15-T01**.

The conflict case is real, not theoretical: the same user runs the terminal in Electron and a browser tab, or two monitors' windows. The OpenAPI description of `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{layoutId}` says why `If-Match` exists — "prevents a stale tab from clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window" — and SCR-029 specifies what the user sees when it fires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Workspace switcher** (CMP-073, SCR-011/SCR-020 tabs): list, create, duplicate, rename, delete, reorder, set default; the unsaved marker `*` on the tab.
- **Save semantics**: `Ctrl+S` saves, `Ctrl+Shift+S` saves as; autosave of layout changes with a 2 s debounce sending a full `PUT` with `If-Match`; a save that changes nothing does not write.
- **Restore**: on boot, load the default (or last-used) workspace via one `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}` and mount panes progressively — layout frame first, then each pane's data — so the skeleton is on screen long before the last kline page arrives (SCR-020: "loading skeleton, no data fetch until mount"; SCR-150).
- **Per-pane state captured**: symbol, interval, chart template, indicator preset ids, drawings scope, scroll/visible-range, pane-specific config (footprint/DOM settings as those Epics land), sync group and axes, scale mode — all into `layout_panes` columns and `pane_config` per `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1.
- **Per-workspace theme and density** (roadmap §5.2 scope line) plus default symbol/interval and "open on startup", edited in **SCR-025**; saving applies without a full workspace remount, only re-resolving panes bound to a changed default.
- **Delete guards** (SCR-025): deleting requires typing the workspace name; the last workspace cannot be deleted ("You need at least one workspace.").
- **Conflict handling (SCR-029)**: on 412, show the conflict variant with a plain-text side-by-side summary of differences (panel count, symbols, sync groups) and [Keep mine] / [Load theirs]; on navigation with unsaved changes, show the unsaved variant with Save / Discard / Cancel, Esc mapping to Cancel and never to Discard, and no default destructive button.
- **Crash restore**: after an abnormal exit the workspace is restored from the last autosave with a notice naming the time ("Restored your layout from 14:02").
- **Missing/delisted symbol**: the pane mounts into an explicit error state naming the symbol with a rebind action; siblings load normally; the workspace stays savable.

## Out of scope
- Export/import files — **E15-S07**.
- Server-pushed conflict notification over WS — R1 detects conflicts on write only.
- Sharing a workspace with another user — R5 collaboration.
- Account/environment binding of a workspace — **E27/E44**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full-fidelity save and restore
  Given a 4-pane workspace with distinct symbols, intervals, indicator presets, drawings, sync groups and scroll positions
  When it is saved as "EU session", the app is quit and relaunched, and the workspace is opened
  Then every pane restores with the same symbol, interval, indicators, drawings, sync group, scale mode, size and visible time range
  And it reaches interactive within 3 s from warm cache

Scenario: Progressive loading, not a blocking wait
  When a saved workspace is opened
  Then the layout skeleton with named panel frames is visible before any market data has arrived, and each pane fills in independently as its data loads

Scenario: A delisted symbol degrades one pane only
  Given a saved pane references a symbol that no longer exists on the exchange
  When the workspace is restored
  Then that pane shows an error state naming the symbol and offering to rebind it
  And the other three panes load and are fully interactive, and the workspace can still be saved

Scenario: A stale window cannot clobber a newer arrangement
  Given the workspace is open in two windows and window B has saved a change
  When window A's autosave fires with its stale token
  Then the API returns 412, window A shows the conflict dialog with a text summary of the differences, and nothing is overwritten until the user chooses

Scenario: Unsaved changes are never silently discarded
  Given the active workspace has unsaved layout changes
  When the trader switches workspaces or closes the app
  Then the unsaved-changes dialog offers Save layout, Discard changes and Cancel, no destructive button is the default, and Esc maps to Cancel

Scenario: The last workspace cannot be deleted
  Given the user has exactly one workspace
  When they attempt to delete it
  Then the action is refused with "You need at least one workspace." and the workspace remains

Scenario: Crash restore is disclosed, not silent
  Given the app exited abnormally after an autosave at 14:02
  When it next starts
  Then the layout is restored and a notice states that it was restored from 14:02

Scenario: Changing density does not remount the workspace
  When the density is changed from cosy to compact in workspace settings
  Then panel chrome re-renders at the new density, no WebGL context is recreated, and no pane refetches data
```

## Technical notes / design
Save is full replacement of the layout aggregate, not a diff — the client always holds the whole tree, and `PUT` with `If-Match` gives us conflict detection for free. The 2 s debounce means a drag that takes four seconds produces two writes, which is fine; what matters is that a write is never issued mid-drag.

Restore ordering is the whole 3 s NFR. Mount the tree first (cheap, no network), then let each pane fetch its own history in parallel with a per-pane skeleton. Nothing waits on the slowest pane. Warm cache means E12's kline cache is populated; the number is measured in that condition, as the NFR states.

The delisted-symbol case is handled at mount, not at save: symbols are validated against E08's instrument list when a pane resolves, and an unknown symbol produces an error pane rather than an exception that takes the tree down. The error pane is a first-class registry entry so it participates in focus order and announcements like any other panel.

Crash detection is a clean-shutdown flag written on graceful exit; its absence at boot means the last autosave is a crash restore and must be disclosed (SCR-020's "Restored your layout from 14:02" state).

Density and theme are token-level: they change CSS custom properties from E05's design system, which is why they can apply without a remount.

## Test plan
Unit: serialisation of pane state to `LayoutInput` and back, debounce behaviour, dirty tracking, ETag handling, clean-shutdown flag. Component: switcher CRUD, settings modal validation (name 1..40, unique, delete confirmation by typing the name), conflict and unsaved dialog variants. Integration: save→reload→restore fidelity across all captured fields against a real API; 412 path; last-workspace guard. E2E (Playwright web + Electron): the full exit-criterion-5 script — build a 4-pane workspace, reload the page, restart the app, relaunch Electron, assert zero loss each time; delisted-symbol restore using a fixture instrument list; two-window conflict. Perf: restore-to-interactive ≤3 s from warm cache at 4 panes, measured and recorded. A11y: axe on SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-025, SCR-029; screen-reader pass of the conflict dialog (`role="alertdialog"`, verb-labelled buttons) and the boot/restore announcement.

## Security notes
All access is `scope: self` and enforced server-side by E15-T01; the client never sends a user id and cannot address another user's workspace. Workspace names and pane labels are user content rendered as text, length-capped at the boundary. The clean-shutdown flag and any autosave cache stored locally must contain no credentials — layouts reference symbols and preset ids only, never keys or tokens — which is also what makes the same payload safe to export in E15-S07. Data classification: user preference data. STRIDE note: the conflict path must fail closed — a 412 never results in a blind retry that overwrites, since that would turn a benign race into silent data loss.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Workspace tabs follow the tabs pattern with the unsaved `*` also conveyed in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"), never by the glyph alone. SCR-029 is `role="alertdialog"` with three explicitly verb-labelled buttons ("Save layout", "Discard changes", "Cancel"), no default destructive action, Esc mapped to Cancel; the difference summary is text, not a canvas. SCR-025 is a standard modal form with grouped fieldsets and an error summary linking to fields. Boot/restore announces progress politely on SCR-150 and announces the crash-restore notice once. Each restoring pane's skeleton carries an accessible name so a screen reader hears "Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, loading" rather than an unlabelled region.

## Performance notes
Restore to interactive ≤3 s for 4 panes from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR); one `GET` per workspace, never per pane; panes mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s (SCR-020); autosave debounced 2 s; settings changes apply without remount, re-resolving only affected panes (SCR-025); conflict dialog appears within 300 ms of detection (SCR-029).

## Observability

title: Cross-pane sync configuration: groups and per-axis toggles (SCR-023)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-003** — "sync symbol, interval, crosshair, time range and drawings across panes, so that multi-timeframe reading is coherent" — with its three scenarios: crosshair sync moves at the same timestamp across a group; selective sync lets symbol propagate while interval stays per pane; sync groups A and B are isolated and each pane's group is labelled. NFR: propagation ≤1 frame, groups persisted in the workspace.

**E15-T03** built the bus and proved the budget. This Story is the control surface: **SCR-023** Multi-chart sync configuration and **CMP-218** SyncMenu, with the per-pane badge that makes membership visible at a glance, plus the group entry in **CMP-216**'s panel menu and the shell's `sync` menu on SCR-020.

One design constraint is non-negotiable and appears in three documents: group membership is conveyed by **letter and name**, never by colour alone (SCR-023 "the badge is text ('A')", CMP-218, and the SCR-020 design checklist "symbol-group colour tags carry a letter/number too").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-023** popover/modal from the shell's sync menu: group selector (A / B / C / none) and independent toggles for **symbol**, **interval**, **crosshair**, **time range**, **drawings (same symbol only)** and **Y-scale** (the last handing off to E15-S05), plus a list of the panels currently in the selected group.
- **CMP-218 SyncMenu** as the per-panel control, reachable from the panel header and from CMP-216's "Sync group ▸" submenu.
- **Per-pane sync badge**: letter + group name + colour, rendered in the panel header (CMP-082) and included in the panel's accessible name.
- **Hotkeys**: `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` assign the active panel to group A/B/C, `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync — routed through E10's remappable hotkey layer.
- **Persistence**: axis flags to `layouts.crosshair_sync`, `layouts.symbol_sync`, `layouts.level_sync` and group membership into each pane's `pane_config`, saved by E15-S03's autosave; a restored workspace comes back with its groups intact.
- **Mismatch warning**: when group members have different intervals, SCR-023's explanatory notice ("Chart 3 has a different interval — crosshair sync will align by timestamp") is shown in the configuration surface, not as a blocking error.
- **Drawings sync** restricted to same-symbol members, per US-LAY-003's scenario and US-DRAW-009's prohibition on cross-symbol drawing sync.
- Leaving a group resets nothing: a pane keeps its own symbol, interval and settings on exit (SCR-023 design checklist).

## Out of scope
- The propagation machinery, loop suppression and timestamp alignment — **E15-T03**.
- Price-scale linking semantics and the refusal path — **E15-S05**.
- Account/trade-group sync (the "Selected account/group" row in SCR-023's sketch) — **R3**, rendered disabled with a reason in R1.
- Syncing across browser tabs or machines.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crosshair follows across a group by timestamp
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A with crosshair sync enabled and different intervals
  When the crosshair moves in pane 1
  Then pane 2's crosshair sits on the bar containing the same timestamp, within one frame

Scenario: Axes toggle independently
  Given group A has symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When the symbol is changed in any member
  Then every member changes symbol and each keeps its own interval

Scenario: Groups are isolated and labelled
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A and pane 3 is in group B
  Then each pane's header shows its group letter and name, pane 3 is unaffected by any change in group A, and the sync surface lists the members of the selected group

Scenario: Membership is not conveyed by colour alone
  Given a trader who cannot distinguish the group colours
  When they inspect a pane header or hear it announced
  Then the group is identified by letter and name in visible text and in the accessible name

Scenario: Drawings sync only between same-symbol panes
  Given group A contains two BTCUSDT panes and one ETHUSDT pane with drawings sync on
  When a drawing is created on one BTCUSDT pane
  Then it appears on the other BTCUSDT pane and never on the ETHUSDT pane

Scenario: Groups survive a restart
  Given a workspace with groups A and B configured and specific axes enabled
  When it is saved, the app restarted and the workspace reopened
  Then the same panes are in the same groups with the same axis flags

Scenario: Leaving a group changes nothing else
  Given a pane in group A showing ETHUSDT 5m after symbol sync had propagated
  When it is set to no group
  Then it keeps ETHUSDT 5m, its indicators and its visible range, and simply stops following the group

Scenario: Interval mismatch is explained, not blocked
  Given group members have different intervals
  Then the sync surface shows the timestamp-alignment notice and sync continues to work
```

## Technical notes / design
Groups are fixed identities (A, B, C) rather than free-form names: three is what SCR-023 specifies, it maps cleanly to three hotkeys, and it removes a naming UI plus a whole class of collision handling from R1. A pane belongs to at most one group.

Axis flags live at two levels by design — the layout row carries the group defaults that the schema already models (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`), while the per-pane group id lives in `pane_config`. That matches §3.8.1 without inventing a table, and it means E15-S03's save path needs no special case.

The configuration surface never touches the engine directly; it writes flags into the SyncBus, which owns the frame-scheduled dispatch. That separation is why toggling an axis mid-sweep cannot cause a re-entrant update.

The "Selected account/group" row is rendered now and disabled with a reason, rather than omitted, so the R3 addition is a flag flip and the design stays stable.

## Test plan
Unit: flag persistence mapping to schema columns and `pane_config`, group assignment/removal, same-symbol filter for drawings. Component: SCR-023 surface states (no group, group A, all axes on, partial axes — matching CMP-218's Storybook list), the mismatch notice, the disabled account row with its reason. Integration: with real engines and the SyncBus — crosshair across differing intervals, isolation between A and B, restart persistence via E15-S03. E2E: assign groups by hotkey, verify isolation, save/restore. A11y: axe on SCR-023; assertion that group identity appears as text in both the visible badge and the accessible name; contrast check that the group colours are decorative, not load-bearing; announcement fires once on membership change. Perf: toggling axes mid-sweep does not exceed the 4 ms sync budget.

## Security notes
Client-side preference state only, persisted through E15-T01's already-validated layout write path; no new endpoint and no new stored secret. The one boundary worth stating explicitly: sync must not become a channel for account or environment context to leak between panes, which is why the account/trade-group axis is disabled in R1 rather than half-wired — when it lands in R3 it must respect each pane's own RBAC scope rather than inheriting the origin pane's.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, with SC 1.4.1 (Use of Colour) squarely in scope: group membership is text (letter + name) in the badge and in each panel's accessible name, with colour as reinforcement only. Each sync axis is an independently labelled switch (CMP-218), not a combined control. Group changes are announced once, politely ("Chart 2 joined sync group A"); crosshair movement is never announced. The surface is keyboard-operable end to end and the hotkeys are remappable. The interval-mismatch notice is text associated with the control it explains.

## Performance notes
Propagation ≤1 frame (US-LAY-003 NFR), ≤4 ms across 6 panes with all axes on (SCR-023), zero React renders on the crosshair path — all inherited from E15-T03 and re-verified here with the real UI attached, since a badge that re-renders per crosshair move would defeat the whole design.

## Observability
`sync.group_created`, `sync.group_changed`, `sync.axis_toggled {axis, enabled}`, `sync.panel_joined_group`, `sync.panel_left_group`. Axis-toggle analytics tell us which axes traders actually use, which informs whether R2 adds more or removes some.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the sync configuration module.
- [ ] SCR-023 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waiver recorded; its sign-off checklist verified, including the colour+letter pairing and the conflicting-sync warning.
- [ ] axe-core green; colour-independence verified manually.
- [ ] Persistence across restart demonstrated in an E2E run.
- [ ] Sync budget re-measured with the UI attached and recorded.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T03** (SyncBus), **E05** (Toggle, Tag/Chip, FormField, Dialog). Blocks **E15-S05**. Persisted by **E15-S03**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-sync-config`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-003, US-DRAW-009 (cross-symbol prohibition); `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-049, SCR-020 (design checklist), SCR-025; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-218, CMP-196, CMP-011, CMP-004, CMP-040, CMP-082, CMP-216; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-003 row; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`); `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (SC 1.4.1).
