title: Multi-chart grid panel: cells, per-cell binding, maximise and budget prompt
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-011** ("overlay a second symbol or a ratio, so that I can see relative strength") and the multi-symbol half of **US-LAY-001** both land on one surface that no other E15 ticket owns: **SCR-049 Multi-chart grid panel** - a single dock slot hosting 2-9 chart instances with a shared header for grid shape, sync group and a "propagate symbol" toggle. It is the surface traders use for multi-timeframe reading (BTCUSDT 4H / 5m side by side) and multi-symbol context (ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT beneath).

The distinction from the outer dock matters and is the reason this is its own Story: **E15-T02**'s DockGrid arranges *panels* across the workspace, each free-form and independently closable; SCR-049 is a *panel* that internally arranges *cells* on a fixed preset shape, drawn into **one shared WebGL context with scissored viewports** rather than one context per cell. That rendering decision is what keeps four charts inside a single dock slot within budget, and it is measured by **E15-K01**'s pane-count curve.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-049** multi-chart grid panel hosting 2-9 chart cells in one dock slot, with preset shapes 1x2, 2x2, 3x3 and 1+3 plus a custom split, chosen from the panel header.
- **CMP-081 DockGrid / Layout Manager** reused in cell mode for the internal arrangement; **CMP-080 DockPanel** as the hosting panel; **CMP-082 PanelHeader** for the shared header.
- **Per-cell header**: symbol, interval and the sync-group tag (letter + name, per the E15-S04 colour-independence rule), with active-cell focus indication.
- **CMP-196 MultiChartLinker** wired per cell so grid cells participate in the same sync groups as top-level panes - a cell may be in group A while its neighbour is in group B.
- **CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu** in the panel header for the grid shape; **CMP-218 SyncMenu** for the panel-wide sync-group default applied to newly added cells.
- **Propagate symbol** toggle: when on, changing the symbol in any cell changes it in all cells of this panel while each cell keeps its own interval (the multi-timeframe case).
- **Maximise a cell and restore**: `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` maximises the focused cell to fill the panel, `Esc` restores; the grid shape and per-cell bindings are preserved across the round trip.
- **Cell focus**: `Ctrl+Alt+1..9` focuses the Nth cell (SCR-049 a11y line); each cell is a labelled `region` whose accessible name carries symbol, interval and sync group.
- **Degraded state**: when the requested grid exceeds the measured GPU budget from **E15-K01**, the explicit reduce-quality prompt from the SCR-049 sign-off checklist is shown with the measured frame cost, rather than silently dropping frames.
- Persistence: grid shape, per-cell symbol/interval bindings, propagate-symbol flag and per-cell sync groups serialise into the panel's `pane_config` (21-database-schema 3.8.1) and are restored by **E15-S03**.

## Out of scope
- Overlay and ratio *series* rendering inside a single chart (the percent-normalised overlay and bar-by-bar ratio computation of US-CHART-011 scenarios 1-2) - chart-engine work owned by **E11**; this Story delivers only the grid that makes side-by-side comparison possible.
- The cross-pane sync machinery and its configuration surface - **E15-T03** and **E15-S04**.
- Free-form drag-resize of cells beyond the preset shapes and the one custom split.
- Order-flow panels inside grid cells (SCR-050 and friends) - **R2**.
- Dragging a cell out of the grid to become a top-level pane.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A preset grid binds each cell independently
  Given a multi-chart grid panel in the workspace
  When the trader applies the 2x2 preset
  Then four chart cells are drawn, each with its own header, and each can be bound to a different symbol and interval

Scenario: Propagate symbol keeps intervals per cell
  Given a 2x2 grid showing BTCUSDT at 4H, 1H, 15m and 5m with propagate symbol on
  When the symbol of any cell is changed to ETHUSDT
  Then all four cells show ETHUSDT and each keeps its own interval

Scenario: Cells participate in workspace sync groups
  Given cell 1 is in sync group A together with a top-level pane, and cell 2 is in group B
  When the crosshair moves in the top-level pane
  Then cell 1's crosshair follows at the same timestamp and cell 2 is unaffected

Scenario: Maximise and restore preserve bindings
  Given a 2x2 grid with four distinct symbol and interval bindings and the third cell focused
  When the trader presses Ctrl+Alt+Enter and then Esc
  Then the third cell fills the panel and then the 2x2 grid returns with all four bindings, sync groups and visible ranges unchanged

Scenario: Exceeding the measured budget prompts rather than degrading silently
  Given the measured pane-count curve from E15-K01 shows a 3x3 grid falls below the frame budget on this machine
  When the trader applies the 3x3 preset
  Then a dialog states the measured frame cost and offers reduce quality or cancel, and no change is applied until the trader chooses

Scenario: Grid survives a workspace restart
  Given a saved workspace containing a 1+3 grid panel with per-cell bindings and propagate symbol off
  When the app is restarted and the workspace reopened
  Then the same grid shape, bindings, sync groups and propagate flag are restored

Scenario: A cell whose symbol lacks history for the range shows a gap
  Given two cells compared over a range where one symbol has no bars for part of it
  When both cells render that range
  Then the missing span is drawn as a gap and never interpolated, and that cell's header states the shortened history

Scenario: An invalid persisted cell count is rejected at the boundary
  Given a workspace document whose grid pane_config declares 24 cells
  When it is loaded or imported
  Then validation rejects the pane with a stated reason and the rest of the workspace still opens

Scenario: Every cell is keyboard reachable and announced
  Given a 3x3 grid
  When the trader presses Ctrl+Alt+5
  Then focus moves to the fifth cell and it is announced with its symbol, interval and sync group as text
```

## Technical notes / design
One WebGL context, scissored viewports. Per SCR-049's performance line the whole grid shares a single context and each cell renders into a scissor rectangle, so adding a cell costs draw calls rather than a context, a swap chain and a fresh set of GPU buffers. This is also why the grid is a panel rather than N docked panels: the outer DockGrid of **E15-T02** deliberately avoids GL churn on layout change, and nesting real panels would have given us up to nine contexts in one dock slot.

Cell bindings live in the panel's `pane_config` JSON rather than in `layout_panes` rows. Cells are not panes - they are not independently dockable, closable or floatable - and modelling them as panes would have leaked cell semantics into **E15-T01**'s `/api/v1/workspaces` payloads and into every consumer of the pane list. The accepted trade-off is that a cell cannot be promoted to a top-level pane in R1.

Sync-group membership is per cell, not per panel, because the multi-timeframe workflow needs exactly that: one cell following the main chart while the others stay put. The panel-level SyncMenu therefore sets a *default for new cells* and the per-cell tag is always the source of truth.

The budget prompt reads the measured curve recorded by **E15-K01** for this machine's capability profile, not a hard-coded cell count; a workstation that clears 3x3 must never see the prompt.

## Test plan
Unit: grid-shape reducer for the five shapes and the custom split; cell-binding serialisation to and from `pane_config` including the 2-9 bound; propagate-symbol semantics (symbol propagates, interval does not); maximise/restore round trip. Component: SCR-049 Storybook states - 1x2, 2x2, 3x3, 1+3, custom, maximised cell, budget-prompt/degraded state, empty cell. Integration: cells joining workspace sync groups alongside top-level panes through the real SyncBus from **E15-T03**; restore through **E15-S03**'s save path; rejection of an out-of-range cell count on load. E2E: apply a preset, bind four symbols, toggle propagate, maximise and restore, save, restart, verify identical state. Performance: four-cell grid held at the SCR-049 budget on the reference machine with a single context asserted programmatically, re-run in **E15-Q04**. A11y: axe on the panel, keyboard-only traversal of all nine cells, announcement assertions on cell focus and grid-shape change.

## Security notes
No new endpoint and no new stored secret: cell bindings ride the already-validated workspace write path of **E15-T01**, and the `pane_config` payload is schema-validated on write like every other pane config. That matters more here than elsewhere because this Story adds a new nested shape to a document that **E15-S07** exports and imports. Two concrete boundaries: a `pane_config` declaring a cell count outside 2-9 or an unknown grid shape must be rejected at the validation boundary rather than reaching the renderer; and an imported workspace must not use a large cell count as a resource-exhaustion vector, so the same cap that bounds the UI bounds the import path. This case is handed explicitly to **E15-X02**'s abuse-case set.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Each cell is a labelled `region` whose accessible name reads "chart, <symbol> <interval>, sync group <letter> <name>" - group identity as text, never colour alone (SC 1.4.1), consistent with **E15-S04**. `Ctrl+Alt+1..9` focuses a cell and `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` / `Esc` maximise and restore, all routed through **E10**'s remappable hotkey layer so they can be rebound when they collide with assistive technology. The active-cell indicator meets SC 2.4.11 (focus not obscured) and SC 1.4.11 non-text contrast on both light and dark surfaces, and is not colour-only - the focused cell's header carries a persistent visible marker. Grid-shape changes are announced once, politely ("Grid changed to two by two, four charts"), reusing CMP-081's existing live region rather than adding a second. The budget prompt is a real dialog with focus management and a described reason, not a toast.

## Performance notes
SCR-049's stated target: total budget for four charts at 50 fps or better from one shared WebGL context with scissored viewports; we hold 60 fps on the reference machine and treat 50 as the floor. Grid-shape changes are subject to CMP-081's 200 ms layout-transition budget. Adding or removing a cell must not recreate the context or reallocate the shared buffers. Crosshair movement across synced cells inherits the one-frame propagation and 4 ms sync budget from **E15-T03** and must produce zero React renders on cell headers. The degraded path is measured, not guessed: the prompt quotes the frame cost from **E15-K01**'s curve for this capability profile.

## Observability
`multichart.grid_changed {shape, cell_count}`, `multichart.cell_symbol_changed`, `multichart.sync_group_changed`, `multichart.cell_maximised` (all analytics, per SCR-049), plus `multichart.budget_prompt_shown {shape, measured_fps}` so we learn how often real machines hit the cap and at which shape - the input that decides whether 3x3 stays offered in R2. Grid frame time is reported under the existing per-panel render metric with cell count as a dimension.

title: ADR and operator/user docs for the workspace document format and sharing rules
body:
## Context
The workspace document is about to become a long-lived contract: it is persisted in Postgres, exported to files that users keep, and extended by every subsequent epic that adds a panel type. Decisions made implicitly in Sprint 08 — how the dock tree is serialised, how versioning works, what may and may not be exported, what happens to an unknown pane kind — will be re-litigated for years unless they are written down once, with their rationale.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires docs to reflect *shipped* behaviour, and the planning brief requires an ADR for decisions of this reach. This chore captures the decision, the format, and the two pieces of user-facing guidance that stop support questions from becoming tickets.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR** `docs/adr/00NN-workspace-document-format-and-sharing.md` recording:
  - The serialised dock-tree shape and its relationship to `layouts` / `layout_panes` in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (why the tree is persisted as panes-with-slots rather than an opaque blob, and what that buys in queryability and validation).
  - The versioning rule: documents carry a schema version; a newer version is **refused** with both versions stated (US-LAY-007), never partially applied; the forward-compat policy for unknown pane kinds within the same major version (dropped with a report).
  - The export allow-list and the id-regeneration rule from `E15-X01`, stated as architecture rather than as an implementation detail.
  - Conflict handling: ETag/`If-Match` with 412 and the [Keep mine]/[Load theirs] resolution, and why last-write-wins was rejected.
  - Rejected alternatives: opaque JSON blob; CRDT-style merge; server-side rendering of layouts; auto-migration of newer documents.
- **Panel-author guide** `docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md`: the registry entry, serialisation contract, lazy mount, hidden-tab unsubscribe after 30 s, accessible name, panel menu entries, density support, float/re-dock survival, and the `E15-Q07` new-panel-type checklist to run. Linked from `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080.
- **Operator/user guidance** in the user docs: saving and restoring workspaces, what export does and does not contain (explicitly: no keys, no tokens, no account bindings), why an import may drop elements, the reduced-capability profile and how to restore the full profile, and what the pane-limit warning means.
- Updates to `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 and `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §16 if shipped behaviour diverged from the plan, per the DoD rule that docs describe what shipped.

## Out of scope
- Documenting other epics' panel internals.
- The collaboration/sharing features of R5 (this ADR constrains them; it does not design them).
- Release notes (release management process).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records a decision with alternatives
  Given the published ADR
  Then it states context, decision, consequences and at least three rejected alternatives with reasons
  And it is accepted by the Architect and the Security engineer

Scenario: A new panel author needs no tribal knowledge
  Given an engineer on E18 adding the footprint panel
  When they follow docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md
  Then they can register, serialise, restore and float a panel without reading the dock package source

Scenario: Failure case - docs diverge from shipped behaviour
  Given the implementation refuses newer-version imports but the docs promise migration
  Then the divergence is corrected in the docs before the epic is Done, and the DoD docs checkbox cannot be ticked otherwise

Scenario: Edge case - export contents claim is verifiable
  Given the user documentation states an export contains no account bindings
  Then it links to the test that asserts it, so the claim is evidenced rather than reassuring

Scenario: Discoverability
  When a reader opens 15-component-catalogue.md CMP-080
  Then it links to the panel-author guide, and the ADR is linked from the E15 epic and from 20-architecture.md module M10
```

## Technical notes / design
- Keep the ADR short and decisive; the long-form format lives in `24-internal-schemas.md`-style documentation and the OpenAPI schema, not duplicated in the ADR.
- The panel-author guide should be a checklist with code snippets, written so that following it is faster than improvising — that is the only way a guide gets used.
- Cross-link rather than copy: the export allow-list is owned by `E15-X01`/the implementation, and the ADR references it so there is one source of truth.

## Test plan
- Doc review by the Architect, the Security engineer and one engineer from a downstream epic (E18 or E21) who has not worked on E15 — their ability to follow the panel guide is the acceptance test.
- Link-check and example-check in CI (code snippets compile against the current API).
- Verify every factual claim about export contents and version handling against the merged tests; any claim with no test is either tested or removed.

## Security notes
- The user-facing statement about export contents is a security-relevant claim; it must match the implemented allow-list exactly and link to its test. Overstating it would create false confidence about sharing a file.
- The ADR records that workspace exports are user-confidential (they reveal watched symbols and trading style), constraining any future "share a workspace" feature in R5 to explicit, audited sharing rather than public links.
- The panel-author guide includes the security checklist items a new panel must satisfy: no unescaped rendering of workspace-derived strings, no client-trusted ids, server-side permission checks for role-restricted panels.

## Accessibility notes
- The panel-author guide makes accessible name, keyboard menu entries and focus behaviour mandatory checklist items, so a11y is inherited by construction rather than retrofitted per panel in E47.
- User documentation describes the keyboard equivalents for every layout operation, so the keyboard path is discoverable and not merely present.

## Performance notes
- The guide states the two performance obligations a panel author must meet — lazy mount (`SCR-024` ≤150 ms) and unsubscribe when hidden for 30 s (`SCR-020`) — plus the rule that layout changes must never remount the WebGL context, with the `E15-Q04` benchmark named as the check.
- The ADR records the measured baselines from `E15-Q04` as the reference point future changes are compared against.

## Observability
- Documents the analytics/audit event vocabulary for the layout surface (`workspace.*`, `panel.*`, `layout.*`, `sync.*`) including which are audited versus analytics-only, so downstream epics emit consistent events instead of inventing names.
- Records where the ops dashboard shows import rejections and probing alerts, for the operator runbook.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR merged and accepted by Architect and Security engineer; linked from the E15 epic and `20-architecture.md` M10.
- [ ] `docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md` merged and linked from CMP-080 in `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] User-facing workspace documentation merged, with the export-contents claim linked to its test.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 and `11-user-stories.md` §16 reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Reviewed by a downstream-epic engineer who successfully followed the panel guide.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (allow-list and versioning rules), `E15-Q04` (baseline numbers), `E15-S07` (shipped export/import behaviour).

## Branch
`docs/e15-workspace-format-adr`

## References

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`, `/chart-templates*`
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 (SCR-020..029)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080, CMP-081
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-002, US-LAY-007, US-LAY-008
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2

title: Design QA of the built workspace, dock system, presets and sync surfaces
body:
## Context
Design QA closes the loop: the built product is compared against the signed-off specification, surface by surface, state by state, and the differences are either fixed or filed. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` makes this a Story-level DoD requirement for net-new UI, and E15 is the largest net-new UI surface in R1 - twelve screens and roughly thirty components that every later epic will inherit. A discrepancy tolerated here becomes the de facto standard for E18..E41.

This review runs in Sprint 09, alongside the tail of E15's engineering work (Sprints 06-09), so findings can be fixed inside the epic rather than carried into R2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Surface-by-surface review** of the implemented SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-023, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-026, SCR-027, SCR-028, SCR-029, SCR-049, SCR-150 and SCR-153 against their spec pages and Figma frames.
- **State walk**: every state enumerated in the specs - loading, empty, populated, unsaved, conflict, crash-restored, over-budget, panel-too-small, invalid drop, at-minimum splitter, degraded, import rejected, version mismatch, delisted symbol - exercised in the real build, not in Storybook alone.
- **Token compliance check**: computed styles inspected against the token values from E15-D13; any hard-coded value is a finding.
- **Density and theme matrix**: compact/cosy/comfortable x dark/light at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, plus 200% zoom.
- **Interaction fidelity**: drag/drop zone geometry against the spec, keyboard move mode, splitter resize (pointer and keyboard), preset application, workspace switch, float and re-dock in the Electron build and the maximised-overlay fallback in the browser build.
- **Accessibility verification** against E15-D15: keyboard model as specified, focus destinations after every layout mutation, announcement strings matching the script verbatim, axe-core clean on every touched screen, one manual screen-reader pass.
- **Motion verification** against E15-D14: nothing animates a content box, reduced-motion behaviour correct, timings within the menu/preset budgets.
- **Copy verification** against the E15-D16 copy deck, string by string.
- **Findings register** with severity (blocker / major / minor / nit), a screenshot pair, the owning ticket, and a disposition - fixed in-epic, filed as a Bug with a priority, or accepted with a written reason.
- **Sign-off report** at `docs/design/specs/e15-design-qa-report.md`.

## Out of scope
- Functional/black-box QA (E15 QA chunk owns test-plan execution) - this review is fidelity to the design specification, though a functional defect found here is filed rather than ignored.
- Performance benchmarking (engineering owns the FPS and latency runs) - but a visually obvious frame-rate problem during a docking interaction is filed as a finding.
- New design work; anything requiring a design decision goes back to the owning design ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every specified state is verified in the real build
  Given the state inventory from the E15 specs
  When each state is exercised in the running application
  Then it is recorded as pass, fail or blocked with evidence
  And a state that cannot be reached is filed as a finding rather than skipped

Scenario: A hard-coded value is found
  Given computed styles on the implemented panel chrome
  When a value does not resolve to a design token
  Then it is filed as a finding against the implementing ticket
  And the fix uses the token rather than matching the value by hand

Scenario: Announcements do not match the script
  Given the E15-D15 announcement script
  When each state change is triggered with a screen reader running
  Then the spoken text matches the script
  And any divergence is filed as a blocker or major finding depending on whether meaning is lost

Scenario: Keyboard parity regressed during implementation
  Given every layout operation
  When each is attempted without a pointer
  Then all succeed as specified
  And any pointer-only operation is a blocker finding that cannot be accepted or deferred

Scenario: A finding is disputed
  Given a discrepancy the engineer believes is a spec error rather than a build error
  Then it is escalated to the CDO for a decision
  And the outcome is recorded, with the spec corrected if the engineer is right

Scenario: The review finds a blocker close to the release gate
  Given a blocker finding in Sprint 09
  Then it is fixed within the epic or the affected Story does not meet its DoD
  And no blocker is silently downgraded to close the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
Review in the real build, not in Storybook. Storybook proves a component in isolation; E15's failures are compositional - a panel header that is fine alone but collides with a sync badge at compact density in a 3x3 grid, or a focus ring that is correct until a floating window overlaps it (WCAG 2.4.11).

Evidence is paired screenshots - spec frame and build - because a prose description of a spacing discrepancy is unresolvable in review. For interaction findings, a short screen recording replaces the screenshot pair.

Severity should be assigned by *user consequence*, not by pixel magnitude: a 2 px gutter error is a nit, while a missing environment badge in a floating window is a blocker even though it is smaller on screen.

The review should explicitly re-check the five things E15's own specs flagged as easy to lose in implementation: the inset focus affordance (no reflow on focus), the letter on every sync badge, the environment word in every floating-window title, Esc mapping to Cancel rather than Discard, and the keyboard move mode's visible instructions.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-by-screen walk against spec pages with paired-screenshot evidence. (2) Full state walk in the real build. (3) Density x theme x zoom matrix sweep. (4) Interaction fidelity session, pointer and keyboard, in both Electron and browser builds. (5) axe-core run on every touched screen plus one manual NVDA pass on the five-task scenario from E15-D15. (6) Computed-style token audit on the chrome components. (7) Motion check including reduced-motion. (8) Copy diff against the copy deck. (9) Findings triage with the FE lead and the CDO; dispositions recorded.

## Security notes
The review verifies that the security-relevant design rules survived implementation, and treats each failure as a blocker: environment disclosure present on every order-capable panel, in every floating window title and window chrome, and preserved when a panel is maximised; RBAC-hidden controls genuinely accompanied by server-side enforcement (spot-checked by attempting a hidden action's API call with QA/Security); untrusted strings from imported workspaces rendered as capped text with no markup interpretation - verified with a crafted fixture containing markup and an overlong name; exports verified to contain no credentials, account ids or environment binding by inspecting an actual exported file; and "Copy panel link" verified to produce a link without account ids or tokens. Any failure here is escalated to the Security engineer as well as filed.

## Accessibility notes
This review executes the verification half of E15-D15. axe-core must be clean on every touched screen; the manual pass covers the five-task scenario (build a 2x2 layout, bind symbols, join a sync group, save, reopen) with NVDA and one VoiceOver spot-check. Focus destinations after every layout mutation are checked against the focus-model table. Announcement text is transcribed and diffed against the script. Target sizes are measured on splitters and panel controls. Contrast is measured in the running build over real panel content, including a dense footprint, rather than over the design's placeholder backgrounds. A pointer-only operation is a blocker that cannot be accepted.

## Performance notes
While formal benchmarking belongs to engineering, this review verifies the design-side constraints that protect the budgets and files failures: focusing a panel must not resize its canvas (observed as a visible reflow or a frame stall), drag previews must not carry live content, drop must commit one layout change, preset application must reuse panel instances rather than remounting, and no animation may change a content box. Anything that visibly stutters during a docking interaction on the reference machine is filed with a recording, since that is a user-visible failure of US-LAY-001's budget regardless of what a benchmark says.

## Observability
The review confirms that the analytics events from the E15-D16 table actually fire with the specified properties - particularly `layout.panel_moved{method}`, `layout.preset_applied{entry}` and `workspace.restore_completed{ms,paneCount,failedPanes}` - since these are the measurements that will tell the team whether E15's design assumptions were right. A missing required event is a major finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All fourteen screens reviewed against their spec pages with paired-screenshot evidence.
- [ ] Full state walk completed in the real build; unreachable states filed.
- [ ] Density x theme x zoom matrix swept at both reference widths.
- [ ] Interaction fidelity verified in Electron and browser builds, pointer and keyboard.
- [ ] axe-core clean on every touched screen; manual screen-reader pass completed with transcripts.
- [ ] Announcement strings diffed against the E15-D15 script.
- [ ] Token compliance audit complete; hard-coded values filed.
- [ ] Motion and reduced-motion verified against E15-D14.
- [ ] Copy diffed against the E15-D16 copy deck.
- [ ] Security spot-checks completed (env disclosure, RBAC enforcement, untrusted strings, export contents, panel link).
- [ ] Required analytics events verified as firing with correct properties.
- [ ] Findings register complete with severity, evidence and disposition; all blockers fixed in-epic, majors fixed or filed with a priority.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-design-qa-report.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** - this sign-off is a DoD input for the consuming US-LAY stories and for the E15 epic itself.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D16** - the handoff pack, including the design-QA checklist published in advance.
- E15 engineering stories implementing US-LAY-001..008 being feature-complete enough to review in Sprint 09.
- A build of both the Electron shell and the browser target.

`design/e15-design-qa`

title: Playwright E2E suite for dock, workspace save/restore and preset gallery
body:
## Context
The layout surface is the one place in CandleViewer where a regression is both easy to introduce (any epic adding a panel type touches the dock registry) and easy to miss (it looks fine until you restore a saved workspace). `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` puts Playwright E2E — web *and* Electron — at the top of the pyramid precisely for journeys like this, and the R1 exit criteria require the charting alpha to survive a restart with its workspace intact.

`E15-Q01` writes the plan; this ticket automates the parts of it that are deterministic and high-value, so that every PR touching `web/` or the dock package gets an honest answer about whether a 4-pane workspace still saves and restores.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New spec files under `e2e/specs/layouts/`:
  - `dock-grid.spec.ts` — apply presets 1×1, 2×1, 2×2, 1+3 from `SCR-022`; drag a pane divider and assert persisted sizes; add a panel from `SCR-024`; remove and undo; assert the `>16 panels` warning path.
  - `dock-drag-drop.spec.ts` — drag a panel to each of the N/S/E/W/centre drop zones of `SCR-021` and assert the resulting tree; assert the invalid-drop affordance; assert the keyboard equivalent via CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel".
  - `workspace-persistence.spec.ts` — save (`Ctrl+S`), save-as (`Ctrl+Shift+S`), reload the page, assert full restore including pane sizes and scroll position; assert the unsaved-changes `*` marker and the `SCR-029` navigation prompt.
  - `workspace-crud.spec.ts` — create/rename/duplicate/delete through `SCR-025`; assert last-workspace-cannot-be-deleted and the type-the-name delete confirmation.
  - `layout-hotkeys.spec.ts` — `Ctrl+1..9` preset slots, `Ctrl+Tab` pane focus with a visible focus ring, `F6` region cycling, `F11` full-screen panel, `Ctrl+Alt+←/→` panel cycling.
  - `workspace-restore-edge.spec.ts` — delisted-symbol pane error state; crash-restore banner ("Restored your layout from 14:02"); stale-write 412 dialog with [Keep mine] / [Load theirs].
- An Electron-runner variant of `dock-drag-drop` and `workspace-persistence` covering `SCR-027` floating windows (float → move → re-dock → restart → position restored).
- Test-data helpers: `seedWorkspace(fixtureName)` hitting `POST /api/v1/workspaces` + `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/layouts` so specs start from a known tree instead of clicking one together.
- Stable selectors: `data-testid` on CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu, CMP-218 SyncMenu — added as part of this ticket where missing.
- CI wiring: suite runs on PRs touching `web/**` and nightly in full (web + Electron), with traces and video on failure.

## Out of scope
- Sync-group behavioural assertions — `E15-Q03`.
- FPS/latency measurement — `E15-Q04` (Playwright is not a profiler; specs assert behaviour, not frame time).
- axe-core full audit — `E15-Q06` (specs here run axe only as a smoke check on `SCR-020`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A 4-pane workspace survives a reload
  Given a seeded 2x2 workspace with chart, footprint, DOM and tape panes
  When the spec saves it, reloads the page and waits for interactive
  Then all four panes are present in the same slots with the same sizes, symbols and intervals

Scenario: Keyboard docking is automated, not just documented
  When the spec opens the panel menu with Shift+F10 and chooses Move panel then Bottom
  Then the panel lands in the bottom region and a live region announces the move
  And the spec asserts the announcement text, not only the DOM position

Scenario: Failure case - stale save is refused
  Given two browser contexts have the same workspace open and context A has saved
  When context B saves with its stale ETag
  Then the API returns 412 and the spec asserts the conflict dialog appears with both resolution actions
  And choosing [Load theirs] replaces the local tree with A's version

Scenario: Edge case - delisted symbol
  Given a seeded workspace whose second pane references a delisted symbol
  When it is restored
  Then that pane shows an error state naming the symbol and the other three panes are interactive

Scenario: Flake gate
  Given the suite is run 20 times consecutively in CI
  Then it passes at least 20 of 20 times, or the offending spec is quarantined with a linked bug before merge
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drag-and-drop in Playwright is notoriously flaky: use `page.mouse` with explicit intermediate moves and wait on the drop-zone highlight state (CMP-214) rather than fixed sleeps; prefer asserting the committed tree via the app's exposed layout snapshot hook over pixel geometry.
- Assert the *serialized* dock tree (a stable JSON shape) for structural cases and reserve geometric assertions for splitter sizing, so refactors of the renderer do not churn the suite.
- Reuse the `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 slot model (`layout_panes.slot_index`) as the vocabulary for assertions so specs read the same way as the API examples in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Electron specs run against the packaged dev build via `_electron.launch`; floating-window assertions use the second `BrowserWindow` handle.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying: the deliverable is tests. Verification is (a) mutation-style sanity — deliberately break pane-size persistence locally and confirm `workspace-persistence.spec.ts` fails; (b) the 20-run flake gate; (c) a review that every spec maps to an `E15-TC-*` id from `E15-Q01`.

## Security notes
- Specs authenticate through the real auth flow with seeded non-privileged users; no test bypasses RBAC or injects tokens directly, so an accidental authorization regression surfaces here too.
- A spec asserts that a `viewer` role can open a workspace but cannot mutate a shared/published layout, and that the API refuses with 403 rather than the UI merely hiding the control.
- Fixture teardown deletes seeded workspaces so CI state never accumulates user data.

## Accessibility notes
- Every drag case has a keyboard twin; the suite fails if a layout operation exists with no keyboard path (CMP-214 mandates this).
- Focus assertions: after preset apply, focus lands on the first pane; after panel close, focus moves to a sane sibling, never to `body`.
- An axe-core smoke check runs on `SCR-020` in the default and 16-pane states; serious/critical violations fail the spec.

## Performance notes
- Specs assert coarse timing guards only (restore to interactive ≤3 s warm, preset apply ≤300 ms) using the app's own performance marks; the fine-grained budgets are `E15-Q04`'s job.
- Suite wall-clock target ≤8 minutes sharded on CI so it can stay on the PR gate rather than being demoted to nightly.

## Observability
- Specs subscribe to the dev analytics sink and assert the documented events fire on the modelled actions (`workspace.saved`, `panel.added`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset`).
- On failure, traces, video, the serialized dock tree and the last 50 analytics events are attached to the CI artefact bundle to make triage a read rather than a re-run.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All listed specs merged and green on web and Electron runners.
- [ ] `data-testid` hooks added to the named components and documented in `15-component-catalogue.md` notes.
- [ ] Suite wired to the PR gate for `web/**` and to the nightly full run.
- [ ] 20-run flake gate passed; any quarantine has a linked bug.
- [ ] Coverage mapping from each spec to `E15-TC-*` ids recorded in the plan from `E15-Q01`.

## Dependencies
- `E15-Q01` for the case ids; `E15-S01`, `E15-S02`, `E15-S05`, `E15-S06` for the surfaces; E10 for the Electron shell harness.

## Branch
`chore/e15-e2e-layouts`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E tier, flake policy)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-027, SCR-029
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts` (If-Match, 412)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1

title: Multi-pane performance benchmark and workspace restore/load scripts
body:
## Context
A layout epic is a performance epic in disguise: one chart at 60 fps says nothing about four order-flow panes plus a DOM and a tape sharing a GPU and one WebSocket. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 makes frame time budget #1 a hard R1 exit gate and budget #2 sets a 30 fps floor for a 5-symbol multi-chart layout; `23-ws-protocol.md` §16.3 sets the reference-workspace bandwidth budget (<350 KiB/s sustained) and full re-snapshot budget (<700 KiB, <400 ms). US-LAY-001 adds ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes, US-LAY-002 adds ≤3 s restore-to-interactive.

Nothing currently measures any of that for a *workspace*. This ticket builds the benchmark harness and the load scripts, and turns the numbers into a tracked series rather than a one-off screenshot.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Frame benchmark** `perf/bench/layout-fps.ts` (Playwright + CDP tracing, headed Chromium/Electron on the §3.1 reference machine):
  - Scenarios: 1 pane; 2×2 with four chart panes; 2×2 with four order-flow panes (chart + footprint + DOM depth-50 + tape); 6-pane `six-pane-sync` fixture; 16-pane stress; degraded profile from US-LAY-008.
  - Per scenario: p50/p95/p99 frame time, dropped-frame count, long-task count, GPU memory, and the per-stage breakdown from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.
  - Actions under measurement: idle live-tick, pan, zoom, crosshair sweep across a sync group, preset apply, panel add/remove, splitter drag, float/re-dock.
- **Restore benchmark**: cold and warm restore-to-interactive for 1/4/6/16-pane workspaces, decomposed into API fetch, tree build, panel mount, first paint, first live frame — so a regression is attributable rather than merely visible.
- **Load script** `perf/k6/workspace-fanout.js`: N clients each restoring the 4-pane reference workspace and holding subscriptions for 1 h, asserting the §16.3 bandwidth and re-snapshot budgets and zero backpressure-induced resyncs; plus a `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{id}` write-storm at the 2-second debounce cadence to confirm persistence is not a hot path.
- **Budget file** `perf/budgets/e15.json` consumed by CI, with the numbers above and an agreed tolerance band.
- **Trend reporting**: nightly run publishing to the existing Grafana perf dashboard (E04) with a regression alert on p95 frame time and restore time.

## Out of scope
- Optimising anything. This ticket measures and reports; fixes are filed as bugs against the owning story or deferred to E46.
- Engine-internal micro-benchmarks (E11/E12) — reused here, not re-implemented.
- Backend ingestion soak (E08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Four order-flow panes meet the story budget
  Given the 2x2 order-flow scenario on the reference machine with live-equivalent replayed data
  When the benchmark runs for 5 minutes
  Then p95 frame time is under 18.2ms (>=55 fps) and no frame exceeds 33ms more than once per 10s
  And the result is written to perf/budgets/e15.json's tracked series

Scenario: Warm restore is under three seconds
  Given a 4-pane workspace and a warm cache
  When restore-to-interactive is measured 10 times
  Then the median is under 3s and the decomposition of each phase is reported

Scenario: Failure case - budget breach fails the nightly build
  Given a change regresses p95 frame time in the 6-pane scenario by more than the tolerance band
  When the nightly benchmark runs
  Then the job fails, the Grafana alert fires, and the report names the §4.3 stage that grew

Scenario: Edge case - 16 panes degrade, never crash
  Given the 16-pane stress scenario
  When it runs for 10 minutes
  Then the app stays above the 30fps floor or applies the documented degradation ladder, and never loses the WebGL context
  And the >16-panel warning reports the measured cost, matching what the benchmark recorded

Scenario: Load script holds the WS budget
  Given 8 k6 clients each holding the reference workspace for one hour
  Then sustained server-to-client bandwidth per client stays under 350 KiB/s and no client is force-resynced by backpressure
```

## Technical notes / design
- Replayed deterministic data (E16 recorder fixtures) is mandatory — benchmarking against live Bybit makes runs incomparable week to week.
- Use CDP `Tracing` frame markers plus the engine's own frame-marker instrumentation (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.2) so the per-stage breakdown is real rather than inferred.
- Pin GPU/driver and record them in every result row; an unpinned driver upgrade is the classic phantom regression.
- The degraded profile scenario must exercise capability detection by *measured frame time*, not user-agent (US-LAY-008 NFR) — the harness forces a slow-GPU condition via CPU/GPU throttling rather than UA spoofing.

## Test plan
- Harness self-test: inject a synthetic 10 ms-per-frame stall and confirm the harness reports it in the right §4.3 stage and fails the budget.
- Run each scenario 3× and report variance; a scenario with >10% run-to-run variance is stabilised before its budget is enforced.
- Cross-check one scenario manually with Chrome DevTools performance panel to validate the automated numbers.

## Security notes
- The benchmark runs against a seeded non-production dataset; no live account or key material is present in fixtures or in published traces.
- Published traces and HAR-like artefacts are scrubbed of auth cookies and bearer tokens before upload to the dashboard bucket.
- The k6 script authenticates as ordinary seeded users through the real auth path, so a load run cannot become an accidental authorization bypass.

## Accessibility notes
- The degraded/reduced-capability profile must not remove keyboard paths or accessible names; the harness runs the `E15-Q06` axe smoke in the degraded scenario to confirm reduction is visual/frequency-only.
- Reduced-motion preference is exercised as one scenario variant, confirming motion reduction does not itself cost frames.

## Performance notes
- Authoritative budgets: `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 #1 (≤16.6 ms p95), #2 (30 fps floor, multi-chart), #14 (heatmap cadence), §4.3 stage allocation; `23-ws-protocol.md` §16.3 bandwidth/re-snapshot; US-LAY-001 ≥55 fps four order-flow panes; US-LAY-002 ≤3 s restore; `SCR-022` ≤300 ms preset apply; `SCR-024` ≤150 ms panel mount.
- A layout change must never remount the WebGL context (`SCR-020`); the harness asserts context-creation count stays constant across preset apply and dock mutations.

## Observability
- Results are emitted as structured JSON and pushed to Prometheus/Grafana via the E04 pipeline; each row carries commit sha, GPU/driver, scenario, fixture and run index.
- Frame-marker spans and the WS frame counters are retained per run so a regression can be triaged from stored artefacts without reproducing locally.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Benchmark harness, restore benchmark, k6 script and budget file merged.
- [ ] Baseline numbers recorded for all six scenarios on the reference machine and attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Nightly job publishing to Grafana with regression alerting wired.
- [ ] Any budget breach found is filed as a bug against the owning story with the §4.3 stage identified.
- [ ] Perf results reviewed by the Architect and referenced from the R1 exit-criteria checklist.

## Dependencies
- `E15-Q02`/`E15-Q03` fixtures; `E15-S01`, `E15-S02`, `E15-S08`; E16 recorded fixtures; E04 metrics pipeline; E11/E12 engine instrumentation.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §16.3
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-002, US-LAY-008

title: Chaos: WS loss, API 5xx, storage failure and workspace crash-restore
body:
## Context
The planning brief lists chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) as a non-negotiable SDLC requirement. For E15 the failure surface is specific and under-tested: the workspace is the *container* for everything, so a failure here degrades every panel at once. The worst outcomes are silent data loss (a save that appears to succeed and did not), a restore that half-applies and leaves a tree the user cannot repair, and a dock tree that survives a renderer crash in a corrupted state.

`23-ws-protocol.md` §4 makes it explicit that there is no session resumption in v1: a reconnect re-subscribes from scratch and every topic re-snapshots. A 4-pane workspace therefore re-snapshots ~600 KiB on every reconnect, and the UI must handle that gracefully rather than flashing every pane through an empty state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos scenario pack `qa/chaos/e15-workspace-chaos.md` plus automation under `e2e/specs/layouts/chaos/`:
  1. **WS drop mid-session** — kill the socket with a 4-pane workspace open; assert panes show a connecting state (not an error, not blank), reconnect re-snapshots all topics, and the dock tree is untouched.
  2. **Repeated flapping** — 10 disconnect/reconnect cycles in 2 minutes; assert no subscription leak (topic count returns to baseline), no duplicate panes, no unbounded memory growth.
  3. **Save fails with 5xx** — `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{id}` returns 503; assert the UI keeps the unsaved `*` marker, surfaces a retry, and never claims success; assert the local tree is not reverted.
  4. **Save fails with 412** — concurrent modification; assert the `SCR-020` [Keep mine]/[Load theirs] path, and that [Keep mine] re-saves with a refreshed ETag rather than looping.
  5. **Restore fails partially** — `GET /workspaces/{id}` succeeds but one pane's referenced `chart_template_id` is missing; assert that pane falls back to defaults with a named notice and the rest restores.
  6. **Delisted / unknown symbol** — pane opens in an explicit error state naming the symbol (US-LAY-002).
  7. **Renderer crash & restore** — force a renderer crash in Electron; assert the crash-restore banner ("Restored your layout from 14:02") and that the restored tree matches the last autosave, with no duplicated panels.
  8. **Storage unavailable at boot** — Postgres down; assert `SCR-150` boot state degrades to a clear "can't load your workspaces" message with retry, not an infinite spinner or a blank shell.
  9. **Rate limiting** — a write-storm triggers 429; assert the 2-second debounce backs off and no save is lost.
  10. **Quota/oversize** — importing or saving an oversized layout document is refused with a stated limit (see `E15-X02` for the adversarial variant).
- Fault injection via a test-only proxy (route interception in Playwright for HTTP, a socket-kill hook for WS) — no production code paths added for testability beyond documented test hooks.
- A **recovery-time table**: for each scenario, measured time to usable state, recorded in the pack.

## Out of scope
- Backend resilience of the ingestion path (E08) and WS gateway internals (E17) — this pack is client-observable behaviour.
- Malicious payloads — `E15-X02`.
- Disaster recovery of the Postgres data itself (infra epics).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reconnect does not destroy the layout
  Given a 4-pane workspace with live data
  When the WebSocket is killed and allowed to reconnect
  Then the dock tree, pane sizes and sync groups are unchanged
  And each pane transitions through a connecting state to live data without an error toast

Scenario: Failure case - a failed save never looks successful
  Given the layout save endpoint returns 503
  When the user presses Ctrl+S
  Then an explicit failure is shown with a retry action, the unsaved marker remains, and no success analytics event is emitted

Scenario: Edge case - flapping does not leak subscriptions
  Given 10 disconnect/reconnect cycles within 2 minutes
  Then the active topic-subscription count returns to its pre-chaos baseline
  And heap growth across the cycles stays within the documented tolerance

Scenario: Crash restore is faithful
  Given a modified 6-pane workspace and a forced renderer crash
  When the app restarts
  Then the restore banner names the autosave time and the restored tree equals the last autosave, with no duplicate panels

Scenario: Boot with storage down is honest
  Given Postgres is unavailable
  When the app boots
  Then SCR-150 shows a named failure with retry within 10s, and the user is never left on an indefinite spinner
```

## Technical notes / design
- Because v1 has no WS resumption, the correct post-reconnect behaviour is *re-snapshot without visual teardown*: panes keep their last frame and overlay a subtle connecting affordance. Assert that, not merely "data comes back".
- The autosave used by crash-restore must be write-ahead (local) so it survives a crash between debounced server saves; the pack asserts the local copy is newer-or-equal to the server copy after a crash.
- Keep fault injection out of shipped code: use network-layer interception and an Electron test hook guarded by the dev flag.

## Test plan
- Each scenario is scripted where deterministic and manual-with-a-checklist where not (renderer crash, storage down), with evidence (video or log excerpt) attached per run.
- The pack runs in full before the E15 QA sign-off (`E15-Q08`) and nightly for the automated subset.
- Negative verification: disable the retry logic locally and confirm scenarios 3 and 9 fail.

## Security notes
- Failure messages must not leak internal detail: no stack traces, SQL fragments, hostnames or internal ids in user-facing error copy; a case asserts this for every injected failure.
- A 412/409 conflict must not disclose another user's data; the conflict dialog shows only the caller's own workspace versions.
- Retry storms must not be usable as a self-inflicted DoS: the backoff behaviour under 429 is asserted, which also bounds abusive client behaviour.

## Accessibility notes
- Every degraded/connecting/error state is announced in a live region and is reachable by keyboard; a chaos run with a screen reader confirms the user is told *which* pane failed, by name.
- Error states meet contrast requirements in both themes and do not rely on colour alone to signal failure.

## Performance notes
- Recovery-time targets: reconnect to all panes live ≤5 s on the reference workspace (consistent with the <400 ms re-snapshot budget plus subscription round-trips in `23-ws-protocol.md` §16.3); boot failure surfaced ≤10 s.
- Flapping must not degrade frame time after recovery; the pack re-runs a short `E15-Q04` frame sample post-chaos and compares against baseline.

## Observability
- Assert that each failure emits a structured client log with a correlation id that can be joined to the server-side request in Grafana/Loki (E04) — a chaos scenario that produces no telemetry is itself a defect.
- `layout.import_rejected{reason}` and save-failure events must carry the failure class so the ops dashboard can distinguish 5xx from 412 from 429.

- [ ] Chaos pack documented with all ten scenarios and the recovery-time table populated.
- [ ] Automated subset merged and running nightly.
- [ ] Evidence attached for the manual scenarios.
- [ ] Defects found filed against the owning stories with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3.
- [ ] Pack referenced from the E15 QA sign-off checklist.

## Dependencies

title: Accessibility audit of the dock system, workspace switcher and layout surfaces
body:
## Context
Drag-and-drop layout systems are the canonical accessibility failure in trading terminals: everything works with a mouse and nothing works without one. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes, and `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-214 DockDropZone states the rule for this epic explicitly — drag-and-drop has a **mandatory keyboard equivalent** via CMP-216 PanelMenu's directional "Move panel" chooser, so no layout operation is pointer-only.

E15 also introduces the app's primary landmark structure: each panel is a `region` with an accessible name, `F6` cycles regions, `Ctrl+Tab` cycles panes. If that structure is wrong here, every epic that adds a panel inherits the defect. This audit is therefore a foundation check, not a polish pass.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated**: axe-core runs wired into the `E15-Q02` suite for `SCR-020`, `SCR-021`, `SCR-022`, `SCR-023`, `SCR-024`, `SCR-025`, `SCR-026`, `SCR-027`, `SCR-028`, `SCR-029`, `SCR-011`, `SCR-153`, in default / 16-pane / degraded / empty states, both themes and all three densities. Serious and critical violations fail CI.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**: NVDA + Firefox and VoiceOver + Safari on the web build, and NVDA on the Electron build, covering: opening a workspace, adding a panel, moving a panel by keyboard, splitting, floating (`SCR-027`) and re-docking, joining a sync group, saving, and importing.
- **Keyboard-only run**: complete every US-LAY-001..008 acceptance scenario with the mouse physically unplugged; any step that cannot be completed is a blocking defect.
- **Focus-management report**: focus order across the dock tree, focus after panel close/preset apply/modal dismiss, focus trapping in `SCR-022`/`SCR-025`/`SCR-026` dialogs, focus restoration when a floating window closes, and visible focus indicators meeting WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast (and 2.4.11 focus-not-obscured, which splitters and floating panels can violate).
- **Announcement inventory**: exact live-region strings for move/split/float/close/preset-apply/sync-group-change, reviewed with the design-system a11y owner so they are consistent rather than ad hoc.
- **Findings register** `qa/a11y/e15-audit.md` with severity, WCAG success criterion, screenshot/recording, owning ticket, and fix status.

## Out of scope
- Chart canvas content accessibility (the DOM-mirror layer) — owned by E11/E12 and audited in E47; E15 audits the *chrome* around it.
- Full-app WCAG certification (E47).
- Colour-token contrast definitions (E05 design system); this audit verifies usage, not token values.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every layout operation has a keyboard path
  Given the mouse is unavailable
  When the auditor performs add, move, split, resize, float, re-dock, maximise, close and preset-apply
  Then every operation completes using documented keyboard commands
  And each is discoverable from the panel menu opened with Shift+F10

Scenario: Panels are named regions
  Given a 4-pane workspace
  When a screen-reader user cycles regions with F6
  Then each panel is announced with a meaningful name such as "Chart, BTCUSDT 1m" including its symbol and interval

Scenario: Failure case - a move with no announcement is a defect
  Given a panel is moved to the bottom region by keyboard
  When no live-region announcement is produced
  Then the audit records a blocking defect against the owning story, and the epic cannot reach QA sign-off

Scenario: Edge case - focus is not lost when a panel closes
  Given focus is inside a panel that is then closed
  Then focus moves to an adjacent panel or the dock container, never to document body, and the new location is announced

Scenario: Automated gate is enforced
  Given the axe-core checks are wired into CI
  When a change introduces a serious violation on SCR-020
  Then the build fails with the rule id and the offending selector
```

## Technical notes / design
- The keyboard move mode needs its own visible instructions (per the `SCR-021` sign-off checklist); verify the instructions are announced on entry and that `Esc` cancels without mutating the tree.
- Sync-group badges must carry a letter as text (CMP-218, `SCR-023`) — verify the accessible name includes the group, not just the colour.
- Floating windows (`SCR-027`) are independent documents: verify each has its own `<title>` naming panel, symbol and environment, its own skip link, and its own focus scope.
- Splitters should expose `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-orientation` and respond to arrow keys, so resizing is reportable to assistive tech and not merely possible.
- `SCR-024` panel picker: category headings must be real headings and each entry's one-line description read with its name; disabled entries must expose their reason, not just be dimmed.

## Test plan
- Execute the automated suite, then the manual matrix (2 screen-reader/browser pairs + Electron), then the keyboard-only run; record each in the findings register.
- Re-test every fixed finding and mark it verified; the register is the evidence artefact for the DoD a11y checkbox on every E15 story.
- Include one run at 200% browser zoom and one at 320 CSS px reflow width to cover WCAG 1.4.10/1.4.4 against the `SCR-153` responsive behaviour.

## Security notes
- Accessible names must not leak sensitive values: panel titles and window titles may include symbol and environment but never account ids, balances or API-key fragments.
- The environment band (DEMO/LIVE) must be conveyed to assistive tech in every floating window — a screen-reader user mistaking LIVE for DEMO is a safety issue, not a cosmetic one.

## Accessibility notes
- Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Criteria most at risk here: 2.1.1/2.1.2 keyboard & no trap, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 1.3.1 info & relationships (regions), 1.4.11 non-text contrast (drop zones, splitters, focus rings), 4.1.3 status messages (move/save announcements), 2.5.7 dragging movements (the explicit mandate for a non-drag alternative).
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for drop-zone and drag previews; verify no essential information is conveyed only by animation.

## Performance notes
- Live-region announcements must be throttled so a rapid sequence of dock operations does not flood the screen-reader queue; verify a burst of five moves produces a coherent, non-overlapping announcement sequence.
- The a11y layer must not cost frames: confirm via an `E15-Q04` sample that region/ARIA updates during a crosshair sweep do not appear in the frame budget.

## Observability
- CI publishes the axe-core JSON report per run as an artefact and trends violation counts, so a slow drift is visible rather than discovered at the E47 audit.
- The findings register links each defect to its ticket so the a11y rollup on the E15 epic DoD can be computed rather than asserted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe-core checks wired to CI for all listed screens/states; serious+critical gate enforced.
- [ ] Manual screen-reader matrix executed on NVDA/Firefox, VoiceOver/Safari and NVDA/Electron, with recordings attached.
- [ ] Keyboard-only run completed with zero blocking gaps, or gaps filed and fixed.
- [ ] Findings register published, every finding triaged, all blocking findings verified fixed.
- [ ] Announcement inventory signed off by the design-system accessibility owner.

## Dependencies
- `E15-S01`, `E15-S05`, `E15-S06` for the surfaces; `E15-Q02` for the harness; E05 design-system a11y tokens and CMP-214/216/218 definitions.

## Branch
`chore/e15-a11y-audit`

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-214, CMP-215, CMP-216, CMP-217, CMP-218, CMP-080..083
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020..029, SCR-011, SCR-153

title: Exploratory charters and cross-epic layout regression pack
body:
## Context
Scripted tests find the bugs you predicted. The layout system's worst defects are combinatorial — a panel type that misbehaves only when floated *and* in a sync group *and* restored from a saved workspace — and they are found by a skilled tester with a charter, not by a spec file. `03-testing-strategy.md` pairs black-box plans with session-based exploratory testing for exactly this reason.

E15 also needs a durable **regression pack**: because every subsequent epic (E18, E19, E21, E26, E30, E41) adds panel types into this dock tree, the pack is the contract that new panels must satisfy. Written once here, it is re-run per epic rather than re-invented.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 minutes each, with a debrief note per session) in `qa/exploratory/e15/`:
  1. *Combinatorial dock abuse* — nested splits, minimum sizes, rapid add/remove, undo, panel duplication, "copy panel link".
  2. *Workspace lifecycle under pressure* — many workspaces, long names, unicode/RTL names, duplicate-name collisions, rapid switching, switching during save.
  3. *Float and multi-monitor* — float, move to a second display, disconnect the display, restart, parent window closed while floating.
  4. *Sync-group edge behaviour* — mixed symbols/intervals, panes joining/leaving mid-interaction, replay-mode panes in a group with live panes.
  5. *Restore and degradation* — restore while offline, restore with a feature flag off, restore a workspace containing a panel type the user's role cannot see.
  6. *Density, theme and zoom* — three densities × two themes × 200% zoom × 1280×800 minimum, hunting overlap and clipping.
- **Regression pack** `qa/regression/e15-layout-pack.md`: ~40 cases, each fast and unambiguous, tagged `smoke` (10) / `full` (40), designed to be run against any build and explicitly re-runnable by other epics when they add a panel type, with a "new panel type checklist" (mounts lazily, unsubscribes when hidden, has an accessible name, has a panel menu, serializes and restores, honours density, survives float/re-dock).
- **Bug taxonomy** for this epic so triage is consistent: layout-corruption, persistence-loss, sync-leak, focus-loss, perf-regression, degradation-incorrect.

## Out of scope
- Automation of the charters (charters are, by definition, unscripted); valuable findings graduate into `E15-Q02`/`E15-Q03` as new specs.
- Security abuse cases — `E15-X02`.
- Panel-internal behaviour of other epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters are executed and debriefed
  Given the six charters
  When each session is run
  Then a debrief note records duration, coverage, findings, and any new spec proposed for automation

Scenario: The regression pack is executable by another epic
  Given an engineer on E18 adds a footprint panel type
  When they run the new-panel-type checklist from the pack
  Then they can confirm or refute dock compliance without reading E15's implementation

Scenario: Failure case - a charter finding is not lost
  Given a charter uncovers a layout-corruption defect
  Then it is filed with the taxonomy tag, a minimal reproduction, and either a new automated spec or a written justification for why it stays manual

Scenario: Edge case - role-restricted panel in a saved workspace
  Given a workspace containing an owner-only panel is opened by a viewer
  Then that panel is omitted with a clear notice and the rest of the workspace is usable, and this is covered by a pack case

Scenario: Smoke subset is fast
  When the 10 smoke cases are run
  Then they complete in under 15 minutes by hand on a staging build
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are time-boxed and chartered, not open-ended "click around"; each states a mission, an area, an oracle and the risk it targets.
- The regression pack deliberately avoids implementation vocabulary so it stays valid across the dock refactors that a long-lived terminal will inevitably have.
- The new-panel-type checklist should be linked from `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080 notes so panel authors find it without being told.

## Test plan
- Run all six charters before the E15 sign-off; re-run charters 1, 4 and 5 after any significant dock refactor.
- Run the full regression pack at the E15 sign-off and the smoke subset on every release candidate thereafter.
- Track the ratio of defects found by charters vs specs as a signal of whether automation is covering the right ground; report it in the epic retro.

## Security notes
- Charter 5 explicitly includes the role-visibility case: a saved or imported workspace must never cause a panel to render data outside the user's permissions, and the check is a client *and* server assertion (the API must refuse, not just the UI hide).
- Any charter finding that touches permissions, export contents or cross-user access is escalated to `E15-X02`/`E15-X04` rather than filed as an ordinary bug.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 6 includes a keyboard-only and a screen-reader segment; findings feed `E15-Q06`'s register rather than a separate list.
- The regression pack's new-panel-type checklist includes accessible name, keyboard menu and focus behaviour so a new panel cannot regress the epic's a11y baseline.

## Performance notes
- Charter 1 and 3 include a subjective smoothness oracle; anything suspicious is handed to `E15-Q04` for measurement rather than argued about.
- The pack's new-panel-type checklist includes lazy mount and hidden-tab unsubscribe after 30 s (`SCR-020`), the two properties that most often silently break the frame and bandwidth budgets.

## Observability
- Each session records the build sha and the analytics events observed, so a finding can be correlated with server logs later.
- Findings are tagged with the taxonomy in the tracker, enabling a per-tag trend across R1 and into E49 defect burn-down.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six charters executed with debrief notes committed.
- [ ] Regression pack published with smoke/full tagging and the new-panel-type checklist.
- [ ] All findings filed with taxonomy tags; graduating specs merged into the E2E suites.
- [ ] Pack linked from the component catalogue notes for CMP-080 and from the E15 epic.
- [ ] Smoke subset timed and confirmed under 15 minutes.

## Dependencies
- `E15-Q02`, `E15-Q03`, `E15-Q05` for stable surfaces and fixtures.

## Branch
`chore/e15-exploratory-regression`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (session-based exploratory testing, regression policy)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-024, SCR-027
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080, CMP-082, CMP-216

title: E15 QA sign-off: rollup, traceability evidence and R1 exit-gate input
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an Epic-level QA sign-off — "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA" — plus rolled-up coverage, a11y verification, perf numbers against budget, and zero open P0/P1 bugs, before E15 can be Done. E15 is also an input to the R1 "Charting alpha" exit gate: the workspace is what the R1 demo actually *is*.

This ticket is the gate itself: it does not test new ground, it assembles the evidence, runs the epic-level pass, and produces a single signed artefact that the Owner, the Architect and the release manager can read in ten minutes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Epic-level pass**: execute the full `E15-Q07` regression pack and the `E15-Q05` chaos pack against a release-candidate build, end to end, on both the web and Electron runners.
- **Evidence rollup** in `qa/signoff/e15-signoff.md`:
  - Traceability: US-LAY-001..008 → test cases → automation → result, sourced from the `E15-Q01` matrix.
  - Coverage: frontend line coverage for the layout/dock packages against the ≥80% threshold from the planning brief, with a named exception list if any.
  - Perf: the `E15-Q04` baseline table vs budgets (≥55 fps four order-flow panes, ≤3 s warm restore, ≤300 ms preset apply, ≤150 ms panel mount, ≤1 frame sync propagation, <350 KiB/s reference-workspace bandwidth).
  - a11y: `E15-Q06` register state — zero open blocking findings, axe-core CI green, screen-reader passes recorded.
  - Security: `E15-X04` review outcome and the disposition of every `E15-X01` threat.
  - Chaos: `E15-Q05` recovery-time table.
  - Defects: open bug list by severity with the assertion that no P0/P1 remains against E15 scope; P2/P3 carried forward with links into E49.
- **R1 exit-gate input**: a short section mapping E15 evidence onto the R1 exit criteria in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5, so the release manager does not have to re-derive it.
- **Demo script**: a 10-minute owner demo — create a workspace, build a 2×2, sync two panes, save, restart, restore, float a panel, export and re-import — used at the sprint review and reusable as a smoke script.
- **Sign-off record**: named sign-offs from the SDET, the Security engineer, the design-system a11y owner and the Owner, with dates.

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects (filed to owning stories or E49).
- Signing off other R1 epics.
- Production readiness review itself (`07-release-and-prr.md`, E44/E43 scope) — this feeds it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sign-off cannot pass with open blockers
  Given an open P1 bug against E15 scope
  When the sign-off is attempted
  Then it is refused and the epic stays out of Done until the bug is fixed or explicitly accepted by the Owner in writing

Scenario: Every story has evidence
  Given the traceability section
  Then each of US-LAY-001..008 shows at least one executed case with a pass result and a link to the evidence
  And any N/A carries a one-line reason per the DoR/DoD convention

Scenario: Failure case - a budget miss is stated, not hidden
  Given the four-order-flow-pane scenario measures 51 fps
  Then the sign-off records the miss, the owning ticket, and either a fix or an Owner-accepted risk with a deadline; it is never rounded up or omitted

Scenario: Edge case - a carried-forward defect is traceable
  Given a P2 defect is deferred
  Then it appears in the sign-off with a link to its E49 entry and an agreed milestone

Scenario: Demo is executed and accepted
  When the demo script is run at the sprint review
  Then the Owner records explicit acceptance on the E15 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Build the rollup from machine-readable sources where possible (coverage JSON, axe report JSON, `perf/budgets/e15.json`, the tracker API) so the document is regenerable rather than hand-copied and stale.
- Run the pass against a real release-candidate artefact, not a dev build, so packaging differences (Electron) are in scope.
- Sign-off is a point-in-time statement bound to a commit sha; record it, because "we signed off" without a sha is not evidence.

## Test plan
- The pass itself is the test plan: full regression pack + chaos pack + demo script on the RC, with results captured per case.
- Spot re-verification of five previously fixed defects chosen at random, to detect regressions in fixes rather than trusting the closed state.

## Security notes
- The sign-off explicitly asserts: exported workspaces contain no secrets or account bindings; cross-user workspace access returns 404; imports are schema-validated and size-bounded; role-restricted panels are enforced server-side.
- No sign-off is valid without the `E15-X04` security review outcome attached; an outstanding high-severity security finding blocks the gate regardless of functional results.

## Accessibility notes
- The a11y section must show axe-core green in CI, the manual screen-reader matrix executed, and zero open blocking findings; a11y is a gate, not a note.
- WCAG 2.2 AA conformance for the E15 screens is stated per screen, so E47 can audit deltas rather than start from scratch.

## Performance notes
- Every budget in the perf table is shown as measured vs target with pass/fail, plus the GPU/driver and fixture used, so the number is reproducible.
- Any budget carried as accepted risk names the E46 ticket that will close it.

## Observability
- Confirm the epic's analytics/audit events are flowing into the E04 pipeline in the RC build (`workspace.*`, `panel.*`, `layout.*`, `sync.*`) and that the ops dashboard shows them — an epic that ships blind is not Done.
- Record the dashboard link and a screenshot of the events landing, as evidence for the DoD observability item.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full regression and chaos passes executed on the RC (web + Electron) with results recorded.
- [ ] `qa/signoff/e15-signoff.md` published with traceability, coverage, perf, a11y, security, chaos and defect sections, bound to a commit sha.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects against E15 scope, or written Owner acceptance.
- [ ] Named sign-offs from SDET, Security, a11y owner and Owner recorded.
- [ ] Demo executed at sprint review with acceptance recorded on the epic; R1 exit-gate section handed to the release manager.

## Dependencies
- All E15 QA tickets (`E15-Q01`..`E15-Q07`) and the security review `E15-X04`; an RC build of the E15 stories.
