title: Linked vs independent price scaling with incompatible-link refusal
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-004** (Should) — "per-pane control over scale linking, so that comparisons are meaningful". Its three scenarios: two scale-linked panes on the same symbol zoom their price axes together; unlinking gives a pane its own scale with the unlinked state shown on the axis; and linking panes showing different symbols with very different price magnitudes is **refused with an explanation and percentage-scale suggested**. NFR: state persisted per pane in the workspace.

That third scenario is the point of the Story. Linking a $90,000 BTC axis to a $0.6 DOGE axis produces a chart where one series is a flat line at the edge — technically correct, analytically useless, and a trap a trader falls into once and distrusts forever. The right behaviour is to refuse and offer percentage scaling, which the engine already supports: `26-chart-engine-design.md` specifies price scale modes linear/log/percent/inverted, and `layout_panes.scale_mode` (`auto | linked | manual | log`) already models the persisted state in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1.

Surfaces: **SCR-023** (the Y-scale row deferred from E15-S04) and **SCR-043** price-scale/time-scale context menus.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scale-link as a sync axis carried by the SyncBus (`priceLevel`/scale range), applied per frame like every other axis.
- Per-pane `scale_mode` persisted to `layout_panes.scale_mode` and restored by E15-S03.
- **Link compatibility check**: linking is permitted when members share a symbol, or when their price magnitudes are within a configured ratio; outside that, linking is refused with a plain-language explanation naming both symbols and their magnitudes, and offering "Use percentage scale" as a one-click alternative that links the panes in percent mode instead.
- **Unlinked affordance on the axis** (SCR-043, SCR-023): the price axis visibly indicates whether it is linked, independent or manual, in text — not by a colour or an icon alone.
- Price-axis context-menu entries (SCR-043): Auto / Linked / Manual / Log / Percent, with the same refusal path when Linked is chosen incompatibly.
- Interaction with log and percent modes: linking two panes in different scale modes normalises to the shared mode and says so.

## Out of scope
- The scale implementation itself (linear/log/percent/inverted maths, axis decimation) — **E11**.
- Time-range sync — **E15-T03**/**E15-S04**.
- Cross-symbol *drawing* sync — forbidden by US-DRAW-009.
- Per-indicator-pane scale linking within a single chart (panes of one chart already share the time axis by construction, §4.2).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Linked scaling propagates a price-axis zoom
  Given two panes showing BTCUSDT are scale-linked
  When the price axis is zoomed in one
  Then the other applies the same price range within one frame

Scenario: Unlinking is visible on the axis
  When a pane is unlinked
  Then its price axis shows in text that it is independent, and zooming it no longer affects the other pane

Scenario: Incompatible link is refused with a useful alternative
  Given one pane shows BTCUSDT around 90000 and another shows a symbol around 0.6
  When the trader tries to scale-link them
  Then linking is refused, the explanation names both symbols and their magnitudes, and "Use percentage scale" is offered
  And accepting it links both panes in percent mode with a correct shared scale

Scenario: Mode normalisation is disclosed
  Given one pane is in log mode and another in linear mode
  When they are scale-linked
  Then both adopt the same mode and a notice states which mode was applied and why

Scenario: Scale state persists per pane
  Given a workspace where pane 1 is linked, pane 2 is manual and pane 3 is log
  When the workspace is saved, the app restarted and the workspace reopened
  Then each pane's scale_mode is exactly as it was

Scenario: A linked partner disappearing does not break the survivor
  Given two scale-linked panes
  When one is closed
  Then the remaining pane keeps its current range, reverts to independent, and states that it is no longer linked
```

## Technical notes / design
Link compatibility is decided on order of magnitude, not on symbol equality alone: same-symbol always links; otherwise compare `log10` of the mid prices and refuse beyond a configured threshold (default 1 decade, tunable). That keeps BTC/ETH comparisons available while catching the BTC/DOGE trap, and it degrades gracefully as new instruments list.

Percent mode is the escape hatch rather than a consolation prize — for comparing two instruments it is the analytically correct scale, so the refusal copy should present it as the better tool, not as a fallback.

Scale propagation rides the existing SyncBus axis path, so it inherits per-frame scheduling and loop suppression; there is no second mechanism to keep consistent.

A closed partner must not leave a pane silently following nothing: unlinking on partner loss is explicit and announced, which also avoids a stale group id persisting into the saved layout.

## Test plan
Unit: compatibility predicate across magnitude pairs (same symbol, within a decade, beyond a decade, zero/at-edge prices), mode normalisation rules, partner-loss transition. Component: axis affordance rendering for each state, refusal dialog copy including both magnitudes, SCR-043 menu entries. Integration: two real engines linked, zoom propagation within one frame; percent-mode link correctness against a known fixture where both series' percentage moves are pre-computed. E2E: link, unlink, refuse, accept percent, save, restart, verify persistence. A11y: axe on the menu and refusal dialog; assertion that link state is text on the axis.

## Security notes
None beyond the Epic baseline — client-side view state persisted through E15-T01's validated write path, no new endpoint, no user-supplied content beyond an enum. `scale_mode` is constrained by the `lp_scale` CHECK constraint server-side, so a tampered client cannot store an arbitrary value.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Link state on the price axis is conveyed in text ("Independent scale", "Linked to group A"), never by an icon or colour alone, satisfying SC 1.4.1. The refusal is a plain-language explanation naming both symbols and their price magnitudes — not an error code — and the suggested alternative is an actionable, keyboard-reachable button. Mode changes announce once. The price-axis context menu (SCR-043) is fully keyboard-operable with type-ahead.

## Performance notes
Scale propagation is one more axis on an already frame-scheduled bus; it must not add measurable cost to the ≤4 ms six-pane budget, and is measured alongside E15-T03's sweep. Percent-mode recomputation happens in the engine's existing scale pass, not per frame in application code.

## Observability
`sync.axis_toggled {axis: 'scale'}`, `scale.link_refused {reason: 'magnitude', symbols}`, `scale.percent_suggested_accepted`, `scale.mode_changed {from, to}`. The refusal counter is the interesting one: if it fires often, the threshold or the copy needs revisiting.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the scale-link module.
- [ ] Refusal copy reviewed by design/content and verified to name both symbols and magnitudes.
- [ ] axe-core green; axis link state verified as text.
- [ ] Persistence across restart demonstrated.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-S04** (sync groups and axis surface), **E11** (price scale modes incl. percent and log). Persisted by **E15-S03**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-scale-linking`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-004, US-CHART-007; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-043; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-218, CMP-041; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-004 row; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`lp_scale`, `scale_mode`); `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2 and the price-scale modes.

1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-041, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-218, SCR-023, SCR-043
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e15-scale-linking`
- PR title: `E15-S05: Linked vs independent price scaling with incompatible-link refusal`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-S05)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1

**Done means**

- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the scale-link module.
- [ ] Refusal copy reviewed by design/content and verified to name both symbols and magnitudes.
- [ ] axe-core green; axis link state verified as text.

**Do NOT**

title: Workspace export and import with schema validation and redaction (SCR-026)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-007** (Should) — "export and import a workspace file, so that I can move a setup between machines or share it with a manager". Its scenarios: export produces "a versioned JSON file containing no secrets and no account bindings"; import by a manager applies panes and settings and "any account-scoped element is dropped with a clear report"; and a file from a newer app version "is refused with the versions stated rather than applying partially". Its NFR is the security requirement: "exported files are schema-validated on import; never embed keys, tokens or account ids."

Surface: **SCR-026** Workspace import (file drop or picker, diff-style preview) and the "export as template" action on **SCR-025**. Endpoint: `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export`. Components: **CMP-067** FileDrop, **CMP-234** ValidationPanel, CMP-027 ErrorState, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog.

This Story deliberately carries the `security` label and a Security perspective: it is the only place in this Epic where data leaves the trust boundary in one direction and untrusted data enters in the other. Both directions need to be treated as adversarial — the export because a workspace file will end up in a chat message, the import because a file from a colleague is indistinguishable from a file from an attacker.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Export**: `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` returning a versioned document `{ schemaVersion, appVersion, exportedAt, workspace, layouts[], panes[] }`, built by an **allow-list** projection — fields are copied in by name, never by spreading a row — so a future column cannot leak by default.
- **Redaction, enforced server-side**: no API keys, no tokens, no account ids, no user ids, no trade-group ids, no `exchange_account_id` in any `pane_config`; account-scoped pane settings are dropped at export time and the dropped set is reported in the file itself so the importer can be told.
- **Import (SCR-026)**: drop or pick a JSON file; parse and validate **in a worker**; show a diff-style preview before anything is applied (panels added, symbols referenced, settings dropped, unknown kinds dropped) as a table, not a canvas; apply on explicit confirmation, creating a new workspace rather than overwriting an existing one.
- **Validation, in order**: size cap (default 2 MB, rejected above); JSON parse with depth and node-count limits; JSON Schema validation of the whole document; `schemaVersion` compatibility check; per-pane validation against the pane registry and the `lp_kind`/`lp_slot`/`lp_scale` enums; only then application.
- **Version handling**: an older compatible version is migrated forward and the migration is reported; a **newer** version is refused outright with both versions stated (never partially applied); an unknown/malformed document is rejected with the offending key named.
- **Unknown panel kinds** are dropped and listed by name in the report rather than silently discarded.
- **Reporting**: the post-import report (CMP-234 ValidationPanel) lists every dropped, migrated and remapped element as text, with counts.

## Out of scope
- Sharing a workspace *inside* the app (user-to-user, links, permissions) — R5 collaboration.
- Rule import/export (SCR-089 shares components but belongs to **E35/E36**).
- Importing drawings or indicator presets that reference objects the importing user does not own — those references are dropped and reported; deep-copying them is out of R1 scope.
- Any binary or compressed container format; R1 exports plain JSON so a human can inspect it before sending it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Export contains no secrets under inspection
  Given a workspace whose panes were bound to accounts and whose user has API keys configured
  When it is exported and the resulting JSON is searched
  Then it contains no API key material, no token, no account id, no trade-group id and no user id
  And the account-scoped settings that were removed are listed in the file's own report section

Scenario: Import previews before it applies
  When a valid workspace file is dropped onto SCR-026
  Then a table preview lists the panels to be added, the symbols referenced and everything that will be dropped
  And nothing is created until the trader confirms

Scenario: A newer schema version is refused, not partially applied
  Given a file whose schemaVersion is greater than the app supports
  When it is imported
  Then the import is refused with both versions stated, and no workspace, layout or pane is created

Scenario: A malformed or oversized file is rejected safely
  When a 50 MB file, a truncated JSON file, or a document with 10000 nested nodes is dropped
  Then the import is rejected with a specific reason, the UI thread never blocks for more than 500 ms, and the app does not crash

Scenario: Unknown panel kinds are dropped and named
  Given a file containing a pane of a kind this build does not know
  When it is imported
  Then that pane is dropped, its kind is named in the report, and the remaining panes are applied

Scenario: A manager importing an owner's workspace gets a usable result
  Given an owner exports a workspace containing account-scoped panels
  When a manager imports it
  Then panes and settings apply, account-scoped elements are absent, and the report states exactly what was dropped and why

Scenario: Import cannot overwrite an existing workspace
  When a file is imported whose name matches an existing workspace
  Then a new workspace is created with a disambiguated name, and the existing one is untouched

Scenario: A 2 MB file validates without blocking
  When a 2 MB valid layout file is imported
  Then validation completes in under 500 ms off the main thread and the UI remains responsive throughout
```

## Technical notes / design
Redaction is server-side, in the export endpoint, because a client-side redactor can be bypassed by anyone who can call the API — and because the server is the only place that knows the full shape of what it stores. The allow-list projection is the design decision that matters most here: a deny-list would silently start leaking the day someone adds a column to `layout_panes`.

Validation order is deliberate and cheap-first: size, then parse limits, then schema, then semantics. A 50 MB file must be rejected before it is parsed, not after.

Parsing in a worker is both a performance requirement (SCR-026: 2 MB in ≤500 ms without blocking) and a containment one — a pathological document stalls a worker, not the trading UI.

Import always creates, never overwrites. Overwrite semantics would need conflict resolution, a confirmation flow and an undo; creating a new workspace makes the destructive case impossible and costs the user one rename.

The file carries its own report section so that a trader who exports today and imports in six months, in a different build, can still see what the export chose to omit.

## Test plan
Unit: allow-list projection over a row containing every sensitive field (asserting each is absent from the output), schema validation positive and negative cases, version compatibility matrix (older/equal/newer/absent), unknown-kind dropping, name disambiguation. Security: a fuzz corpus of malformed, oversized, deeply nested, duplicate-key and prototype-pollution-shaped JSON documents (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`) asserting rejection without side effects; a regression test that fails if any new column appears in the export without being added to the allow-list. Contract: schemathesis on the export endpoint. E2E: export from user A, import as user B, verify the report and the absence of account-scoped elements; newer-version refusal; oversized rejection. A11y: axe on SCR-026; keyboard-only file selection; the diff preview read as a table. Perf: 2 MB in ≤500 ms off-thread.

## Security notes
This is the Epic's primary security ticket. **Outbound**: the export is treated as public-by-assumption — a workspace file will be pasted into chat, so the guarantee is not "we did not include keys" but "the projection cannot include anything not named in the allow-list", plus a test that fails when a new column is added without a decision. No keys, tokens, account ids, user ids or trade-group ids (US-LAY-007 NFR, `04-security-program.md`). **Inbound**: the file is fully untrusted input — size-capped, depth- and node-capped, schema-validated, semantically validated against the pane registry and the database CHECK enums, parsed off-thread, and never used to construct a component, open a window or issue a request until validated. Prototype-pollution shapes are explicitly tested. Pane titles and workspace names from an imported file are user content, length-capped and rendered as text. STRIDE: Spoofing (a file claiming a foreign schema version) → refused; Tampering (crafted pane kinds) → registry allow-list; Information disclosure (export leakage) → allow-list projection; Denial of service (billion-laughs-shaped JSON) → size/depth caps and worker isolation; Elevation of privilege (account-scoped panes surviving into another user's session) → dropped server-side at export and again at import.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The file input has a visible label and the drop zone has a keyboard alternative — a file cannot be importable by pointer only (SCR-026). The import diff is a real table with headers, not a canvas or a graphic. Validation errors are listed as text naming the offending key, with an error summary at the top linking to each item (CMP-234). The refusal for a newer version states both version numbers in prose. The post-import report is announced politely and remains readable after dismissal.

## Performance notes

title: Responsive layout and measured reduced-capability profile (SCR-153)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-008** (Should) — "the layout adapts to a small screen and weaker GPU, so that the app is usable everywhere". Scenarios: under 1280 px wide, "panels collapse into a tabbed arrangement with no loss of function"; when a weak GPU is detected the app "suggests a reduced profile (lower heatmap depth, 200 ms cadence, fewer panes) and applies it on acceptance"; and restoring the full profile is remembered per device "with the measured frame cost shown". Its NFR is the one that shapes the implementation: "capability detection based on measured frame time, not on user-agent strings."

Surfaces: **SCR-021** (the collapse behaviour) and **SCR-153** Degraded-mode state, whose GPU-fallback variant this Story owns. Components: **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-069** InfoPanel, **CMP-028** Callout, **CMP-227** EstimatedBadge.

**E15-K01** already produced the probe and the reduced-profile config object; this Story is where they become user-visible behaviour. SCR-153's governing principle applies directly: "the automatic feature-shedding is disclosed, never silent", and "trading remains possible or is explicitly blocked — never ambiguous".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Responsive collapse**: below 1280 px the dock tree collapses into a tabbed arrangement — every panel still reachable, none removed, no function lost; above the breakpoint the previous arrangement is restored exactly (the collapse is a view transform, not a destructive layout mutation).
- **Capability-driven suggestion**: on boot, E15-K01's probe classifies the device; a `reduced` classification raises a non-blocking suggestion stating the **measured** frame time and exactly what the reduced profile changes, applied only on acceptance.
- **Reduced profile application**: the config object from E15-K01 — lower heatmap depth, 200 ms cadence, reduced max panes, non-focused pane update rate — applied through the existing panel settings, not through a parallel code path.
- **Manual override and memory**: the trader can restore the full profile at any time; the choice is remembered **per device** (local, not server-side, since it describes hardware rather than preference), and the measured frame cost is shown alongside the control.
- **SCR-153 GPU-fallback banner** (CMP-092): `role="status"`, naming precisely what is degraded and what still works, with a manual "reduce quality" control and an explicit exit/restore state.
- **Panel-level disclosure**: panels whose fidelity was reduced carry a badge repeating the specific degradation in their accessible name (SCR-153), using CMP-227's convention for estimated/reduced data.
- **Pane-count coupling**: `recommendedMaxPanes` drops on a reduced profile, so E15-S01's add-pane confirmation quotes the reduced number — one source of truth, not two.

## Out of scope
- The measurement and the probe itself — **E15-K01**.
- Non-GPU degradation causes on SCR-153 (exchange WS down, recorder down, rule engine down) — owned by **E08**, **E16**, **E35** respectively; this Story implements only the GPU/capability variant and the shared banner shell it plugs into.
- The `degraded-2d` canvas fallback renderer — **E11**.
- Mobile/touch layouts — Android is out of scope per the owner decision of 2026-09-14; the narrow-viewport case here is a laptop or a small desktop window, not a phone.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Narrow viewport collapses without losing function
  Given a 2x2 workspace and a window resized below 1280 px
  When the collapse occurs
  Then every panel remains reachable as a tab, none is removed, and each keeps its symbol, interval and settings

Scenario: Widening restores the exact prior arrangement
  Given the layout collapsed to tabs at 1100 px
  When the window is widened past 1280 px again
  Then the original tree, sizes and focus are restored exactly, and no WebGL context was lost during either transition

Scenario: A weak device gets a measured suggestion, not a guess
  Given the capability probe measured a p95 frame time above the reduced-profile threshold
  When the workspace loads
  Then a non-blocking suggestion states the measured frame time and lists exactly what the reduced profile changes
  And nothing is applied until the trader accepts

Scenario: Detection never consults the user agent
  When the capability detection code path is inspected
  Then no branch depends on navigator.userAgent, the GPU renderer string, or any device allow-list

Scenario: Shedding is disclosed per panel
  Given the reduced profile is active
  Then the degraded-mode banner names what is reduced and what still works
  And each affected panel carries a badge whose accessible name states its specific reduction

Scenario: The override is remembered per device
  Given the trader restores the full profile on a laptop
  When they reopen the app on that laptop
  Then the full profile is still in effect and the measured frame cost is shown next to the control
  And the same account on the reference machine is unaffected

Scenario: Trading surfaces are never the thing that gets shed
  Given the reduced profile is active under load
  Then order entry and position display keep their full budget, and only optional visual work is reduced
```

## Technical notes / design
The collapse is a presentation transform over the same tree — tabbing every leaf into one tabset for display while the stored layout is unchanged. That is what makes the restore exact and keeps the transition free of GL churn; a destructive re-layout would remount canvases twice per resize.

The suggestion is non-blocking by design. A modal on boot that says the machine is slow is both insulting and easy to dismiss wrongly; a persistent, dismissible suggestion that quotes a number the trader can verify respects them and is more likely to be accepted.

Storing the profile choice per device rather than per user is a deliberate split from every other setting in this Epic: it describes the hardware in front of the trader, and syncing it to a workspace would mean a laptop's compromise following them onto the reference machine.

Routing the reduced profile through the existing panel settings rather than a separate "degraded mode" branch keeps one code path under test. A parallel path is how degraded modes rot into something nobody has run in six months.

SCR-153's protection rule — shed optional work, never order entry or position display — is stated in the config object's ordering, so what is shed first is data, reviewable in a diff.

## Test plan
Unit: collapse/restore transform preserving tree identity, profile config application, per-device persistence, pane-count coupling. Static: a CI assertion (lint rule or grep) that no user-agent or GPU-renderer string appears in a capability branch — this is the only way the NFR stays true over time. Component: banner variants, panel badges, suggestion accept/dismiss, restore control with the measured number. Integration: throttled-CPU run classifying as reduced, accepting, and verifying the applied knobs. E2E: resize below and above the breakpoint asserting no GL context loss and exact restore; per-device memory across relaunch. A11y: axe on SCR-153 and the collapsed tabbed arrangement; screen-reader pass confirming the banner is `role="status"` and states cause plus what still works in plain sentences. Perf: verify the reduced profile actually improves measured frame time on the throttled profile — a degradation that does not help is a bug.

## Security notes
The capability measurement is timing data about the local device. It must stay local: stored in device-scoped storage, never sent to the server with user identifiers, and never used as a fingerprinting signal — a high-resolution device performance profile tied to an account is exactly the kind of correlatable identifier a self-hosted trading terminal should not be creating. The analytics event from E15-K01 carries a coarse bucket, not a raw timing series. No other new surface.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The collapsed arrangement uses the standard tabs pattern with arrow-key navigation and no function removed — "responsive" must not mean "fewer capabilities for the person on the smaller screen". The degraded banner is `role="status"` naming exactly which capability is degraded and what still works, in plain sentences, and per-panel badges repeat the specific degradation in their accessible name (SCR-153). The suggestion is keyboard-reachable, dismissible, and never steals focus. Reflow at 1280 px and below satisfies SC 1.4.10 without horizontal scrolling or loss of content.

## Performance notes
This Story is the mitigation for **R8 Browser/GPU compat**: it is what keeps a weak device above the 30 fps floor (roadmap §5.3.2) instead of stuttering silently. Collapse and restore transitions must cost no GL context churn; the reduced profile must produce a measurable frame-time improvement on the throttled profile, recorded against E15-K01's baseline; the probe adds no cost after its warm-up window.

## Observability
`degraded.entered {cause: 'gpu', sheddedFeatures}`, `degraded.exited {durationMs}`, `capability.profile_suggested {measuredFrameMs}`, `capability.profile_accepted`, `capability.profile_restored {measuredFrameMs}`, `layout.collapsed {viewportWidth}`, `layout.expanded`. Acceptance rate against suggestion count tells us whether the copy is convincing or the threshold is wrong.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the responsive and capability modules.
- [ ] CI assertion present that no capability branch reads a user-agent or GPU renderer string.
- [ ] Reduced profile demonstrated to improve measured frame time on the throttled profile; before/after recorded.
- [ ] SCR-153 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waiver recorded; its checklist items for the GPU-budget cause verified.
- [ ] axe-core green; reflow verified at 1280 px and below; manual screen-reader pass of the banner.
- [ ] Confirmed that trading surfaces retain full budget under the reduced profile.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-S02** (panels, tabsets and the view menu must exist to collapse into), **E15-K01** (the probe and the reduced-profile config object).

## Branch
`feat/e15-responsive-degraded`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-008, US-DOM-005, US-SET-008; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-021, SCR-153; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-028, CMP-069, CMP-092, CMP-227, CMP-214, CMP-215, CMP-216; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-008 row; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 2; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1 and #14; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (SC 1.4.10); `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R8.

title: Abuse cases: malicious workspace import, cross-user access and layout DoS
body: ## Context `E15-X01` enumerates the threats; this ticket tries to make them real. The highest-value target is the workspace import path (US-LAY-007, `SCR-026`): a file authored by one user, handed to another, parsed and turned into application state. Second is the authorization boundary — `workspaces:*` is scoped `self`, and the only way to know the scope is enforced is to attack it as another user. Third is resource abuse: an unbounded layout document or a write-storm is a cheap self-hosted DoS. These are adversarial tests, deliberately separate from `E15-Q01`'s functional negatives: QA asks "does the error message appear?", this ticket asks "can I make the app do something it should refuse?". ## Scope / Deliverables - Abuse-case suite `security/abuse/e15/` with automated cases where possible and a manual playbook where not, covering each `SR-E15-nn`: - **Malicious import corpus**: unknown pane kinds; `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys (prototype pollution); deeply nested trees (1000 levels); 100k panes; 50 MB file; NaN/Infinity/huge numbers in grid coordinates; duplicate `slot_index`; negative and fractional sizes; strings of 1 MB in names; null bytes; invalid UTF-8. - **Injection through names**: workspace/layout/pane names containing ``, `javascript:` URLs, RTL-override and zero-width characters, and template-ish `{{7*7}}` payloads — asserted safe at every sink: tab label, panel header (CMP-082), panel menu (CMP-216), live-region announcement, Electron window title (`SCR-027`), export filename, and any log line. - **Id smuggling**: import a file asserting another user's `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `chart_template_id`, or an `account_id` binding; assert ids are regenerated and account bindings dropped with a report. - **Cross-user access**: user B calls `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{A's id}` and `/layouts/{A's id}`, including id-in-body vs id-in-path mismatch and a nested `layoutId` belonging to another workspace; expected 404 with no existence disclosure and no timing oracle. - **Privilege**: a viewer importing a workspace containing an owner-only panel type or a trading panel; assert server-side refusal, not UI hiding. - **Resource abuse**: creating workspaces/layouts/panes past the documented caps; a `PUT` write-storm beating the 2-second debounce; concurrent saves from 10 tabs; assert 429/422 with backoff and no unbounded growth in Postgres. - **Export leakage**: diff a full export against the `E15-X01` allow-list; grep for token-shaped, key-shaped and uuid-shaped values; assert no account id, user id, session material or API-key fragment appears. - **CSRF / clickjacking on layout mutations**: cross-origin `PUT` attempts and framing the workspace page. - A **findings report** with severity (CVSS-style rating per `04-security-program.md`), reproduction, and the fix ticket. ## Out of scope - Auth/session attacks (E09's abuse cases) beyond using them as the entry condition. - Network-level and infrastructure attacks (E43 pen-test). - Fuzzing the WS protocol (E17). ## Acceptance criteria ```gherkin Scenario: Malicious import is refused safely Given a layout file containing a __proto__ key and a 1000-level nested tree When it is imported Then the import is rejected with a stated reason, no object prototype is modified, the UI stays responsive, and the existing workspace is unchanged Scenario: Names cannot execute Given a workspace named with an XSS payload When it is rendered in the tab, panel header, panel menu, announcement and Electron window title Then the payload is displayed as inert text at every sink and no script executes Scenario: Failure case - cross-user access must not disclose existence Given user B requests user A's workspace id Then the response is 404 with a generic body, and the response time is not measurably different from a request for a non-existent id Scenario: Edge case - id smuggling is neutralised Given an import file asserting another user's chart_template_id and an account binding When it is imported Then new ids are generated, the account binding is dropped, and the user is shown a report listing exactly what was dropped Scenario: Resource caps hold Given an attempt to create panes beyond the documented cap or to PUT the layout 100 times per second Then the API responds 422 or 429 with backoff guidance, database growth stays bounded, and no save from a legitimate client is lost ``` ## Technical notes / design - Drive the import corpus at both layers: the UI (`SCR-026`, worker-parsed, so also check the worker does not become the unguarded path) and the API directly, since a UI-only guard is not a guard. - Prototype-pollution checks need a post-condition assertion on `Object.prototype` and on a canary object, not merely "no crash". - Timing-oracle testing for 404-vs-403 should use a statistical comparison over many samples rather than a single request pair. - Reuse the `E15-Q02` seeding helpers for multi-user setup so the abuse suite starts from a realistic, RBAC-correct baseline. - Where a finding is a missing bound rather than a bug, the fix is a documented cap in `22-api-openapi.yaml` plus a 422 — record it as a contract change, not a silent server tweak. ## Test plan - Run the full suite against a staging build before the `E15-X04` review and again on the release candidate. - Each finding gets a regression test in the appropriate suite so it cannot silently return; high-severity findings graduate into the PR gate. - Re-run the export-leakage diff whenever the export schema changes — it is the cheapest control for the most sensitive output. ## Security notes - Findings are triaged per `04-security-program.md`: Critical/High block the epic; Medium needs a fix or a dated accepted risk; Low may be deferred to E43 with a link. - The corpus itself is stored as test data with a README warning; it must never be shipped in a production bundle, and CI asserts it is excluded from the build output. - Anything found here that also applies to other user-authored documents (rules import `SCR-089`, chart templates) is escalated to those epics rather than fixed only locally. ## Accessibility notes - The rejection and dropped-elements reports are the user's only feedback in every attack-adjacent path; cases assert they are text, keyboard-reachable, announced, and name the offending key (`SCR-026`) without echoing raw attacker-controlled content unescaped. - Verify that an RTL-override or zero-width payload in a name cannot visually spoof another workspace's label in the switcher (CMP-073). ## Performance notes - Validation must fail fast: an oversized or deeply nested document is rejected within the `SCR-026` ≤500 ms worker budget rather than by exhausting memory; cases assert main-thread responsiveness during rejection. - The write-storm case asserts the API's rate limiting does not degrade the legitimate debounced path measured in `E15-Q04`. ## Observability - Every rejection must emit `layout.import_rejected{reason}` with a bounded reason enum, and repeated cross-user 404s from one principal must be visible in the ops dashboard as a probing signal with a documented alert threshold. - Cases assert that no attacker-controlled string is written raw into logs (log injection), and that log lines carry a correlation id. ## Definition of Done - [ ] Abuse suite merged with the full corpus and multi-user fixtures. - [ ] All `SR-E15-nn` requirements from `E15-X01` exercised by at least one case. - [ ] Findings report published; Critical/High fixed and verified; Medium fixed or Owner-accepted with a date. - [ ] Regression tests added for every finding; corpus excluded from production bundles (CI-enforced). - [ ] Results handed to `E15-X04` for the epic security review. ## Dependencies - `E15-X01` (requirements), `E15-S02` (persistence), `E15-S07` (export/import); `E15-Q02` seeding helpers; E09 for multi-user RBAC fixtures. ## Branch `chore/e15-abuse-cases` ## References - title: SAST/DAST rules and CI security gates for the workspace document surface
body:
## Context
A threat model and a round of abuse testing protect the code as it is today. Automated rules protect it against next quarter's well-meaning change — the one that adds a convenient `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to a panel header, or relaxes the import schema to accept an extra field "just for now". `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (OWASP ZAP) in CI; this ticket makes those tools actually *know about* the E15 surface instead of running generic rules over it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** in `security/semgrep/e15/`:
  - Ban `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML` and `document.write` anywhere in the layout/dock packages and in anything rendering workspace-derived names.
  - Flag any Electron `BrowserWindow` title, tooltip or menu label built from unescaped workspace/pane data.
  - Flag `JSON.parse` of imported files that is not immediately followed by the project's schema validator, and flag validator calls that pass `additionalProperties: true` or omit depth/size bounds.
  - Flag assignment of client-supplied `id`, `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `chart_template_id` or account fields on the import/create paths (the id-regeneration rule from `E15-X01`).
  - Flag workspace queries lacking a `user_id` predicate — the `scope: self` enforcement rule — in the backend workspace repository.
  - Flag new `/workspaces*` handlers missing an `x-rbac` annotation or a rate-limit decorator.
- **CodeQL** query pack additions for taint flow from the import/parse entry points to DOM and window-title sinks, run on the frontend and API code.
- **Bandit/pip-audit/npm audit/Trivy** wiring confirmed to cover the new packages; the schema-validation dependency pinned and watched.
- **Secret scanning**: a rule asserting that no fixture workspace/export file in the repo contains key-shaped, token-shaped or account-id-shaped values, plus a CI check that the `E15-X02` abuse corpus is excluded from production bundles.
- **DAST (OWASP ZAP)**: an authenticated scan profile for the `/workspaces*` endpoints and the workspace page, with the import endpoint included and a tuned false-positive baseline so the job is trusted rather than ignored.
- **Gate policy**: which findings fail the build (High+ SAST, any new secret, any DAST High) vs which open a ticket, documented in the security README so the gate is predictable.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings the rules surface (filed to owning stories).
- The broader org-wide SAST baseline (E03/E43) — this extends it.
- Runtime WAF/Tailscale network controls (infra).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A regression is caught by the rule, not by a person
  Given a PR that renders a workspace name with dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep job fails, names the rule and the line, and links the E15 threat model entry

Scenario: Scope enforcement is machine-checked
  Given a new workspace query written without a user_id predicate
  When CI runs
  Then the rule fails the build with an explanation of the scope:self requirement

Scenario: Failure case - noisy rules are not allowed to ship
  Given a proposed rule that produces more than a documented false-positive rate on the current codebase
  Then it is tuned or downgraded to warning before merge, so the gate stays credible

Scenario: Edge case - DAST authenticates correctly
  Given the ZAP profile
  When the scan runs
  Then it is authenticated as a real seeded user, exercises the import endpoint, and its baseline is committed so new alerts are visible as a diff

Scenario: Fixtures leak nothing
  Given the repository's workspace fixtures and export samples
  When the secret-scanning rule runs
  Then no key-shaped, token-shaped or account-id-shaped value is present
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rules are written against the real code paths and validated by running them over both the current codebase (expect zero findings after fixes) and the `E15-X02` corpus and a set of deliberately-vulnerable snippets (expect a finding each) — a rule with no proven true-positive is decoration.
- Prefer narrow, high-signal rules scoped by path over broad bans that teams learn to suppress; every suppression must carry a reason comment, and CI rejects bare suppressions.
- The DAST baseline must be committed and reviewed; an un-baselined ZAP job is a job everyone ignores within two sprints.
- Keep the CI wall-clock impact bounded: run the full pack nightly and the fast subset on PRs, following the E03 CI conventions.

## Test plan
- Rule unit tests: each Semgrep rule ships with a passing and a failing fixture in the standard Semgrep test format, run in CI.
- Validate the CodeQL taint queries against a deliberately introduced sink and confirm the alert appears in the PR.
- Run the ZAP profile against staging, triage every alert once, and record the baseline; re-run after the `E15-X02` fixes land.

## Security notes
- These gates implement `SR-E15-nn` requirements from `E15-X01` as enforceable controls; the mapping rule → requirement is recorded in the rules README.
- Gate policy must be explicit about what blocks a release versus what files a ticket, so a security finding is never quietly bypassed under sprint pressure.
- Scanning artefacts (SARIF, ZAP reports) are retained per the security program's evidence retention rules and are inputs to the E43 pen-test scoping.

## Accessibility notes
- One rule targets an a11y-adjacent security control: any code path that renders an error or rejection message must route through the app's announced-message helper, so security feedback cannot regress into a silent or visual-only state.
- CI reporting itself is plain text/SARIF, readable without colour, so a colour-blind reviewer can triage from the log.

## Performance notes
- PR-gate subset target ≤3 minutes; full pack nightly ≤20 minutes. If the DAST scan exceeds its window it is moved to nightly-only rather than being allowed to slow every PR into irrelevance.
- Rules must not require building the app; they run on source, keeping the gate cheap.

## Observability
- All findings publish SARIF to the code-scanning dashboard with the E15 rule ids, so trend and MTTR per rule are measurable.
- A weekly report of suppressions added is generated, because suppression growth is the leading indicator of a gate losing its meaning.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Semgrep rule pack merged with passing/failing fixtures and a rule → `SR-E15-nn` mapping.
- [ ] CodeQL taint queries merged and demonstrated to catch a seeded sink.
- [ ] ZAP authenticated profile and committed baseline in place; nightly job green.
- [ ] Secret-scanning rule for fixtures and the bundle-exclusion check enforced in CI.
- [ ] Gate policy documented; zero outstanding High findings on the E15 packages.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (requirements), `E15-S07` (import/export code to scan); E03 CI pipeline; E09 seeded users for authenticated DAST.

## Branch
`chore/e15-sast-dast-rules`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/SCA/DAST tooling and gates)
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*` (`x-rbac` annotations)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-026, SCR-027

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e15-sast-dast-rules`
- PR title: `E15-X03: SAST/DAST rules and CI security gates for the workspace document surface`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-X03)
- Required reviewers: `infra/` (@CandleViewer/devsecops), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/security, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, security

**Done means**

- [ ] CodeQL taint queries merged and demonstrated to catch a seeded sink.
- [ ] ZAP authenticated profile and committed baseline in place; nightly job green.
- [ ] Secret-scanning rule for fixtures and the bundle-exclusion check enforced in CI.
- [ ] Gate policy documented; zero outstanding High findings on the E15 packages.

**Do NOT**
- Do not weaken a control to make a scan pass; triage or escalate instead of suppressing a finding.
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**

- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

title: Security review and sign-off for E15 layouts, workspaces and sharing
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic labelled `security`, that the STRIDE model be finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off) and a sign-off comment recorded by the Security engineer before the epic is Done. E15 earns that label on one fact: it is the first epic that lets a document authored by one user be executed as configuration by another.

This ticket closes the loop — a white-box review of the implemented code against the model, verification that every finding is genuinely resolved rather than merely closed, and a written sign-off that the `E15-Q08` QA gate and the R1 exit review can cite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box code review** of the layout/dock package, the workspace API handlers and the export/import path, against the `SR-E15-nn` requirements:
  - Input validation: strict schema, `additionalProperties: false`, depth/size/count bounds, numeric ranges, and validation performed server-side as well as in the import worker.
  - Id regeneration on import; no client-asserted `id`, `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `chart_template_id` or account binding is ever honoured.
  - Authorization: every `/workspaces*` handler enforces `workspaces:read`/`workspaces:write` with `scope: self` at the query level; nested `layoutId` is verified to belong to the caller's workspace; non-existent and not-owned both return 404.
  - Output encoding at every sink that renders user-authored names: tabs, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-216 PanelMenu, CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, live regions, Electron window titles, export filenames, logs.
  - Export allow-list implemented as an allow-list (not a deny-list), with a test asserting a newly added field is excluded by default.
  - Rate limiting and caps on workspace/layout/pane creation and on the debounced `PUT`.
  - Audit vs analytics split: `workspace.deleted` / `workspace.exported` reach the audit log; layout arrangement events stay analytics-only by design.
- **Verification pass**: independently re-test each Critical/High finding from `E15-X02` on the release candidate rather than trusting the closed state.
- **Findings disposition table**: every threat from `E15-X01` → mitigation → evidence (code ref, test id, scan result) → status (fixed / accepted / not-applicable with reason).
- **Sign-off note** `docs/security/signoff/e15.md` bound to a commit sha, with the Security engineer's name and date, plus Owner sign-off on any accepted risk.
- **Handover to E43**: a short list of E15 surfaces the pen-test should probe before Live enablement (import path, cross-user access, export contents).

## Out of scope
- New feature work or refactoring (findings are filed as fixes to owning stories).
- The pen-test itself (E43).
- Signing off other epics' sharing surfaces (rules `SCR-089`, chart templates) beyond noting shared risk.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled threat has a disposition
  Given the E15-X01 threat list
  Then the disposition table accounts for 100% of entries with evidence, and no entry is left blank or "TBD"

Scenario: Fixes are verified, not assumed
  Given a Critical finding marked fixed in E15-X02
  When the reviewer independently re-tests it on the release candidate
  Then the exploit fails, and the verification is recorded with the commit sha

Scenario: Failure case - an unresolved High blocks sign-off
  Given a High-severity finding with no fix and no Owner-accepted risk
  Then sign-off is withheld and the E15 epic cannot reach Done

Scenario: Edge case - a control exists only client-side
  Given import validation implemented solely in the browser worker
  When the reviewer replays the import payload directly against the API
  Then the gap is raised as a finding and must be closed server-side before sign-off

Scenario: Sign-off is citable
  When the sign-off note is published
  Then it names the commit sha, the reviewer, the date, the accepted risks with review dates, and is linked from E15-Q08 and the R1 exit checklist
```

## Technical notes / design
- Review by requirement, not by file: walk each `SR-E15-nn` and demand the code and the test that satisfy it, which makes "we probably handle that" impossible to pass off.
- The single most important structural check is that validation and authorization live on the server: the browser worker is a UX nicety, and the reviewer must replay payloads directly at the API to prove it.
- Prefer allow-lists in two places — exported fields and accepted pane kinds — and assert the default-deny property with a test that adds a synthetic field/kind and expects exclusion.
- Record inherited assumptions from E09 and E17 explicitly, so a future change to session or transport triggers a re-review of this sign-off rather than silently invalidating it.

## Test plan
- Re-run the `E15-X02` abuse suite and the `E15-X03` scans on the release candidate; attach results.
- Perform a manual replay of the three highest-value attacks (malicious import at the API, cross-user layout access, export leakage diff) independently of the automated suite.
- Confirm each regression test added for a finding actually fails when the fix is reverted locally.

## Security notes
- This is the epic's security gate; no exceptions are granted verbally — accepted risks require the Owner's written acceptance and a dated review, per `04-security-program.md`.
- The sign-off must state the data classification conclusion: workspace exports are user-confidential and must not be treated as shareable-by-default in any future collaboration feature (a direct input to R5 collaboration work).
- Any finding with cross-epic reach (rules import, chart templates, future sharing) is escalated with a ticket in the owning epic before sign-off, not after.

## Accessibility notes
- The reviewer verifies that every security-relevant message (rejection, dropped-elements report, version mismatch, permission refusal) is perceivable: text, keyboard-reachable, announced, and adequately contrasted — a security control that only a sighted mouse user can perceive is an incomplete control.
- The DEMO/LIVE indicator's integrity in floating windows is re-checked as an anti-spoofing control.

## Performance notes
- Confirms that the added validation and rate limiting do not breach the `E15-Q04` budgets: import validation within the ≤500 ms worker budget, and the debounced save path unaffected at the legitimate 2-second cadence.
- Confirms that rejection paths fail fast and bounded, so a hostile document cannot consume the frame budget of a live trading workspace.

## Observability
- Verifies that audit entries for `workspace.deleted` and `workspace.exported` are written append-only and are queryable, and that `layout.import_rejected{reason}` uses a bounded enum.
- Verifies the probing alert (repeated cross-user 404s / repeated import rejections) exists in the ops dashboard with a documented threshold and owner.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed against every `SR-E15-nn` requirement with evidence recorded.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings verified fixed on the RC; Medium fixed or Owner-accepted with a date.
- [ ] Disposition table complete with no blank entries.
- [ ] `docs/security/signoff/e15.md` published, bound to a commit sha, signed by the Security engineer, with Owner signatures on accepted risks.
- [ ] Pen-test handover list delivered to E43; sign-off linked from `E15-Q08` and the R1 exit checklist.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (model), `E15-X02` (abuse findings), `E15-X03` (scan gates); a release-candidate build of the E15 stories.

## Branch
`chore/e15-security-review`

## References

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-007
